sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Regardless of legal fault in a car-motorcycle collision, who usually suffers worst and how can motorists help?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Whoever is legally at fault, the motorcyclist is usually the one who loses in a car-motorcycle crash, and alert drivers who watch for riders can reduce those crashes, injuries and deaths.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: What does the term No-Zones mean around large trucks and buses?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: No-Zones are the areas around trucks and buses where crashes are most likely, and some of them are blind spots in which a car vanishes from the large-vehicle driver's view.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What visual check tells you immediately whether a truck or bus driver can spot your car beside them?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Trucks and buses have big blind spots on both sides, so if you cannot see the driver's face in the side mirror, that driver cannot see you either.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Which side should you use to pass a truck or bus, and how should you pace the pass?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Pass a truck or bus on the left and as quickly as you can, moving fully ahead of it so the driver can see you, and never cruise alongside it.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: How far back can a truck or bus rear No-Zone stretch, and why is tailgating there a triple trap?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: The rear No-Zone directly behind a truck or bus can stretch as far as two hundred feet, so a tailgating car is hidden from the driver, cannot see ahead, and has no escape if the big vehicle brakes hard.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Why must you switch to low beams whenever you trail a large truck or bus after dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Dim your headlights whenever you follow a large vehicle at night, because bright beams bounce off its side mirrors and blind its driver.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How does your strategy for clearing side No-Zones differ from avoiding the two-hundred-foot rear No-Zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Side No-Zones are passed quickly on the left, while the rear No-Zone of up to two hundred feet is avoided by not tailgating at all.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: After overtaking a large vehicle, what must appear in your rearview mirror before you merge back over?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: After passing a large vehicle, do not cut back in too soon: wait until its entire front shows in your rear-view mirror, and keep your speed up once you are in front of it.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Roughly how much stopping distance do trucks and buses require compared with passenger cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Truck and bus drivers need close to twice as much room to stop as car drivers do.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, how many feet did the cited safety study find a loaded truck needs versus a car?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: A National Safety Council study cited in the manual found that a loaded truck traveling fifty-five miles per hour needs four hundred thirty feet to stop safely, compared with one hundred ninety-three feet for a passenger car.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How do the fifty-five-mile-per-hour stopping numbers connect to the general rule on truck braking space?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: In the study the manual cites, the loaded truck needs four hundred thirty feet at fifty-five miles per hour against one hundred ninety-three feet for a car, which is the nearly double stopping room drivers must leave.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Why should you never slip behind a truck or bus while it is backing up?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Never cross behind a truck or bus that is backing up, because drivers of large vehicles cannot see directly behind them and may not see you at all.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: Why do large trucks and buses often swing left before making a right-hand corner?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: To make a right turn safely, a truck or bus driver has to swing wide to the left first, which opens a gap on the right that can become a squeeze play.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: What must you avoid doing whenever a large vehicle ahead has its right turn signal flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: While a large vehicle's right turn signal is blinking, do not try to pass it on the right; the driver cannot see you and you could be trapped, so wait until the turn is finished.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: What separates the front No-Zone mistake from the turning No-Zone mistake around large trucks?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: The front No-Zone is about cutting in too soon after passing, while the turning No-Zone is about never passing on the right of a truck signaling a right turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What must you do with any vehicle left standing beside a rural highway, or if it cannot move?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Any vehicle you leave standing beside a rural highway, whatever the reason, has to be moved off the paved or main traveled part of the road, and if it cannot be moved you must use lights and markings to warn other traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Which brake and gear steps apply every single time you park on a slope?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: When you park on a hill, always set the hand brake and shift into park, or into reverse or low gear if the car has no park position, so it cannot roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Facing downhill next to a curb, which way do your front wheels point and what gear holds the car?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Parked facing downhill beside a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb and shift into reverse or park.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Facing uphill next to a curb, how should you angle your front tires and set the transmission?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Parked facing uphill beside a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and shift into low gear or park.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: When parking uphill or downhill where there is no curb at all, which direction do your wheels turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road, whether the car faces uphill or downhill.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: At a curb, how do wheel angle and manual gear choice flip between downhill and uphill parking?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Downhill at a curb the wheels turn toward the curb with reverse or park, but uphill at a curb they turn away from it with low gear or park.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Which three pedestrian and traffic surfaces are off-limits for parking at all times?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: You may not park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk, or on a sidewalk.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Within how many feet of a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection is parking prohibited?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Parking is banned within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: How many feet of clear space must you leave before a roadside stop sign, flashing beacon, or traffic signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Parking is banned within thirty feet of a stop sign, a flashing beacon or a traffic control signal placed at the roadside.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: Within what distance of the nearest railroad track rail is parking outlawed?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Parking is banned within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park in Alabama?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Parking is banned within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Besides corners and crossings, which three access points or roadway structures forbid parking?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: You may not park in front of a driveway, on any bridge, or inside a tunnel.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: What counts as double parking, and does Alabama law allow it even briefly?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Double parking is not allowed: you may not park on the roadway side of a vehicle already parked at the curb or the edge of the highway.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: What do a yellow-painted curb and official no-parking signs tell a driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: You may not park beside a curb painted yellow or anywhere official signs forbid parking.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: In ascending order, which four footage buffers govern parking near hydrants, crosswalks, roadside signals, and rails?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: The no-parking distances differ by hazard: fifteen feet from a hydrant, twenty feet from a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection, thirty feet from a roadside stop sign or signal, and fifty feet from the nearest rail.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: In order, how do you line up, reverse, and finish steering into a parallel parking space?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: To parallel park, pull up even with the parked car ahead of the space, ease back gently toward the space, turn the wheels sharply, begin straightening them, and finish with the wheels parallel to the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Who inside a vehicle must wear a restraint under Alabama's safety belt law?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Alabama's safety belt law requires every occupant of the vehicle to be restrained, no matter how old they are.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: Where on your body should the lap portion of a seat belt sit for peak crash protection?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: A seat belt works best when it is pulled snug across the hip bones.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Through what age must young riders be properly restrained under Alabama's child restraint statute?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Under Alabama's child restraint law, children through age fifteen must be restrained whenever they ride in a motor vehicle in the state.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Which seating rows and vehicle types fall under Alabama's child restraint requirements?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: The child restraint law covers riders in both front and back seats of passenger cars, pickup trucks, vans seating ten or fewer, minivans and sport utility vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: What two consequences hit a driver who violates Alabama's child restraint law?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: A driver who breaks the child restraint law pays a fine and also has points put on their driver record.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: Until what age or weight threshold must an infant ride in a rear-facing car seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: An infant rides rear-facing, in an infant-only seat or a convertible seat, until reaching at least one year of age or twenty pounds.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: After outgrowing rear-facing, until what age or weight does a child ride in a forward-facing seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Next comes a forward-facing seat, or a convertible seat turned forward, until the child is at least five years of age or forty pounds.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Until a child reaches what birthday is a booster seat mandatory in Alabama?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: A booster seat is required until the child is six years of age.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: Once a child graduates from a booster at six, what size-appropriate restraint applies and until what age?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: After the booster stage, the law's size-appropriate system is a seat belt, which it lists until a child is fifteen years of age.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: What single habit does the manual identify as the most effective defense against serious crash injuries?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: The manual calls wearing seat belts the most effective way to reduce serious injuries in traffic crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How does Alabama's general safety belt law pair with its specific child restraint law?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: The safety belt law covers every occupant of any age, while the child restraint law adds size-appropriate seats for children through age fifteen.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How do the age and weight cutoffs line up across rear-facing, forward-facing, and booster stages?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Rear-facing lasts until at least one year or twenty pounds, forward-facing until at least five years or forty pounds, and the booster seat until six years of age.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: How quickly must a driver recognize traffic signs, lights, and markings—and how must regulatory boards be treated?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Every driver must know signs, signals and road markings well enough to recognize them instantly and to obey regulatory signs without hesitating.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: For what two visibility reasons do modern highway boards favor bold graphics over wordy text?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Signs now use more symbols and pictures because they can be recognized faster at higher speeds and from farther away.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Which two visual features of a road board are coded to its message category even before you read it?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: A sign's shape and its color are both coded to the kind of message it carries, so learn shapes and colors as well as individual signs.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Into which three functional groups does Alabama divide all traffic boards?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Traffic signs fall into three types by function: regulatory, warning, and information or guide signs.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What do regulatory boards govern, what standard colors do they use, and are they optional?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves, are black and white unless shown in their actual color, and must be obeyed.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: When vehicles reach a four-way stop one after another, which driver earns the right to proceed first?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: At a four-way stop, vehicles leave in the order they arrived, so the first one to come to a complete stop is the first one allowed to go.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: When two or more drivers halt at a four-way stop at the exact same instant, who goes first?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: When two or more vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same moment, the one farthest to the right goes first.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Even when right-of-way is clearly yours at a four-way stop, why should you wait a few seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Even when it is your turn at a four-way stop, wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts into the intersection, because many drivers ignore the rule.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: What speed adjustment and two right-of-way priorities does a yield board require?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: A YIELD sign tells you to slow down so you can give the right of way to pedestrians crossing and to vehicles on the intersecting road.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What critical mistake does a white-on-red wrong-way regulatory board alert you to?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: A white-on-red regulatory sign warns that you are heading onto a one-way highway or ramp from the wrong direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What does the regulatory board placed at the mouth of an oncoming one-way roadway forbid?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Another regulatory sign marks a one-way roadway whose traffic is coming toward you, and you may not enter it at that point.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: What approach mindset and track check does the white railroad regulatory crossbuck require?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: The railroad regulatory sign means approach with caution and make sure every track is clear before you cross.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What movement is prohibited at an intersection displaying a crossed-out left-turn arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: A no-left-turn sign means you may not turn left at that intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Under a posted no-parking board, does staying behind the wheel make sitting there legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Under a no-parking sign you may not park in the area even if you remain inside the car.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What two conditions—person and decal—must both be met to park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: You may not park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped, on public or private property, unless a handicapped person drives or directs the vehicle and it visibly shows the handicapped sticker.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: For what sole reason may you pull over beside an emergency-stopping-only board?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: An EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign allows stopping only for real emergencies.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: Under what weather and road conditions does a posted speed-limit number—such as thirty—apply as the top speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A posted speed limit is the speed allowed under normal conditions, and a sign reading SPEED LIMIT thirty means thirty miles an hour is the top speed in that area.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: On which types of highways do dual maximum-and-minimum speed boards usually stand?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Some signs post both a maximum and a minimum speed for a stretch of highway, and minimum limits usually appear on freeways and other controlled-access highways.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: What two ways tell you a reduced school-zone speed limit is currently in effect?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: A school-zone speed limit applies during the hours the sign shows, and it may also be displayed on a lighted sign with flashing amber lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What must every vehicle occupying a lane marked left-lane-must-turn-left do at the upcoming corner?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: A LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT sign means traffic in the left lane has to turn left at the intersection ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which turning directions are off-limits when an intersection posts a no-turns board?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: A NO TURNS sign means you may turn neither right nor left at that intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: What exact boundary along a highway does a regulatory do-not-pass board mark?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: One regulatory sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Which red-light turns are forbidden when a no-turn-on-red board hangs at a traffic light?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.memory_hook: Neither right nor left on red
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted at a signal-controlled intersection, you may not turn right or left on a red light.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: On which side must you pass a regulatory keep-right divider board?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: One regulatory sign tells you not to drive to the left of it.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: How can a multi-lane regulatory panel split duties between the curb lane and the adjacent lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: A lane-use sign can require the right lane to turn right while the lane beside it may either turn right or go straight.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: Where are side-by-side double right turns legal in Alabama, and what applies everywhere else?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them; at unsigned intersections the normal right-turn rules apply.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: What travel rule does a horizontal black-and-white one-way arrow enforce?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: A one-way arrow sign means you may travel only in the direction the arrow points.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: How do standard hazard warnings and road-construction warnings split background colors?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Warning signs are black on yellow, except construction-area warning signs, which are black on orange, and they warn of hazards that call for extra caution.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Which two high-alert foot-traffic zones use bright fluorescent yellow warning panels?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow on a sign marks pedestrian crossings and school zones.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What geometric outline identifies the vast majority of roadway warning boards?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Most warning signs are diamond shaped, though there are some exceptions.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How do yellow, orange, and fluorescent yellow divide warning duties across Alabama roads?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.memory_hook: Yellow general, orange work, fluorescent walkers
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Ordinary warning signs are black on yellow, construction warning signs are black on orange, and fluorescent yellow is kept for pedestrian crossings and school zones.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: Which four bend or alignment changes do curved-arrow warning diamonds preview?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Curve warning signs tell you of a sharp left turn, a curve to the right, a gradual curve right then left, or a winding road ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: What junction geometry do perpendicular and angled stem warning diamonds show?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Side-road warning signs show that a side road joins the highway ahead, either from the right or at an angle.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What surface hazard and driver response go with a bump warning diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: A BUMP sign warns of a bump ahead and tells you to slow down.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: What must you prepare to do when a T-intersection warning shows your road ending straight ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: One warning sign means the road does not continue straight, so you must turn right or left.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Why must you keep all four tires on paved asphalt beside a soft-shoulder warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: A SOFT SHOULDER sign warns that the roadside is soft, so stay on the pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.front: What two tight alignment layouts do sharp-zag and double-arrow T-end diamonds warn about?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.expected_back: Other warning signs show a sharp left turn followed by a sharp right, or a road that ends ahead and turns both right and left.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.front: How are directional curve-arrow boards arranged along the outside of a sharp bend?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.expected_back: Arrow signs warn of a sharp turn or curve in the direction of the arrow and are normally set up in a series.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: How does a road-narrows warning differ slightly in meaning from a pavement-narrows warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: A ROAD NARROWS sign means the road ahead is narrower than the one you are on, and a PAVEMENT NARROWS sign means the paved surface ahead is narrower.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: Which sides of an upcoming traffic island may you use after passing an island-ahead split-arrow diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: An island-ahead warning sign means you may pass the island on either side.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: What roadway feature and speed action does a dip warning diamond call for?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: A DIP sign warns of a dip in the road and tells you to slow down.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: How wide is the span ahead when you pass a one-lane-bridge warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: A ONE LANE BRIDGE sign means the bridge ahead has no room for you to meet or pass another car or truck.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How do road-narrows, pavement-narrows, and one-lane-bridge escalate from tighter room to single-file?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: ROAD NARROWS refers to the whole road getting narrower, PAVEMENT NARROWS to the paved surface, and ONE LANE BRIDGE to a bridge too narrow to meet or pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.front: What upcoming intersection rules do stop-ahead and yield-ahead diamonds prepare you for?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.expected_back: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs warn that a STOP sign or a YIELD sign is coming up.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Do you halt right beside a stop-ahead warning diamond or farther down the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs only warn that a control is coming; the stop or yield itself happens at the STOP or YIELD sign further on.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.front: What does a small square yellow advisory-speed plaque mounted beneath a curve diamond tell you?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.expected_back: An advisory speed sign gives the top safe speed for taking the turn ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.front: What three actions belong at a railroad-crossing-ahead warning—and why does physics demand them?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.expected_back: A railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign means slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, since a train cannot stop quickly.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.front: What roadside elevation hazard does a low-shoulder warning diamond highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.expected_back: A low-shoulder sign warns that the shoulder sits much lower than the road surface.

sec08-card-sec08-F46.front: What entering traffic must you scan for near truck-crossing and fire-station warning diamonds?
sec08-card-sec08-F46.expected_back: Truck-crossing and fire-station signs tell you to watch for trucks or fire trucks pulling onto the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F47.front: How do pavement-ends and dead-end warnings differ in what lies down the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F47.expected_back: A PAVEMENT ENDS sign warns that the surface ahead turns to gravel or dirt, and a DEAD END sign means the street has no outlet.

sec08-card-sec08-F48.front: Why does Alabama place lane-ends warnings in a three-board sequence ahead of a dropped lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F48.expected_back: Lane-ends signs warn that the number of lanes changes ahead, and the three signs come in a series as a repeated reminder to merge into the next lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F49.front: On which side of a two-lane highway—and at what zone boundary—does the no-passing warning stand?
sec08-card-sec08-F49.expected_back: The NO PASSING ZONE warning sign stands on the left side of a two-lane road to warn where a no-passing zone begins.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Why should your eyes sweep the left roadside—not just the right—before starting a two-lane pass?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: The no-passing warning sign belongs on the left side of a two-lane road, at the point where the zone begins, so look left for it.

sec08-card-sec08-F50.front: What happens if your vehicle or rooftop cargo exceeds the feet-and-inches number on a low-clearance diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F50.expected_back: A low-clearance sign means vehicles or loads taller than the clearance shown cannot fit under the structure ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F51.front: What transition—and ongoing reminder—does a vertical two-way-traffic warning convey?
sec08-card-sec08-F51.expected_back: A two-way traffic sign means you are leaving a separated one-way roadway for a two-way road, and it also reminds drivers they are on a two-way road.

sec08-card-sec08-F52.front: At a merge warning diamond, who yields right-of-way and how should the ramp driver blend in?
sec08-card-sec08-F52.expected_back: At a merge sign, a driver joining from the right gives way to main-route traffic and uses the speed-change lane to blend in smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F53.front: Which four signal, junction, median, or slope changes have dedicated advance warning diamonds?
sec08-card-sec08-F53.expected_back: Other warning signs announce a traffic signal ahead, a crossroad, a divided highway starting or ending, and a downhill grade.

sec08-card-sec08-F54.front: Which four traction, bridge, livestock, or wildlife hazards do specialized warning diamonds announce?
sec08-card-sec08-F54.expected_back: Warning signs also flag slippery-when-wet pavement, a narrow bridge, cattle crossings and deer crossings.

sec08-card-sec08-F55.front: Do pedestrian-crossing boards appear strictly at corners, and what duty applies when walkers step in?
sec08-card-sec08-F55.expected_back: A pedestrian-crossing sign marks a spot where people on foot often cross, not always at an intersection, and you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk while watching both sides.

sec08-card-sec08-F56.front: What two student-safety alerts come from school-crossing boards and school-bus-stop-ahead boards?
sec08-card-sec08-F56.expected_back: A school-crossing sign means slow down and watch for children crossing, and a separate sign warns of a school bus stop ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F57.front: Why might you encounter bicycle, pedestrian, or school boards in two different yellow shades across Alabama?
sec08-card-sec08-F57.expected_back: Bicycle, pedestrian and school crossing signs may appear in either their older or their current colors.

sec08-card-sec08-F58.front: At least how many feet of side clearance does Alabama's bicycle-passing regulatory board require?
sec08-card-sec08-F58.expected_back: One bicycle sign states that a three foot minimum clearance is required when passing a cyclist.

sec08-card-sec08-F59.front: When does Alabama's bikes-may-use-full-lane board remind drivers that cyclists belong right in the travel lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F59.expected_back: Another sign tells drivers that a cyclist may use the full lane when the travel lane is narrow.

sec08-card-sec08-F60.front: What nickname describes shared-lane bicycle pavement markings, and what do they remind drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-F60.expected_back: Shared lane markings, called sharrows, tell road users that people on bicycles may be riding in the travel lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F61.front: What four potential changes—and driver response—come with a road-construction warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F61.expected_back: A ROAD CONSTRUCTION sign means you are entering a work area, so watch for a flagman, one-way traffic, other signs or obstructions, go carefully and follow instructions.

sec08-card-sec08-F62.front: Which three human or equipment hazards get dedicated orange work-zone warnings along Alabama highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F62.expected_back: Work-zone signs also warn of a flagman ahead, workers in or near the road, and mowing equipment ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F63.front: During which hours do large sequencing work-zone arrow panels run, and what two messages do they send?
sec08-card-sec08-F63.expected_back: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones by day and night to steer drivers into certain lanes and show that part of the road ahead is closed.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: What is the purpose of guide boards, and which color pair gives route directions and distances?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Guide or informational signs inform and direct drivers, and those giving motorist directions are green and white.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What roadside needs are advertised on blue-and-white highway guide boards?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Blue and white guide signs are the ones used for motorist services.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Which destinations are marked by brown-and-white roadside guide boards?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Brown and white guide signs mark points of public recreational or cultural interest.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What three practical purposes do green roadside mileposts serve along Alabama's main highways?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Mileposts stand along most sections of Alabama's main highways to help drivers pinpoint where they are, to locate emergency incidents, and to aid highway maintenance.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: At which two compass state borders—or route start—does Alabama highway milepost numbering begin at zero?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Milepost numbering is meant to start at zero at the south and west state lines, or at the junction where a route begins.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Into what four broad categories does Alabama group roadway pavement markings?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Pavement markings generally come in four types: centerline striping, edge striping, crosswalks and pavement messages.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What traffic does a centerline divide, and how does Alabama's manual state its color on two-lane versus multi-lane or one-way roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: The centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions, and the manual says it is painted yellow on two-lane highways and white on multi-lane highways and one-way streets.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What passing rule applies along a broken, dashed centerline?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: A broken centerline marks areas with no passing restriction, where you may pass when it is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: When a solid yellow stripe runs alongside a broken stripe, how do you tell whether passing is banned for you?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Where passing is restricted, a solid yellow line runs beside the broken line, and if the solid line is on your side you may not pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What passing rule applies when two solid yellow stripes replace the broken centerline?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: When passing is banned for traffic in both directions, the broken line is replaced by two solid yellow lines.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How do broken alone, solid-on-your-side, and double-solid yellow stripes step up passing restrictions?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.memory_hook: Broken allows, single yours, double everyone
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: A solid yellow line on your side bans your passing, two solid yellow lines ban passing both ways, and a broken line alone allows passing when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: On a two-lane road marked no-passing both ways, for what sole maneuver may you cross the centerline?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: On a two-lane, two-way road where passing is banned both ways, you may cross the centerline only as part of a left turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: On an undivided multi-lane two-way highway, when is crossing the centerline permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: On a multi-lane, two-way road, the centerline may be crossed only while making a left turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Which drivers—and from which directions—are allowed inside a center two-way left-turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: A two-way left turn lane is reserved only for vehicles turning left from either direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What lane flow do broken white stripes divide, and may you cross them?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Two or more lanes moving the same way are separated by broken white lines, and you may cross them when passing.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What boundary does a solid white right-edge stripe mark, and when may tires cross it?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: A solid white edge line marks the outside of the traffic lane and may be crossed only by traffic moving onto or off the shoulder.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Where do yellow left-edge lines appear on divided roads, and on which side must you pass yellow-painted islands?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Yellow left edge lines sometimes appear on divided roads where traffic cannot pull fully off, and yellow also marks obstructions and islands, which you must pass on the right.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Between lanes moving the same way, does a normal solid white stripe ban lane changes or discourage them?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: A normal solid white line separates lanes going the same direction where crossing is discouraged but not forbidden.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What extra message does an extra-wide solid white lane stripe add beyond a standard stripe?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: A wide solid white line adds emphasis where crossing calls for unusual care.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What is the legal rule when two parallel solid white lines separate same-direction lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: A double solid white line separates lanes going the same direction, and crossing it is prohibited.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Where can solid white crosswalk stripes appear, and what must you do when pedestrians occupy an unsignalized one?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Solid white lines mark crosswalks at intersections and sometimes between them, and with no controlling signal a driver must stop at any crosswalk occupied by pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: In what color are pavement words like school zone or railroad crossing painted, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Pavement messages such as SCHOOL ZONE or RR CROSSING are painted in white letters on the road to warn of conditions ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: What is your baseline duty at a steady circular red light—and what post-stop turns can apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: At a steady circular red light, stop and stay stopped until it turns green, although a right turn, and in certain cases a left turn, is allowed after stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Which lamp precedes steady yellow, what does yellow mean, and what entry rule hits on red?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: A steady circular yellow follows the green and means clear the intersection; you must not enter once the red comes on.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: Which movements does a steady circular green allow—and whom must you still yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: On a steady circular green you may go straight or turn either way, yielding to vehicles and pedestrians lawfully in the intersection, unless a sign forbids the turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What do alternating red flashers paired with a railroad crossbuck mean, and what multi-track check follows?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Red flashing lights work with crossbuck signs at many railroad crossings, and you must always stop when they begin flashing because a train is near, checking every track before you cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: At a gated railroad crossing, do you wait for the gate arm to drop before stopping or stop as soon as lights blink?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Where gates are used with flashing lights, stop as soon as the lights start, before the gates come down, and stay stopped until the gates rise and the lights stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: How do green and yellow turn arrows govern turning lanes compared with circular traffic lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Arrows control specific turning movements, and yellow and green arrows give left turns the same control that the standard light gives through traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Why is turning on a green arrow called a protected movement?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: A green arrow lets you go in the arrow's direction while opposing traffic has to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: When a steady green arrow glows alongside another lens, what moves may you make and whom do you yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: A steady green arrow, alone or with other lights, lets you enter for the arrow's movement or any other movement the other lights allow, still yielding to pedestrians and vehicles lawfully in the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: What is ending whenever a steady yellow arrow replaces a green arrow—including alongside a circular green?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: Yellow arrows follow green arrows to show the protected movement is ending, and a steady yellow arrow shown with a circular green means that protected turn is ending.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: When a steady yellow arrow glows alone or beside circular red, what happens once that yellow arrow goes dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow shown alone or with a steady circular red clears the protected turn, and you may not enter the intersection after it goes out.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How does a green turn arrow contrast directly with the yellow arrow that follows it?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A green arrow is a protected turn with opposing traffic stopped, and a yellow arrow means that protection is ending.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: Where are lane-use control lights mounted, and what do they regulate?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Lane use control signals hang over individual lanes of a street, highway or freeway to show which lanes you may or may not use.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: What does a steady red X hanging directly above a lane forbid—and how strong is its authority?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: A steady red X over a lane means you may not drive in that lane, and it overrides the other traffic controls there accordingly.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: What does a steady downward green arrow over a lane allow—and do normal road rules still apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: A steady green arrow over a lane means you may drive in that lane while obeying all other controls and normal safe practice.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: In Alabama's manual, what unique rule applies under a steady yellow X hanging over a lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: The manual says a steady yellow X lets you drive in that lane only with caution, because it signals potentially hazardous conditions.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How do Alabama's red X, downward green arrow, and steady yellow X divide overhead lane control?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.memory_hook: Red closed, green open, yellow caution
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Over a lane, a red X closes it, a green arrow opens it, and a yellow X allows it only with caution.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How is a roundabout controlled, and in which clock direction does traffic circle the center island?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: A roundabout is a circular intersection, usually without a traffic signal, where traffic travels counter-clockwise around a central island.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Which way do you steer to enter a roundabout, whom do you yield to, and how do you reach your street?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: You enter a roundabout from the right, yielding to vehicles already circulating, and follow the circle to the right until you reach your road.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: Why are roundabouts replacing traditional intersections across the United States?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: Roundabouts are spreading in the U.S. because one-way counterclockwise flow creates fewer conflict points and moves traffic more safely and efficiently than standard intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: By roughly what three percentages do roundabouts cut fatal crashes, injury crashes, and total crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.memory_hook: Ninety fatal, seventy-five injury, thirty-five all
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: Compared with other intersection controls, roundabouts cut fatal crashes about ninety percent, injury crashes about seventy-five percent and all crashes about thirty-five percent, according to the crash statistics the manual cites.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: Before reaching the yield line of a roundabout, what speed, sign, and crosswalk duties come first?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: To drive a roundabout, slow down, obey the signs, and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists before you enter.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: From which side does circulating roundabout traffic approach your bumper—and when do you pull in?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: Yield to traffic coming from your left that is already in the roundabout, and enter only when there is a safe gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: How fast should you drive once inside a roundabout, and how do you depart onto your target road?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: Keep your speed low inside the roundabout and turn off onto your road as you reach its exit.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.front: Walking across a roundabout leg, which way does a pedestrian look at the curb versus on the center splitter island?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.expected_back: At a roundabout, pedestrians at the curb look left for oncoming traffic, while those on the crosswalk island look right.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.front: What two legal ways can a bicyclist navigate through a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.expected_back: Bicyclists may ride through the roundabout or use the crosswalk instead.

sec09-card-sec09-F49.front: Between entering drivers on the approach and drivers already inside the roundabout, who holds right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F49.expected_back: Vehicles already in a roundabout have the right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F50.front: Even when your destination road lies to your left, why must you never turn left at a roundabout entry?
sec09-card-sec09-F50.expected_back: Never turn left to enter a roundabout; wait for a safe gap and turn right into it.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.front: Whom must you watch for and yield to again as you peel out of a roundabout exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians and bicycles as you leave the roundabout.

sec09-card-sec09-F46.front: What is the effortless fix—and strict ban—if you accidentally pass your intended roundabout exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F46.expected_back: If you miss your exit, go around the roundabout again, and never back up inside it.

sec09-card-sec09-F47.front: How do you clear the way for an ambulance depending on whether you are approaching or already inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F47.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle, pull over before entering if you are not yet in the roundabout; if you are already in, continue to your exit and then pull over, avoiding any stop inside.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Why does emergency-vehicle response flip once your front bumper crosses into the roundabout circle?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: An emergency vehicle means pull over if you have not entered the roundabout, but keep going to your exit first if you are already inside.

sec09-card-sec09-F48.front: What is the raised paved collar around a roundabout's center island for, and who should stay off it?
sec09-card-sec09-F48.expected_back: A truck apron is a paved area on the inside of a roundabout for the rear wheels of large trucks, and cars, pickups and SUVs are not meant to use it.

sec09-card-sec09-F51.front: Under what sole circumstance should you ever stop your vehicle inside a roundabout circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F51.expected_back: Once inside a roundabout, do not stop unless stopping is the only way to avoid a crash or other danger.

sec09-card-sec09-F52.front: What two steps are critical before pulling into a two-lane roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F52.expected_back: In a two-lane roundabout, pick your lane and yield to traffic in both lanes before you enter.

sec09-card-sec09-F53.front: In a two-lane roundabout, which lanes handle right turns, left or U-turns, and straight-through travel?
sec09-card-sec09-F53.expected_back: In a two-lane roundabout, use the right lane for right turns and the left lane for left turns and U-turns, and to go straight follow the pavement markings, arrows or signs.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Why must drivers actively study bad weather, low light, and emergency situations?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Most drivers learn under normal conditions, so safe driving in changing weather, light or emergencies must be learned through study and experience.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Roughly what fraction of Alabama's fatal traffic crashes happen after dark despite lighter traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: About half of Alabama's fatal crashes happen during darkness, even though traffic is light then.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What does never overdriving your headlights require of your nighttime speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Never overdrive your headlights: keep a speed at which you can stop within the distance your lights show ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Under normal clear conditions, roughly how many feet ahead do high-beam headlights illuminate?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Under normal conditions, high beams usually light the road about three hundred fifty feet ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Within how many feet must Alabama drivers dim high beams for oncoming cars versus cars ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.memory_hook: Five hundred meeting, two hundred following
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: The law requires dimming your headlights within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle and within two hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: What should you do if an oncoming driver refuses to dim high beams after you switch to low?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: If an oncoming driver keeps high beams on after you dim, keep yours dimmed anyway, since blinding that driver only endangers you.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: How should you maintain vehicle lights and glass to protect visibility at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Keep lights working and lenses clean, and keep all vehicle glass clean, free of defects and clear of frost and steam.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: When does state law require full headlights rather than parking lights by clock window and visibility?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: State law requires headlights, not just parking lights, starting a half-hour after sunset and lasting until a half-hour before sunrise, and also whenever you cannot see clearly for at least five hundred feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: If twilight or gray weather leaves you unsure whether headlights are needed, what should you switch on?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: When unsure whether lights are needed, turn them on low beam, which helps you see and helps others see you.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Which five unlit or slow road hazards demand close night scanning, and what trip prep helps?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: At night watch closely for signs, pedestrians, bicycles, slow vehicles and animals, and study maps ahead of time.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: How can a passenger and deliberate eye movement keep your vision sharp on night drives?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: A companion can act as a second pair of eyes for signs and hazards, and moving your eyes from near to far and side to side eases night eye fatigue.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How do the two high-beam dimming distances line up against the visibility threshold requiring headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Dim within five hundred feet of oncoming traffic and within two hundred feet behind a car, while headlights are required whenever you cannot see five hundred feet ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Where should you guide your eyes when bright oncoming headlights threaten to dazzle you?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: To cut glare from oncoming lights, look away toward the right edge of the pavement and its white line.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: How do you cut blinding headlight glare shining into your cabin from traffic behind you?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: For glare from behind, use a day-night mirror or adjust the mirror to block most of the light.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What four actions protect you first if your vehicle breaks down at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: In a night breakdown, pull well off the road, turn on four-way flashers, raise the hood, and stay with the car if you can.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: If forced to walk after a night breakdown, how do you walk and where do flares or reflectors belong?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: If you must walk, carry a light and walk on the left edge facing traffic, and place flares or reflectors one hundred to five hundred feet behind the car on the right edge.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Why is speeding extra dangerous after dark, even along routes you drive every day?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Speed is more dangerous at night because at high speed your headlight range does not give enough stopping distance, so obey limits even on roads you know.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Which six winter hazards challenge drivers, and does bad weather alone excuse most winter crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Winter adds darkness, fog, rain, snow, sleet and ice, and in most cases bad weather alone cannot be blamed for crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What three steps ready your engine, windows, and washer tank before pulling out in winter?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Warm the engine while clearing snow and ice from the car and windows, and keep washer fluid mixed with anti-freeze.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Why should you skip spraying windshield washers at highway speed during extreme cold?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: In extreme cold, avoid using washers at high speed, since the fluid can freeze on the glass and block your view.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: How can you safely gauge road slipperiness in winter and set your pace?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Test your brakes gently at low speed to learn how slippery the road is, then set your speed to match.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: Where do snow treads go, and what speed and spacing adjustments remain required?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Snow treads on the drive wheels improve traction in snow, but you still drive below normal speed and leave more stopping room.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: Do snow treads grip glare ice, and what equipment works best on severe ice or deep snow?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Snow treads do not grip ice; for severe ice, hard-packed snow or very deep snow, reinforced tire chains are best.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: When do running windshield wipers trigger Alabama's headlight law, and what wiper setting is excluded?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Alabama law requires headlights whenever wipers are running for rain, sleet or snow, but intermittent wiper use does not require them.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: How many times longer is your stopping distance on snow or ice compared with dry asphalt?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: On snow or ice a car needs three to twelve times the stopping distance it needs on dry pavement, so keep well back.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: How should manual-clutch and automatic drivers start moving on slick snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: To start on snow or ice, keep engine speed very low; with a clutch release it slowly or use second or high gear, and with an automatic accelerate gently.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: How should you brake normally or stop suddenly on packed snow or ice, and what stays engaged?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: On packed snow or ice brake gently, and for a sudden stop pump the brakes, easing off whenever the wheels lock or start to slip, without pushing in the clutch.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: What happens to engine, brake, and steering control the moment tires lose traction in a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: A skid happens when the tires lose their grip, and then the engine, brakes and even steering lose effect.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: Why must you stay off the brake pedal during a skid until forward rolling returns?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Do not brake in a skid until you regain your forward direction, since braking speeds the skid and locked front wheels lose steering.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: How do you straighten a skid in a rear-wheel-drive vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: To end a skid, keep the rear from outrunning the front; in a rear-wheel drive car, easing off the gas slows the rear wheels and, with steering, straightens the car.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: How does throttle technique change when straightening a skid in a front-wheel-drive car?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: In a front-wheel drive car, a light touch on the gas speeds the front wheels so the front catches up and the skid straightens.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: When tight space prevents accelerating out of a skid, what fallback does the manual note alongside expert caution?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: Without room to accelerate, the next best step is to disengage the transmission and steer the way the rear is skidding, though many experts warn against shifting to neutral in a panic.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: At what wet-road speeds does a standard car start partial hydroplaning and reach total hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: On wet roads most tires wipe the surface up to thirty-five miles per hour, but in a standard car partial hydroplaning starts near thirty-five miles per hour and can become total near fifty-five miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: Why can a mild crosswind or gentle road crown spin a totally hydroplaning vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: With total hydroplaning there is no friction to brake, speed up or turn, so wind or a slight curve can cause an uncontrollable skid.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: What is your immediate pedal move when hydroplaning, and how do partial and total responses differ?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: If you hydroplane, take your foot off the accelerator; correct a partial-hydroplane skid, but in a total one just release the gas and ride it out.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: Even with deep tire tread, when should you expect complete hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Good tires with deep tread help prevent hydroplaning, but when water is deeper than the tread, expect complete hydroplaning above fifty miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: When should you drive in fog or heavy snow, and what rule governs your pace if you must?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Avoid driving in fog or a snowstorm unless absolutely necessary, and when visibility is limited, slow down enough to stop within the distance you can see.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: Which headlight setting belongs in fog or falling snow, and why?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: Use low beams in fog or heavy snow to cut the glare thrown back at you.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: What should you do if dense fog blinds your view or exhausts your eyes?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: If you cannot see, or tire from straining to see, pull fully off the road, leave the lights on, park and wait for better visibility.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: How should you handle narrow hilly or wooded roads with hidden blind pockets?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: Narrow hilly or wooded roads hide blind pockets where another car may be only feet away before you see it, so use extra caution and tap the horn on dangerous curves.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: What does Alabama law say about shifting into neutral to coast down hills?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: The law forbids coasting downhill with the transmission in neutral.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: Why does deadly carbon monoxide risk spike in winter, and can you smell the gas?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: Carbon monoxide poisoning is likelier in winter, when windows stay shut and engines are warmed up, and the fumes have no odor and can kill.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: Which four physical symptoms warn of carbon monoxide exposure, and what is the sole remedy?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: Sudden weariness, yawning, dizziness and nausea signal carbon monoxide poisoning, and the only cure is plenty of fresh air.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.front: What three habits prevent carbon monoxide buildup in or around your vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.memory_hook: Inspect exhaust, crack glass, open garage
sec11-card-sec11-F43.expected_back: Prevent it by having the exhaust checked for leaks, not idling or driving with windows shut tight, and never warming up in a closed garage.

sec11-card-sec11-F44.front: Why does the manual stress thinking before acting during any sudden driving emergency?
sec11-card-sec11-F44.expected_back: In any emergency, think before you act, since instinct, like slamming the brakes in a skid, can be the wrong move.

sec11-card-sec11-F45.front: What early sound warns of a bad tire, and what four steps handle a sudden blowout?
sec11-card-sec11-F45.expected_back: After a blowout, grip the wheel, steer straight, ease off the gas and do not brake until the car is under control; a thumping bulge can warn of one.

sec11-card-sec11-F46.front: What tire neglect commonly triggers blowouts, and how does rapid air loss steer the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F46.expected_back: Under-inflation is one of the most common causes of blowouts, and a tire losing air fast pulls the car to one side.

sec11-card-sec11-F47.front: How do the warning signs and driver actions for losing a wheel compare with a tire blowout?
sec11-card-sec11-F47.expected_back: Losing a wheel gives the same warnings and needs the same response as a blowout: hold tight, steer straight, ease off the gas, no braking until slowed and in control.

sec11-card-sec11-F48.front: If your steering suddenly stops responding, how should you handle gas, gears, and brakes?
sec11-card-sec11-F48.memory_hook: Lift gas smoothly, brake gently later
sec11-card-sec11-F48.expected_back: If steering fails, ease off the gas without braking or shifting, then brake very gently once the car has slowed.

sec11-card-sec11-F49.front: What early pedal feel warns of brake trouble, and what do you do if the pedal drops to the floor?
sec11-card-sec11-F49.expected_back: If the brake pedal sinks to the floor, pump it; a spongy, slowly sinking pedal is the usual early warning of brake failure.

sec11-card-sec11-F50.front: If pumping a dead brake pedal fails, what three backup methods can slow and stop the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F50.expected_back: If pumping fails, apply the parking brake gently to avoid a skid, shift to a lower gear, or switch off the engine in gear, knowing power steering and brakes then stop assisting.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Which three mechanical failures all share the rule of easing off the gas instead of braking hard?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: A blowout, a lost wheel and a steering failure all call for easing off the gas instead of braking hard.

sec11-card-sec11-F51.front: What three steps bring you safely back after your right wheels drop onto a low shoulder?
sec11-card-sec11-F51.expected_back: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, do not swerve back; stay on it, slow down, then ease gently back onto the pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F52.front: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane head-on, what four actions apply and which lane is off-limits?
sec11-card-sec11-F52.memory_hook: Pull right, slow, warn, never left
sec11-card-sec11-F52.expected_back: If a car comes at you in your lane, pull right, slow down, sound the horn or flash lights at night, and never swerve into the left lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F53.front: How should you adjust speed or lane position if an overtaking car gets trapped beside you?
sec11-card-sec11-F53.expected_back: If a passing car is stuck beside you, slow down when it can still get ahead, speed up when it must drop back, and move onto a good shoulder if a crash is nearly certain.

sec11-card-sec11-F54.front: How does clearing a car stalled on railroad tracks differ between manual and automatic transmissions?
sec11-card-sec11-F54.expected_back: A stalled manual car may be moved off tracks by running the starter in low or second gear, but an automatic has to be pushed.

sec11-card-sec11-F55.front: When a train approaches your stalled car on the tracks, which direction must you evacuate on foot?
sec11-card-sec11-F55.expected_back: If a train is coming and the car will not move, leave it and walk beside the tracks toward the train so debris from the impact will not hit you.

sec11-card-sec11-F56.front: If your vehicle plunges into deep water and briefly floats, how must you exit right away?
sec11-card-sec11-F56.memory_hook: Climb out window, keep doors shut
sec11-card-sec11-F56.expected_back: If your car lands in deep water and stays afloat, escape through a window right away, since opening a door lets water rush in.

sec11-card-sec11-F57.front: Which end of a submerged car usually sinks first, and how do you survive if it goes under?
sec11-card-sec11-F57.expected_back: A sinking car usually goes down front first, leaving an air pocket in back; breathe there and escape through a window once it settles.

sec11-card-sec11-F58.front: How do you respond to smoke rolling from under the hood, and what must never touch an engine fire?
sec11-card-sec11-F58.expected_back: For smoke from under the hood, pull off and turn off the ignition, and smother any fire with an extinguisher, dirt or sand, never water.

sec11-card-sec11-F59.front: How can you cool an engine in stop-and-go traffic, and what rule applies if steam boils out?
sec11-card-sec11-F59.memory_hook: Rev in neutral, leave cap shut
sec11-card-sec11-F59.expected_back: In slow traffic, shifting to neutral and briefly racing the engine during stops helps prevent overheating; if steam appears, pull over, shut off the engine and do not open the radiator cap.

sec11-card-sec11-F60.front: Which backup lights should you try if headlights die, and where do you slow on a dark empty road?
sec11-card-sec11-F60.expected_back: If headlights fail, try the parking lights and turn signals; on a dark empty road, slow down on the pavement before moving onto the shoulder.

sec11-card-sec11-F61.front: What three steps save you if wipers quit in a downpour or the hood flies open at speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F61.expected_back: If wipers fail in heavy rain or snow, or the hood flies up, slow down, look out the open side window, and get off the highway.

sec11-card-sec11-F62.front: What two moves handle an accelerator pedal that sticks down while driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F62.expected_back: A stuck accelerator may come free if you hook your toe under the pedal and lift; otherwise turn off the engine to slow down.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which Alabama residents need a driver license on public roads, and what single farm exception exists?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Every Alabama resident who drives a motor vehicle needs a driver license, except when temporarily moving a farm tractor or implement of husbandry on a road.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Who must pass the Alabama driver exam, and when can an expired out-of-state license skip testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Anyone never licensed in Alabama, or whose Alabama license expired more than three years ago, must pass the driver exam; an out-of-state license expired one year or less needs no exam.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does the expiration cutoff that triggers a driver exam differ between Alabama and out-of-state licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: An expired Alabama license triggers a new exam after more than three years, but an expired out-of-state license triggers one after more than one year.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: When may a federal employee legally drive in Alabama without holding an Alabama driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: A federal employee driving a vehicle owned or leased by the U.S. government needs no Alabama license for that driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which drivers aged 16 or older with a valid license from another state or country need no Alabama license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: A resident aged sixteen or older carrying a valid home-state or home-country license may drive without an Alabama one, including out-of-state military families stationed here on long assignments.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Under what condition and yearly day cap may a visitor aged 16+ from a non-licensing country drive in Alabama?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: A non-resident aged sixteen or older from a country that does not license drivers may drive here up to ninety days per calendar year if the vehicle is registered for the current year at home.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: How many days after moving to Alabama may a new resident keep driving on a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A new resident with a valid license from the previous state may drive on it for thirty days after moving to Alabama.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: How does a new Alabama resident's grace window compare with the yearly cap for visitors from non-licensing countries?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: A new resident may drive on the old state's license for thirty days, which is a different window from the ninety-day yearly limit for visitors from countries that do not license drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: When may an out-of-state student attending school in Alabama drive without getting an Alabama license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: A non-resident full-time student enrolled at an Alabama school, college or trade school may drive on a valid home license.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which three groups based on age, out-of-state record, or testing will Alabama refuse to license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Alabama will not license anyone under sixteen, anyone suspended or revoked in any state, or anyone who fails a required exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Which substance-abuse or health conditions cause Alabama to deny a driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A license is also refused to a habitual drunkard or narcotics addict, or to someone whose physical or mental impairment, in the view of ALEA or the examiner, would prevent ordinary control of a vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What education requirement must license applicants under age 19 satisfy in Alabama?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Applicants under nineteen must meet Alabama Act ninety-three-three hundred sixty-eight, which calls for secondary school graduation or current attendance, with limited exclusions.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does Alabama's minimum regular licensing age differ from the age cutoff for the school-attendance rule?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: The minimum licensing age is sixteen, but the separate under-nineteen rule ties licensing to school graduation or attendance under Act ninety-three-three hundred sixty-eight.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What federal status must every applicant prove when applying for a first-time Alabama license or ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Every applicant for an original Alabama license or ID card must prove authorized presence in the United States under federal law.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which two document-count options prove your identity at the counter, and what list must always be represented?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: For identification you bring two documents with at least one bearing a photo, or three non-photo documents, and either way one must be from the Primary Listing.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does the two-document ID path differ from the three-document ID path regarding photos?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: The two-document identification path needs at least one photo document, while the three-document path may be all non-photo, and both need one Primary Listing item.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Which three items must you bring to transfer an out-of-state driver license to Alabama?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: To transfer an out-of-state license you show that license, a Social Security card or other accepted number proof, and one more Primary Listing document.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How do you prove your birth date if you have no prior Alabama license or ID record on file?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: A prior Alabama license or ID record can prove your birth date; without one, only an original or certified Primary Listing document is accepted.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which document versions are accepted at the license counter, and what must a certified copy show?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Only originals or agency-certified copies are accepted, and a certified copy must carry an original certification.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: What physical flaws or missing signatures will cause an examiner to reject an identity document?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: A document is rejected when key details show white-out, erasures or alterations, are missing or unreadable, are hidden by a fold, tear, hole or staple, or when it is not properly signed.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Which five elements must appear clearly on a notarized document for Alabama to accept it?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A notarized document needs a readable seal or stamp, the notary's readable name, a signature, the state of commission, and a commission expiration date still current when notarized.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Name the core identity records that qualify on Alabama's Primary Listing?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Primary documents include a certified U.S. birth certificate, an unexpired U.S. passport, an Alabama license or ID, a naturalization or citizenship certificate, and a valid foreign passport with a U.S. immigration document.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What must every 15-year-old bring, and what extra rule applies to a foreign birth certificate without a US passport?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Every fifteen-year-old applicant must show a certified U.S. birth certificate, and a foreign birth certificate must be translated into English and embassy-certified unless the person has a U.S. passport.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Which everyday school, military, or court records count on Alabama's secondary document list?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Secondary documents include a marriage license, a military ID or DD-two hundred fourteen, a school photo ID, a certified school record, and court decrees such as divorce, adoption or name change.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: When must you bring proof of your Social Security number, even if you opt out of printing it on your card?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Social Security number proof is needed for any license class, renewal, vessel license or ID card unless the number is on file, even if you do not want it printed.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What must acceptable Social Security proof display, and which five original records qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: That proof must be an original showing all nine digits, such as the card, a certified Social Security Administration letter, form DD two hundred fourteen, a W2, or a Medicare or Medicaid card whose number ends in A.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: At least how many days of authorized stay in the United States must immigration documents show?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Immigration documents must show at least thirty days of permitted stay remaining in the United States.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Which additional federal records may non-citizen applicants submit alongside their application?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Non-citizens may add documents such as an Employment Authorization Document with a valid Social Security card, a visa allowing more than thirty days of stay, or a valid I-ninety-four record.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Besides English, which eleven foreign languages are available for Alabama's written knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Written exams are offered in Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Thai and Vietnamese.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What testing accommodation is available if an applicant cannot read and understand the written knowledge check?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: An applicant unable to read and understand the knowledge test may take an oral exam, which the automated testing equipment can deliver.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: When did Alabama's Graduated Driver License law take effect, and what general minimum driving age does it set?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Alabama's graduated license law took effect October one, two thousand two, and the minimum driving age is sixteen, with certain exceptions and restrictions.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: What exact license class and restriction letter do you earn by passing the written knowledge exam at age 15?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: At fifteen you can earn a restricted Learner License by passing an exam drawn from this manual, giving a Class D license with a Y restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Who is legally allowed to ride in the front passenger seat beside a 15-year-old Y-restricted learner?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: Before age sixteen a Y-restricted learner drives only with a licensed Alabama driver aged twenty-one or older, or a licensed or certified instructor, in the seat beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: How does the front-seat companion rule change once a learner turns 16, and how long does a 15-year-old's permit last?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: After the sixteenth birthday any licensed driver may sit beside the learner, and the license issued at fifteen lasts four years and can be renewed once.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does the required front-seat supervisor for a 15-year-old learner compare with a learner who has turned 16?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: A learner aged fifteen needs a companion who is a licensed Alabama driver aged twenty-one or older or a driving instructor, while after the sixteenth birthday any licensed driver may ride beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How many years is a learner license issued at age 15 valid, and how many renewals are allowed?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The learner license issued at fifteen stays valid for four years and may be renewed only one time.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: What restriction code, supervision rule, and term length apply to a Learner License first earned at age 16 or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: A Learner License earned at sixteen or older also carries the Y restriction, requiring a licensed driver beside you, and is valid for four years.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Why is the companion rule simpler when you get your Learner License at 16 or older instead of 15?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: A learner license earned at sixteen or older needs only a licensed driver beside you, unlike the stricter companion rule that applies before age sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: What two sets of violations can get an Alabama Learner License suspended or revoked?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: A Learner License can be suspended or revoked for the same causes as a driver license, and also revoked for breaking its own terms.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: When does a teen aged 16 or 17 become eligible to take the road skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: A driver from sixteen to under eighteen may take the road test after holding a learner license, including a comparable out-of-state one, for six months or until turning eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How long must a 16- or 17-year-old hold a learner license before scheduling the road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Drivers aged sixteen to under eighteen must hold the learner license for six months or until turning eighteen before taking the road test.
