sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: What happens to your learner card, your Y restriction, and the fee when you pass the road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: You surrender the learner license at the road test, and passing removes the Y restriction for the rest of the four-year period at no cost.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Does lifting the Y restriction after passing the road skills check start a brand-new four-year expiration period?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Removing the Y restriction after the road test does not start a new term: the regular license runs only for the remainder of the original four-year period.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What license, restriction code, weight cap, and engine limit apply to 14- and 15-year-old motor-driven cycle riders?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: At fourteen or fifteen you can get a Class M license with a B restriction for a motor driven cycle of at most two hundred pounds and one hundred fifty cubic centimeters engine displacement.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: Starting at age 16, what vehicles does an unrestricted Class M motorcycle license cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: From sixteen a Class M license covers motorcycles only, meaning vehicles with a rider's seat or saddle built to run on no more than three wheels on the ground, tractors excluded.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How does a Class D license with a Y restriction differ from a Class M license with a B restriction?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Class D with a Y restriction is the car learner license, whereas Class M with a B restriction is limited to motor driven cycles for riders aged fourteen or fifteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: What kinds of driving restrictions can the ALEA Director add to a license, and what happens if you ignore one?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: The ALEA Director may add restrictions needed for safe driving, such as corrective lenses or mechanical aids, and violating one can cost you the license.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: At what minimum age can you earn an Alabama vessel license, and what two paths qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: A vessel license is available from age twelve by passing the vessel exam at a license office or showing an approved boating safety course certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What must you wear during the road test if your permit or license already carries a corrective-lens restriction?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: A driver restricted to corrective lenses must wear them during the road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What restriction gets added to your license if the counter vision screening shows you need corrective lenses?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: If the vision exam shows you need lenses to see better, you will be required to wear corrective lenses whenever you drive.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What is your next step after failing the counter vision check, and when can you finish testing?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Failing the vision exam means seeing a licensed eye specialist and returning the report to the examiner; if it shows you see well enough to drive safely, you may finish the test.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: How does the corrective-lens rule for the road test connect with the rule triggered by the vision screening?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Corrective lenses are required during the road test for drivers already restricted to them, and are required for all driving when the vision exam finds they are needed.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Which three core subjects appear on Alabama's knowledge test, and what single study source supplies every question?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: The knowledge test asks about Alabama traffic laws, road signs and safe-driving rules, and its questions come from this manual.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which test plus fee unlocks a learner license, and which test plus fee unlocks a regular driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: A learner-license applicant receives the learner license after passing the knowledge test and paying the fee, while a regular-license applicant receives the license after passing the road test and paying the fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: What testing and study rules apply if you want both a motor-driven cycle license and a car learner license?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Someone applying for both a motor driven cycle license and a learner license must take both exams, and cycle or motorcycle applicants study the separate motorcycle manual.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which knowledge-test applicants are allowed to use Alabama's automated testing terminals?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Automated testing is offered to every applicant who takes the knowledge test.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: How do the knowledge test and the road test split up the path from beginner to regular driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The knowledge test leads to the learner license, while the road test is the final step that leads to the regular license.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Who administers Alabama's road test, and who must accompany a 16-year-old applicant to the appointment?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: The road test, given by a driver license examiner, is the last step toward driving on public roads, and a sixteen-year-old applicant must come with a parent or guardian.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Which specific lights, signals, and sound equipment does the examiner inspect on your car before starting the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Before the road test the examiner checks that the vehicle is safe and has brake lights, left and right turn signals, and a horn.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which two vehicle papers must you show before the road test, and when is a rental car allowed?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: You must show proof of insurance and registration for the road test, and a rental car qualifies only if you are named on the rental agreement as an additional driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How do you insert a penny to check tire tread, and what visual cue means the tire must be replaced?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: For the penny tread test, insert Lincoln's head first into the deepest groove; if his whole head shows, the tires are too worn to drive on and need replacing.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: How should you position your back and feet in the driver's seat, and what safety risk comes from slouching?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Sit upright with your back against the seat and feet on the floor, because slouching can make the restraint system less effective.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Where should your right heel stay for pedal control, and how high should the top of the steering wheel sit?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Keep your heel on the floor while your foot pivots between brake and accelerator, and set the steering wheel top no higher than your shoulders and below your chin.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What can ALEA require if a driver appears to have a condition affecting safe driving, and what happens if unreported?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A driver who seems to have an impairment affecting driving may need a physician's statement and periodic examiner checks, and failing to report the condition can lead to revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: What identity proof does an Alabama non-driver ID require, and which three groups of residents is it meant for?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A non-driver ID card needs the same identity proof as a license and serves people who cannot physically qualify, hold no current Alabama license, or are giving up driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: How many years does an Alabama license last, and how many days early can you renew before expiration?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: An Alabama license expires four years after issue and may be renewed any time within one hundred eighty days before the expiration date printed on it.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Which residents temporarily away from Alabama may renew by mail, and what four-year rule applies to their card?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Military members and dependents, college students and others temporarily out of state for work may renew by mail if their photo-and-signature license was issued within the last four years.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: How long is Alabama's post-expiration renewal grace period, and does your license stay valid during those days?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: State law gives a sixty-day grace period after expiration for renewal, and the license stays valid during that period.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: How long after expiration can you renew without retesting, and what start date anchors the new four-year term?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: A license can be renewed without an exam within three years after expiring, and the new license runs four years from the last expiration date, not from the issue date.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Once you are past the grace period, may you legally drive on an expired license just because the three-year renewal window is open?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Although renewal stays possible up to three years after expiration, you may not legally drive on an expired license.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How does the 180-day window before expiration differ from the 60-day window after expiration?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The one hundred eighty-day window before expiration is for early renewal, while the sixty-day window after expiration is a grace period in which the license is still valid.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What single benefit does the three-year post-expiration window grant, and what does it strictly forbid?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Renewing without an exam is allowed up to three years after expiration, but that late-renewal window does not let you drive on the expired license.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does the four-year term start date differ between a timely renewal and a late renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: A normal renewal runs four years from issue, whereas a late renewal runs four years from the last expiration date.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Where and how do you replace a lost, destroyed, or unreadable license that has not expired?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: An unexpired license that is lost, destroyed or unreadable is replaced with a duplicate from the Probate Judge or License Commissioner, with no exam but with proof of identity such as a certified birth certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What criminal charges and penalties can strike someone who files a false affidavit to get a duplicate license?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: A false affidavit used to get a duplicate license can bring forgery or perjury charges, or both, punished by fine, prison or both.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: When do you apply for a duplicate license rather than a license renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A duplicate replaces an unexpired license that is lost, destroyed or unreadable, while a renewal replaces one that is expiring or expired.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Who must process changes to license classes, restrictions, or endorsements, and will mail forwarding deliver your card?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Adding, changing or removing classes, restrictions or endorsements requires a driver license examiner, and licenses and ID cards are never forwarded to another address.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Which documents are needed to change the name on your license, and where must STAR ID holders go?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A name change needs documents such as a marriage certificate or court order with an updated Social Security card, and STAR ID holders must make it at an ALEA office.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Within how many days of moving inside Alabama must you report your new address, and what does updating your record cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: After moving within Alabama you have thirty days to tell the Driver License Division your new address, which is updated on your record free of charge without reissuing the card.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does the cost of reporting an in-state address move compare with getting a corrected card after a name change?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: An address change within Alabama must be reported within thirty days and is free, while a corrected license after a name change carries a duplicate fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Which vehicles and craft do Alabama's non-commercial Classes D, M, and V each cover?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.memory_hook: D passenger, M cycles, V boats
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Class D covers generally all passenger vehicles not in Classes A, B, C or M; Class M covers motorcycles and motor-driven cycles, and Class V covers motorized watercraft.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Which license class covers standard passenger cars, and which two letters cover motorcycles and motorized boats?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.memory_hook: D cars, M bikes, V vessels
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Class D is the ordinary passenger-vehicle license, while Class M is for motorcycles and motor-driven cycles and Class V for motorized watercraft.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: What combined weight rating and towed-unit rating trigger the need for a Class A commercial license?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Class A is for combination vehicles with a combined weight rating over twenty-six thousand pounds when the towed vehicle is rated over ten thousand pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Which vehicles require a Class B license versus a Class C commercial license?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.memory_hook: B heavy single, C sixteen-plus hazmat
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Class B is for single vehicles rated over twenty-six thousand pounds towing no more than ten thousand pounds, and Class C is for vehicles built for sixteen or more people including the driver or placarded for hazardous materials.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: When two heavy rigs both exceed 26,000 pounds, what exact trailer rating separates Class A from Class B?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Class A and Class B both involve vehicles rated over twenty-six thousand pounds, but Class A applies when the towed vehicle is rated over ten thousand pounds and Class B when the tow is no more than that.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: Which lower vehicle classes may holders of Class A, Class B, or Class C licenses legally drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Higher classes include lower ones: Class A holders may drive Class B, C and D vehicles, Class B holders Class C and D, and Class C holders Class D.
pills: A DRIVES B C AND D

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: When does a licensed 12- or 13-year-old boater need an adult aboard, and at what age may a licensed teen boat solo?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Anyone who turned twelve after January one, two thousand two and holds a vessel license may operate a vessel only with a licensed adult aged twenty-one or older aboard and ready to take control, though a licensed operator aged fourteen or older may operate alone.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: What birthday cutoff exempts boaters from the vessel exam, and what office step is still required?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: People born before April twenty-eight, nineteen fifty-four need no vessel exam but must still visit a driver license office to have the vessel class issued.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: What credential must you physically carry whenever driving, and whom must you show it to on request?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: While driving you must carry the proper license or learner permit and show it to any law enforcement officer who asks.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Under Alabama's June 2024 Hands-Free Law, when does physically holding a wireless device become a violation?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Under the Hands-Free Law effective June two thousand twenty-four, holding a wireless device is a violation when the driver is seen drifting across lanes without signaling, swerving, or otherwise driving improperly.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: Within a 24-month window, what fines and license points apply to first, second, and third hands-free convictions?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.memory_hook: Fifty one, hundred two, one-fifty three
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: Within a twenty-four-month period, hands-free convictions cost a fifty dollars fine and one point the first time, one hundred dollars and two points the second, and one hundred fifty dollars and three points the third.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: How broadly does Alabama's Hands-Free Law define a wireless device?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: For this law a wireless device means any device used to start or receive communication information or data.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: How do the fine and points on second and third hands-free convictions within 24 months scale up from the first?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: A second hands-free conviction within twenty-four months doubles the first fine to one hundred dollars with two points, and a third brings one hundred fifty dollars with three points.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Beyond court fines or jail, in which four administrative ways can a traffic conviction cost your driving privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: On top of whatever the court imposes, a conviction for breaking a traffic law can cost you your license through cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What minimum reinstatement fee applies before you can get relicensed after losing your Alabama privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Getting relicensed after a cancellation, suspension, revocation or disqualification requires a reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars plus any other state-law requirements.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: How much extra money gets tacked on if you fail to surrender a canceled, revoked, or suspended license on time?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Failing to surrender your license within the allowed time after it is canceled, revoked or suspended adds a fifty dollars fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which extra reinstatement charges follow a drug-related conviction versus an unpaid child-support suspension?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Reinstatement after a drug-related conviction costs an extra twenty-five dollars, and reinstating after a suspension for unpaid child support costs an extra fifty dollars.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: How do Alabama's base reinstatement fee and its three possible extra charges stack together?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: Every reinstatement costs at least one hundred dollars, with fifty dollars more for a late license surrender, twenty-five dollars more after a drug conviction, and fifty dollars more after a child-support suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: For what eligibility or paperwork reasons may the ALEA Director cancel a driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: The ALEA Director may cancel a license on finding the holder was not entitled to it, and missing or false application information or application fraud is also grounds for cancellation.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Once a revocation period finally ends, what must a driver do to get licensed again?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Once a revocation period ends, the driver may apply for a new license but must take and pass the complete examinations again.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does getting licensed after revocation differ from the core reason behind a cancellation?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: After revocation you must apply for a new license and pass the complete examinations, whereas after cancellation the issue is that you were never entitled to the license at all.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Which fatal crash or criminal-use convictions force the ALEA Director to revoke a license?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: The Director must revoke a license after a conviction for manslaughter or homicide caused by operating a motor vehicle, or for using a motor vehicle to commit a felony.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Which alcohol or controlled-substance driving convictions trigger mandatory license revocation in Alabama?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Revocation is also mandatory on a second or later conviction for driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle under the influence of alcohol, or for driving as a habitual user of, or while too impaired by, a controlled substance to drive safely.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Which conviction number makes license revocation mandatory for alcohol or controlled-substance impaired driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Mandatory revocation for driving under the influence of alcohol is triggered by a second or subsequent conviction, and the same holds for controlled-substance impairment.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What failure at an injury or fatal crash scene triggers mandatory license revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Failing to stop, give aid, or identify yourself after a crash that kills or injures another person is a mandatory revocation offense.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which sworn-statement crime, twelve-month reckless streak, or vehicle-theft offense also mandates revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Perjury or a false sworn statement to the Director about license or vehicle laws, three reckless driving convictions within twelve months, and unauthorized use of someone else's vehicle all require revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What triggers a license suspension, and what two snags can block reinstatement afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: A license may be suspended after certain convictions or a finding of incompetence to drive, and it is reinstated afterward unless it expired meanwhile or the suspension requirements were not all met.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Even when your suspension calendar finishes, which two things prevent automatic license reinstatement?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: A suspended license is reinstated when the period ends, unless it expired during the suspension or the suspension requirements were not all met.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Which three patterns of poor driving skill or repeated violations are grounds for license suspension?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Suspension grounds include serious moving-violation convictions frequent enough to show disrespect for traffic laws, a record of habitually reckless or negligent driving, and incompetence to drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: How can lending out, damaging, or misbehaving out of state get your Alabama license suspended?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Allowing unlawful or fraudulent use of your license, mutilating it, or committing an offense in another state that would be grounds here can also lead to suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Which police-pursuit, street-racing, or traffic-court failures can suspend your license?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Convictions for fleeing or trying to elude a police officer or for racing on highways can bring suspension, as can failing to answer a traffic summons on time or failing to pay.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: Which age group of drivers risks license suspension for withdrawing from school before graduation?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Drivers aged fifteen through eighteen who withdraw from school before graduating, under certain conditions, can have the license suspended.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Which insurance, family-court, or health issues appear on Alabama's suspension list?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Failing to keep SR-twenty-two insurance when it is required, unpaid child support, and medical reasons are further grounds for suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: What record point count or Graduated Driver License ticket count appears on the suspension list?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: The suspension list includes having four or more points on the driving record, or two or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: How does the four-point suspension listing relate to the two-violation Graduated Driver License listing?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: The suspension list names four or more points on the record or two or more moving violations on a graduated license as two separate grounds for suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: How does Alabama's suspension list treat a first-offense DUI or drug conviction for juveniles and adults?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A first-offense DUI or drug offense, for a juvenile or an adult, is listed as grounds for suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Does a traffic conviction outside Alabama add points to your Alabama driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Alabama's point system suspends licenses on uniform grounds, and points are charged for listed offenses whether they happen in Alabama or elsewhere.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: How many points hit your record for an alcohol-and-driving conviction that does not trigger mandatory revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: A conviction on a charge involving drinking alcohol and driving that did not require mandatory revocation carries six points.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: How many points do reckless driving, vehicular reckless endangerment, and Admin Per Se violations each carry?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Reckless driving or reckless endangerment with a motor vehicle carries six points, and an Admin Per Se violation also carries six points.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: How many points are assessed for failing to yield right-of-way or illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Failing to yield the right of way and passing a stopped school bus each carry five points.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: By how many points do reckless driving and Admin Per Se exceed failing to yield or passing a school bus?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Reckless driving and an Admin Per Se violation each carry six points, one more than failing to yield or passing a stopped school bus.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How do the points for passing a stopped school bus compare with an emergency-vehicle violation?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Passing a stopped school bus carries five points, while an emergency vehicle violation carries two points.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: How many points apply to wrong-side driving or illegal passing versus following too closely?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Driving on the wrong side of the road or passing illegally carries four points, and following too closely carries three points.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How do the point values for tailgating and work-zone marker violations compare with illegal passing?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Following too closely and ignoring work-zone markers each carry three points, one less than illegal passing at four points.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: At what exact speed over the posted limit does speeding jump from 2 points to 5 points?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.memory_hook: Two up to twenty-five, five above
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Speeding one to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit carries two points, but speeding twenty-six miles per hour or more over the limit carries five points.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Speeding 26 mph or more over the limit carries the exact same 5-point hit as which right-of-way offense?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Speeding up to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit costs two points, but twenty-six miles per hour or more over costs five points, the same as failing to yield.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: How many points are charged for failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers carries three points.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: How many points apply to inability to control a vehicle, improper lane use, drinking while operating, motorcycle misuse, or emergency violations?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Inability to control the vehicle, an improper lane violation, drinking alcohol while operating a vehicle, improper motorcycle operation, and an emergency vehicle violation each carry two points.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: How many points do missing or wrong turn signals, improper turns, coasting, and unsafe operation each add?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Failing to signal or using the wrong turn signal, making an improper turn, coasting, and unsafe operation each carry two points.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Over a two-year window, how many suspension days follow 12–14 points, 15–17 points, and 18–20 points?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: Within a two-year period, twelve to fourteen points bring a sixty-day suspension, fifteen to seventeen points bring ninety days, and eighteen to twenty points bring one hundred twenty days.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: Over a two-year window, how long is your license suspended at 21–23 points versus 24 or more points?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Within a two-year period, twenty-one to twenty-three points bring a one hundred eighty-day suspension, and twenty-four or more points bring three hundred sixty-five days.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: At what two-year point totals do Alabama's shortest 60-day suspension and longest 365-day suspension begin?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: The shortest point suspension, sixty days, starts at twelve points within two years, and the longest, three hundred sixty-five days, starts at twenty-four points.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: What kind of hearing may you request after getting a suspension notice, and where is it held?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: After receiving a suspension notice, a driver may ask for a pre-suspension or administrative hearing before an ALEA agent in the home county.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: What are the two ways to submit a request for an Alabama administrative license hearing?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: An administrative hearing can be requested in writing to Driver License Services or online.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What highway design features set freeways apart and make long trips safer with less driver fatigue?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.memory_hook: Divided lanes, zero stops, zero crossings
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Freeways are multi-lane, controlled-access, divided highways with no stops and no cross traffic, built for long trips with less fatigue and more safety.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: What two habits anchor safe freeway driving, and which lane belongs to slower-moving vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Safe freeway driving means keeping pace with traffic and staying alert, and vehicles moving slower than the normal flow must keep to the right.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Why should you pick one freeway lane matching your desired pace instead of weaving across lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Weaving from lane to lane is dangerous; pick a lane moving at the pace you want and stay in it.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Before shifting freeway lanes to overtake or exit, what two steps must come well ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: When you must change lanes to pass or exit, check traffic carefully and signal well before you move.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Where must you park during a freeway breakdown, and where should you stay if possible?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: In a freeway breakdown, park completely off the traveled lanes and stay with the vehicle if you possibly can.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Which three visual distress signals tell patrolling officers you need help on a freeway shoulder?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.memory_hook: Open trunk, raised hood, white cloth
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: The distress signals are an open trunk, a raised hood if weather allows, and a white cloth tied to a door handle or antenna, and an officer who sees them will help.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Under what sole circumstance is parking along a freeway permitted?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Parking on the freeway is not allowed except in an emergency.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: How do entrance ramps and acceleration lanes work together when joining a freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Entrance ramps are short one-way ramps that lead to an acceleration lane, where you speed up to match through traffic if possible.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What three actions move you smoothly from the acceleration lane into live freeway traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: From the acceleration lane, watch for a gap, signal, and merge smoothly into traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: While through drivers should make room, who legally yields when entering a freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Freeway drivers should leave room for merging traffic, but an entering driver must yield if they do not.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: When, if ever, should you come to a full stop inside a freeway acceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Do not stop completely in the acceleration lane unless it is absolutely necessary.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: How must you enter a freeway ramp posted with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: On an entrance ramp with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane, entering drivers obey the sign and stop if needed instead of forcing their way in.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: How does a highway interchange let traffic cross, enter, or leave without conflicting?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: An interchange joins two highways at different levels with separate connecting roads, so vehicles can cross, enter or leave without interfering with others.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What are the four standard highway interchange designs named in the Alabama manual?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Four common interchange types are directional, cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What traffic pattern does a directional interchange serve, and how are minor turns handled?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: A directional interchange serves heavy traffic moving between only two legs, with other movements handled by ordinary diamond-type ramps.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How does a cloverleaf interchange connect four directions, and which two conflicts does it eliminate?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: A cloverleaf interchange uses loop connections for turns on and off the freeway from four directions and removes left-turn and cross-traffic conflicts.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: How many ramps form a diamond interchange, and where do left turns take place?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: A diamond interchange has four ramps for entering or leaving with the flow, and left turns are made after you leave the freeway.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: At what roadway meeting shape is a trumpet interchange built?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: A trumpet interchange gives freeway access where another road meets it in a T, as a variation of the directional or diamond design.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: At a diamond interchange, do left turns happen on the freeway mainline or after leaving on a ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: A diamond interchange lets you enter and leave with the flow on four ramps, and any left turn comes only after you are off the freeway, never on it.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: How should you position your vehicle as your planned freeway exit approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Plan your exit early and watch the signs, moving into the proper lane well ahead of time.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Where must you shed speed when leaving a freeway, and what awaits at the ramp end?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: To exit, signal, enter the deceleration lane and slow there, never slowing suddenly on the freeway itself, and be ready to yield or stop at the end of the ramp.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Which three moves are strictly forbidden if you roll past your freeway exit, and what should you do?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: If you miss your exit, do not stop, back up or turn around; go on to the next exit and come back.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What two vehicle conditions are prerequisites for safe driving under Alabama equipment law?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: You cannot be a safe driver unless your vehicle is properly equipped and mechanically sound, and Alabama law sets the safety equipment required.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Which two independent braking controls must every automobile carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Every automobile needs two separate ways of applying the brakes: a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: What must every vehicle's muffler prevent, and which exhaust modifications are outlawed?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Every vehicle needs a working muffler that stops excessive or unusual noise, and muffler cutouts, bypasses and similar devices are forbidden.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: What deadly hazard requires periodic inspection of your vehicle's exhaust system?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: The exhaust system must not leak carbon monoxide into the vehicle and should be checked periodically.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: What equipment rule applies to every motor vehicle built with a windshield?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Any motor vehicle with a windshield must have wipers in good working order.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: How many feet behind the vehicle must required rearview mirrors show clearly?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: All vehicles must have rear view mirrors that let the driver see two hundred feet behind.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: Which four front and rear lamp types make up Alabama's minimum vehicle lighting list?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Required lighting includes a minimum of two white headlights, one or more red taillights, a brake light, and a light over the rear license plate.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: From how far must all required lamps be seen, and how far ahead must properly aimed high beams reach?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: All lights must be visible from at least five hundred feet, and the high beam must light objects at least three hundred fifty feet away and stay properly aimed.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: Is flashing both turn signals together permitted to warn approaching traffic of a vehicle hazard?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Flashing both turn signals, or another pair of lights, at the same time to warn of a vehicle hazard is permitted.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How do the footage rules compare across rearview mirrors, lamp visibility, and high-beam reach?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.memory_hook: Two hundred mirror, five hundred, three-fifty
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Rear view mirrors must show two hundred feet behind, while every light must be visible from five hundred feet and high beams must reach three hundred fifty feet.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: What shares of crash deaths stem from hitting the steering assembly versus windshield or dash without belts?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: In crashes, steering assemblies cause thirty percent of fatal injuries and hitting the windshield, its frame or the dash causes another forty percent, second collisions that safety belts can prevent.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.front: Under what age do children require special infant or child restraints under the manual's equipment section?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.expected_back: Children under six years old need special child and infant restraints to protect them from serious injury or death.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: Why are special child and infant seats critical for young passengers in crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Traffic crashes are the leading killer of children, and child and infant restraints keep small children from becoming flying missiles in a crash.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: What sound device must every motor vehicle carry, and who alone may mount bells, sirens, or whistles?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Every motor vehicle needs a working horn, and bells, sirens or exhaust whistles are allowed only on emergency vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: When is honking your horn lawful, and what can needless honking bring?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.memory_hook: Safety warnings only, needless risks arrest
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Use the horn only to give a warning reasonably needed for safety, never to announce arrival or call passengers, because needless use can lead to arrest.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: What four checks cover tire load rating, air pressure, and uneven tread wear?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.memory_hook: Right load, proper air, check wear
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Buy tires rated to carry your car's weight, check pressure often, never drive on under-inflated tires, and have uneven wear checked for wheel or alignment problems.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: Below what tread depth measurement does an automobile tire become illegal in Alabama?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: A tire is illegal once its tread is less than one sixteenth inch deep.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: Which driving habits and trip checks protect your tires and spare from premature failure?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.memory_hook: Smooth starts, cool breaks, check spare
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: Avoid jack-rabbit starts and screeching stops unless truly necessary, go easy on corners and rough roads, let tires cool on long hot trips, and check the spare now and then.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: What rule governs mixing different tire types on your car or between front and rear axles?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: Never use different types of tires, and ask your dealer before mixing types between front and back.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: Which six vehicle systems wear down over time and require periodic inspection to prevent serious crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: Brakes, exhaust, cooling systems, lights, wipers and tires wear out, and any one left unmaintained could cause a serious crash, so have the car checked.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: What route details should you lock down with a map before starting a freeway trip?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: Plan freeway trips with a map, deciding exactly where you will get on and off.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: Why must you check fuel, water, oil, and all five tires before entering a freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: Check fuel, water and oil before a freeway trip, because no service stations sit directly on freeways, and check every tire, including the spare.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: Where do most pupil-transportation injuries and deaths happen, and what does the manual call that area?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: Most children hurt or killed in pupil transportation are outside the bus, struck by drivers who ignore its flashing red lights and stop arm, in the area called the DEATH ZONE.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Which core attitudes and habits define a safe driver on every single trip?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: A safe driver knows and respects the rules, follows proper procedures, keeps a good attitude and is courteous at all times, using good habits on every trip, short or long.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What steps belong right after climbing into the car and before turning on the ignition?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: On entering the car, adjust the seat and mirrors, make sure passengers are seated so they will not interfere, and buckle up with every passenger before switching on the ignition.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: How does starting an engine with a manual transmission differ from starting an automatic?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: With a manual transmission push in the clutch before turning the key; with an automatic, have the indicator in park or neutral and press the brake as you turn the key.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: How should you sit and grip the steering wheel, and when may one hand leave it?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Sit upright and grip the outside rim with both hands, firm enough for control but not so tight it slows your reflexes, removing a hand only to signal or operate the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What sequence gets you safely out of a parallel parking spot and into traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: To leave a parallel parking space, look over your shoulder and in the mirrors, wait until clear, signal, and enter the nearest lane, staying there until a lane change is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: What rule governs staying inside your lane instead of drifting across lane lines?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: You must keep within a single lane, never weaving between lanes or straddling the lane marking.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: Does a roadway section need painted lines to count legally as a traffic lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: A traffic lane is any part of a road wide enough for a vehicle or line of vehicles to travel safely, and it exists whether or not it is marked.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: When should you decide on an upcoming turn and merge into the proper turning lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Plan each turn early rather than at the last moment, and move into the proper turn lane well before it once the change is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: At least how far ahead must your turn signal start blinking, and how long does it stay on?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet before turning and keep the signal on until you actually turn, so both pedestrians and drivers know your intention.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: While actually rounding a corner, where must your hands stay and who holds right-of-way?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Both hands belong on the wheel during the turn itself, and pedestrians have the right of way over motor vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: From slowing down on approach to finishing in your new lane, what steps complete a safe turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Slow down before turning, check front, rear and sides for cars and pedestrians, finish in the proper lane, and cancel the signal afterward.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Why might you pair hand and arm signals with your electric turn signals during daytime driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: In daylight you may add hand and arm signals to your signal lights, because bright sunlight can make a flashing signal hard to see.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Which lane do you start in and which lane do you enter when turning right from a four-lane highway?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: For a right turn from a four-lane or divided highway, get into the right lane well ahead and turn tightly into the right lane of the cross street.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Unless signs or markings allow extra turn lanes, how do you execute a left turn off a four-lane or divided road?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: For a left turn there, move to the lane nearest the center line or divider, turn from the inside lane without a wide swing, and enter just right of the cross street's center line, unless signs or markings allow turns from more lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: On a four-lane highway, how does your starting lane for a right turn compare with your starting lane for a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: A right turn from a four-lane highway starts in the right lane and ends tight in the cross street's right lane, while a left turn starts from the inside lane nearest the center line.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: When must your turn signal start flashing, and when do you switch it off?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Turn signals go on at least one hundred feet before the turn and kept on until you turn, and then must be switched off once the maneuver is complete.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Do hand and arm signals replace your electric turn lights in daylight, or how are they used?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Signal lights are the standard turn signal, and hand and arm signals are an addition for daylight when sunlight can wash out the light, not a replacement.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Under what visibility and traffic conditions is a three-point turn normally permitted?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: A three-point turn reverses your direction and must not endanger other traffic, so it is normally allowed only where you can be seen from far away and traffic makes it safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: On which road types and sightline distances are three-point turns strictly outlawed?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Three-point turns are banned on interstate freeways, on curves, and near hilltops where drivers approaching within five hundred feet from either direction cannot see you.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: Which laws regulate three-point turns, and can you count on a sign marking every illegal spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Local ordinances govern three-point turns, there may be no warning signs, and prohibiting signs are usually posted only at hazardous spots.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: If no sign forbids a turnaround, may you make a three-point turn when oncoming traffic inside five hundred feet lacks sightlines?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Three-point turns are prohibited where oncoming drivers within five hundred feet cannot see you, even when no sign forbids the turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: When do you shed speed for a curve, and how do you use the gas while rounding it?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Slow down before a curve so you do not cross the center line or leave the road, entering slowly enough to accelerate slightly while rounding it.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: How do the road rights and traffic duties of bicyclists compare with those of motor vehicle drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: People on bicycles have the same road rights and responsibilities as people in motor vehicles, so drivers and cyclists alike must know and obey state traffic laws.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: Where on a roadway does a bicyclist normally ride, and which situations allow moving left?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: A cyclist on a roadway rides as close as practicable to the right curb or edge, except when passing, preparing a left turn, or avoiding hazards such as debris, opening car doors or pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Are cyclists allowed to ride two abreast in Alabama, and which direction must they travel?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: People on bicycles may ride two abreast at all times, and they must ride with the flow of traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does the keep-right rule fit together with riding two abreast and moving left on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Cyclists normally keep as far right as practicable, yet they may also ride two abreast at all times and move left to pass, to turn left, or to avoid hazards.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which signals do bicyclists use to warn others before turning, changing lanes, or stopping?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Cyclists signal turns, lane changes and stops with the same hand and arm signals that drivers use.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: When a bicycle lane is present, must cyclists use it, and what is Alabama's rule on sidewalk riding?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Cyclists must use a bicycle lane where one exists; sidewalks and multipurpose paths are not bicycle lanes, and riding a bicycle on the sidewalk is illegal in Alabama.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Which age group of cyclists must wear a fastened helmet, and on what public places does that apply?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Cyclists under sixteen must wear a securely fastened helmet on public roads, other public rights-of-way, public bicycle paths and in public parks.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: What are the only three reasons a motorist may legally enter a marked bicycle lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: A driver may enter a bicycle lane only to park where parking is allowed, to enter or leave the highway, or to prepare for a turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: How should you position your vehicle before turning across a bicycle lane at an intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: To turn across a bicycle lane, move into the lane before the turn, but only when doing so does not endanger a cyclist using it.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: When must drivers stay out of a bicycle lane, and how do they handle turning across one?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Drivers stay out of bicycle lanes except to park, enter or leave the highway, or prepare a turn, and for a turn across the lane they move into it first when it is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: At least how much space must you leave when passing a bicyclist in Alabama, and why does speed matter?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Alabama law requires at least three feet between your vehicle and a person on a bicycle when you pass, and wind from fast vehicles can push a cyclist enough to cause a crash.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: How does the group covered by the bicycle helmet mandate differ from who must obey the three-foot passing rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: The bicycle helmet rule applies to riders under sixteen, while the three-foot passing clearance applies to every driver passing any cyclist.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: In which road locations and traffic situations should you hold back instead of passing a cyclist?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Avoid passing a cyclist uphill, on curves, where visibility is limited, or when other vehicles occupy the lane you would need to use.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: How should you behave behind a cyclist when a narrow roadway makes safe passing impossible?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: When a narrow road makes passing unsafe, stay a safe distance behind the cyclist, without tailgating or blasting the horn, until you can pass.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: At which three everyday conflict points must drivers scan extra carefully for approaching bicycles?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Watch closely for cyclists at intersections, when crossing sidewalks, and when entering or leaving alleys or driveways.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: What happens to a bicycle's braking power in wet weather, and how must drivers adjust?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: A bicycle brakes far less well in wet weather, so drivers should allow for its reduced ability to slow or stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What equipment should bicycles carry for night riding, and how should motorists adjust after dark?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: State law says bicycles should carry lights or reflectors for night riding, and drivers need extra caution in darkness or poor visibility.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: What road rights do motorcyclists hold, and which group of riders shows up in many motorcycle crashes?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: Motorcyclists share the same road rights and responsibilities as other users, and a substantial share of motorcycle crashes involve riders with limited experience.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: How wide is a motorcycle compared with a passenger car, and how does that affect a driver's eyes?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: A motorcycle is only about two feet wide against a car's five to six feet, so it is hard to pick out and its distance and speed are hard to judge.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Which car maneuver causes a huge share of car-motorcycle injury crashes, and what must you verify first?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: Left turns in front of an oncoming motorcycle cause a large share of car-motorcycle injury crashes, so look twice and know the motorcycle's speed before you turn left.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Why is merely spotting an oncoming motorcycle not enough before starting a left turn across its lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Seeing a motorcycle is not enough before a left turn, because drivers also misjudge its distance and speed, so look again and know its speed first.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: Before pulling out or turning in front of a signaling vehicle, what must you confirm first?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Before turning in front of any vehicle, make sure it is really turning and not going straight with a forgotten signal still blinking.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: How much following time should you keep behind a motorcycle in normal conditions, and why avoid tailgating?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: Leave the same two-second following distance behind a motorcycle as behind any vehicle, since tailgating can distract the rider.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: May you pull alongside a motorcycle inside the same traffic lane if the lane looks wide enough?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane, and a driver must never pull alongside it in the same lane, even a wide one, which is illegal and very dangerous.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: If a motorcyclist rides near one edge of the lane, may a car squeeze into the open side?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: A motorcyclist changing position within the lane is still using a full lane, so a car may never share that lane even when the rider is far to one side.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: When must you stretch your following gap behind a motorcycle beyond normal, and what visual trap appears?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Give motorcycles even more following distance in darkness, rain or on wet, slippery roads, and watch for rain glare that can hide a rider at night.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How does your two-second dry-road gap behind a motorcycle change when darkness, rain, or slick pavement hits?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Behind a motorcycle the normal gap is the same two seconds as behind a car, but in darkness, rain or on slippery roads the gap should be longer.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.front: Which wind forces and road-surface hazards can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or lane path abruptly?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.expected_back: Crosswinds on open highways and bridges, windblasts from fast large trucks, and road hazards such as gravel, seams, manhole covers, rough rail crossings or metal bridges can make a rider suddenly change speed or direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Does a medicine need a doctor's prescription to impair your driving, or do store-bought remedies count too?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Many drugs can weaken your ability to drive safely, whether a doctor prescribed them or you bought them over the counter.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What specific question should you ask your physician whenever starting a prescription medication?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: When you take prescription medicine, ask your doctor about any side effects that could affect your driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Which four impairing ingredients lurk inside some non-prescription cold pills and allergy remedies?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Some non-prescription allergy remedies and cold pills contain codeine, alcohol, antihistamines or bromides, and each of these can affect driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: What three mental or alertness side effects can antihistamines trigger—so strongly some double as sleep aids?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Antihistamines, taken for cold congestion and allergies, can cause inattention, confusion and drowsiness, and some are even used as sleep aids.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: What medical class are barbiturates, and what drunk-like effects appear when someone overuses them?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Barbiturates are sedatives used mainly for sleep, and overusing them brings drowsiness, confusion and poor coordination much like drunkenness, leaving the person unfit to drive.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How does Alabama's manual contrast antihistamine side effects with overused barbiturates?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Antihistamines may cause drowsiness and confusion as side effects, while barbiturates produce drunk-like symptoms when used to excess.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: How can illegal drugs like hallucinogens and heroin affect environmental awareness, and may users ever drive?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: The most dangerous drugs, such as LSD and heroin, are available only illegally and can leave users unaware of their surroundings, so no one under their influence may drive.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What link do studies cited in Alabama's manual find between marijuana use and traffic violations?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Studies cited in the manual link marijuana use to more traffic-violation arrests, and experts agree it should not be used when driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: Does mixing alcohol with medication merely double impairment, or do something far worse?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Combining alcohol with drugs does not merely double the effect; it multiplies it and has caused deaths, so never drink while taking medicine.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: When a driver lives with a chronic illness or physical impairment, who is responsible for explaining any driving restrictions?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: For a chronic illness or physical impairment, the physician is responsible for telling the patient about any driving limits that may apply.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which bad habit causes most rear-end crashes, and which space around your car is easiest to control?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions, and the space ahead of your car, called following distance, is the space you can control most easily.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: Which two real-time factors should determine how much following distance you leave ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Set your following distance by the speed of traffic and the condition of the road, leaving enough room to stop if you must.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Which time-based method replaced the old one-car-length-per-ten-miles-per-hour formula in Alabama's manual?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: The old rule of one car length for every ten miles per hour has given way to the two-second rule, which the manual calls easier to apply and safer.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: How do you apply Alabama's two-second rule using a fixed roadside landmark?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: For the two-second rule, pick a fixed object ahead, start counting one thousand one, one thousand two as the car ahead passes it, and if you reach it first, ease off until the gap is safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Under what weather, road, or vehicle-length conditions should you stretch your following count to four or five seconds?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: When road or weather conditions are poor, stretch the gap to a four- or five-second count, and use the longer gap too when driving a vehicle longer than a car.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How does Alabama's following-distance count shift from ideal passenger-car driving to bad conditions or long rigs?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: The two-second count is for good conditions, while bad roads, bad weather or a long vehicle call for four or five seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: How should your right foot respond immediately whenever brake lights glow or the gap ahead shrinks?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Watch for brake lights and a shrinking gap ahead, and move your foot to the brake pedal right away so you are ready to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What does stopping distance help determine, and which human factor governs actual stopping distance first?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: How far your car needs to stop helps decide a safe speed, and actual stopping distance depends first on the driver's mental and physical reaction time.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How does rough dry concrete compare in stopping grip against slippery brick or smooth asphalt?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Pavement type and condition change stopping distance a great deal, since rough dry concrete grips far better than slippery brick or smooth asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: Which three tire characteristics govern stopping traction, and where do you verify proper tire size?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Tire type, condition and tread depth all determine how much traction you have for stopping, so check the owner's manual or a dealer for the right tire size.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: What stopping trade-off separates wide tires from small narrow tires across dry versus wet roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Large, wide tires may stop sooner on smooth dry roads but skid or hydroplane more easily when wet, while small, narrow tires may cut through standing water yet lose overall stopping power.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: Beyond tires, which suspension and brake factors affect stopping—and what happens if one wheel locks early?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Chassis design, weight distribution, suspension, shock absorbers and the type, condition and balance of the brakes all affect stopping, and a brake that locks before the others can cause serious trouble.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: Which wind condition surprises many drivers by stretching a sudden high-speed highway stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Wind direction and speed also affect stopping, and drivers often do not realize how much difference a strong tail wind makes during a sudden high-speed stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: On Alabama's stopping chart, what thinking, braking, and total footage apply at twenty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: The manual's stopping-distance chart gives twenty-seven feet of thinking distance plus thirty-four point seven feet of braking distance, or sixty-one point seven feet in total, at twenty-five miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: At fifty-five miles per hour on Alabama's chart, how many feet go to reacting, braking, and total stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: On the same chart, at fifty-five miles per hour a driver covers sixty feet while reacting and one hundred sixty-eight feet while braking, two hundred twenty-eight feet in all.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: At sixty-five miles per hour on Alabama's chart, what thinking, braking, and total distances are needed?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: At sixty-five miles per hour the chart shows seventy-one feet of thinking distance and two hundred thirty-four point seven feet of braking distance, a total of three hundred five point seven feet.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: What four immediate obligations apply right after you are involved in a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: If you are in a crash you must stop at once and help anyone injured, call for medical help if needed, and warn other traffic with flags, flares or whatever you have before police arrive.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Under what sole life-or-death threat may you move an injured crash victim—and how should they rest?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Do not move injured people unless it is absolutely necessary to get them away from fire or another danger, and keep them lying or sitting down until trained medical help arrives.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: Along with comfort and shock care, what caution does Alabama's manual give untrained helpers?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Give first aid, keep the injured comfortable and treat for shock, but remember a layman can give too much first aid; a Red Cross or similar course is recommended.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: Which three details must you state—and which credential must you display—to others involved in any crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: In any type of crash you must stop, tell the others involved your name, address and registration number, and let them see your driver license.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Whose names and addresses—plus scene notes—should you write down for your own protection at a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: At a crash, collect the names and addresses of everyone involved and of any witnesses, and note other relevant details.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: What insurance details must you share if another involved party asks—and what if you lack them on-scene?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: If another person involved asks, give the name and address of your liability insurance company and your local agent, and if you cannot do so at the scene, provide it later.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: What three options satisfy Alabama law if you bump into an unattended parked vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: If you hit an unattended vehicle, either notify the police, try to find its owner, or leave a written note with your name and address where it will easily be seen on that vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: What must you do if a driving mishap damages a mailbox, fence, sign, or other non-vehicle property?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: When a mishap damages any other kind of property, you must let the property owner know.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: How fast must an injury or fatal crash be reported—and how does city versus state-highway jurisdiction split?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: A crash with injury or death must be reported by the fastest means available, to local police inside a city or town or to the State Troopers on a state highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: After injury, death, or five hundred dollars damage, when and within how many days is Safety Responsibility form thirty-one required?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: After a crash with injury, death or five hundred dollars or more in damage, the involved driver has thirty days to send a written Form SR-thirty-one if the at-fault party was uninsured; when both parties were insured, neither files it.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Which state unit receives Safety Responsibility thirty-one forms, and what two delivery methods work?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: SR-thirty-one forms go to the ALEA Safety Responsibility Unit by mail or can be submitted online through ALEA's driver license website.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How does immediate police notification for injury crashes contrast with the thirty-day written crash form?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A crash with injury or death is reported to police right away, while the written SR-thirty-one within thirty days applies when an uninsured at-fault party is involved.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: What four scene facts should a witness give dispatchers when calling in a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: A witness reporting a crash should give the exact location, whether the road is blocked, and the likely damage and injuries, and every crash should go to the law enforcement agency with jurisdiction.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: What shape, colors, and markings identify the advance railroad warning—and how many feet ahead does it stand?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: The round railroad warning sign is yellow with a black X and the letters RR, and it stands seven hundred fifty feet before the track to warn of a crossing ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: What three painted road markings work together ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Before a crossing the pavement may carry a large X with two R's, a yellow line ahead of it means no passing, and white lines beside the track mark where to stop for a train.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: What is mandatory the instant red railroad crossing lights start flashing?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: When crossing lights start flashing you must always stop and wait until it is safe to go.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: When red lights flash and crossing gates drop, what two conditions must both finish before you roll?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: Red flashing lights warn you to stop as crossing gates come down, and you stay stopped until the gates rise and the lights quit flashing.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: How must you handle a railroad crossing that has no active lights or gates?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: At a crossing with no warning device, slow down and look and listen for trains before going on.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.front: What action does a white railroad crossbuck direct, and what does a numbered plaque underneath warn?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.expected_back: The crossbuck sign appears at most crossings and means slow down and be ready to stop when a train is seen; a sign under it shows the number of tracks when there is more than one.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How do the round yellow railroad marker and the white crossbuck differ in placement?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: The advance railroad sign is round and yellow and stands seven hundred fifty feet before the track, while the crossbuck stands at the crossing itself.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.front: Which four bus and hazmat vehicle groups must stop before every railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.expected_back: School buses, church buses, all passenger buses, and trucks hauling flammables, explosives or other hazardous material must stop before every railroad crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.front: Within what exact range of feet from the tracks must a required railroad stop take place?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.expected_back: The manual says a stop at a railroad crossing must be made within fifteen to fifty feet of it.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.front: How fast may you approach tracks, and what is required at crossings with active electric or mechanical warnings?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.expected_back: Approach slowly enough to be sure you can stop once a train first comes into view, and come to a complete stop at crossings protected by electric or mechanical signals as the manual directs.

sec07-card-sec07-F46.front: Besides stopping for gates or trains, what extra check applies whenever a crossing spans multiple tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F46.expected_back: You must stop when the crossing gate is down or a train is approaching, and with more than one track you must be sure every track is clear before crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How do railroad stopping rules split between buses or hazmat trucks and ordinary passenger cars?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Buses and hazardous-material trucks must always stop at crossings, while other drivers must stop for flashing lights, lowered gates or an approaching train.

sec07-card-sec07-F47.front: Why must you never shift gears while crossing railroad rails—and how do manual drivers prepare?
sec07-card-sec07-F47.expected_back: Never change gears while on the tracks, because that can stall the car; with a manual transmission, shift down before you cross.

sec07-card-sec07-F48.front: When can a train appear, and what rule applies in bumper-to-bumper traffic at a crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F48.expected_back: Expect a train on any track at any hour, and in heavy traffic do not start across until you know you can clear the crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F49.front: Right after a caboose or last railcar clears the crossing, what hidden ambush must you wait to rule out?
sec07-card-sec07-F49.expected_back: After the last car of a train passes, wait until you are sure no second train is coming on another track, especially from the opposite direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F50.front: May you ever weave around lowered crossing gates or try to beat an oncoming train?
sec07-card-sec07-F50.expected_back: Driving around lowered gates is against the law, so stay put until they rise, and never race a train to the crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F51.front: How should you adjust when following a bus or hazmat tanker toward railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F51.expected_back: Be ready to stop when you follow buses or trucks that are required to stop at crossings.

sec07-card-sec07-F53.front: How do yearly railroad-crossing deaths compare with aviation crashes, and what share occur at active-warning crossings?
sec07-card-sec07-F53.expected_back: Crossing crashes kill more people in the United States each year than all aviation crashes together, and nearly fifty percent of train-vehicle collisions happen at crossings with active warning devices.

sec07-card-sec07-F54.front: Is walking or playing on railroad tracks, trestles, or rail yards legal—and where may you cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F54.expected_back: Walking or playing on tracks, trestles, rail yards or equipment is illegal, and you should cross tracks only at designated crossings.

sec07-card-sec07-F55.front: What two immediate steps come in order if your car stalls directly on railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F55.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on a crossing, get everyone out right away and clear of the tracks, then call local law enforcement for help.

sec07-card-sec07-F56.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, how far—in miles and football fields—does a freight train need to stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F56.expected_back: Trains cannot stop quickly: a freight train going fifty-five miles per hour needs a mile or more, about the length of eighteen football fields.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Which four groups of people using the roadway are bound by Alabama traffic laws?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Traffic laws cover everyone on the road: drivers, motorcycle and bicycle riders, and pedestrians.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Why does the manual advise every driver to review the handbook again every few years?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: The Legislature changes traffic laws from time to time, so every driver should restudy the manual every few years.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What is the primary crash danger of high speed according to the manual?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Speed often turns a minor mishap into a fatal one; its main danger is making collisions more severe rather than more frequent.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What four live conditions limit your legal pace under Alabama's basic speed law?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Alabama's basic speed law says never drive faster than is reasonable for current road, weather, vehicle and personal conditions.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What legal weight does exceeding a speed limit carry, and how strict is every municipal limit?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.memory_hook: Over limit risks arrest, city maximum
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Going faster than a speed limit is prima facie evidence of unlawful speed and can get you arrested, and every limit inside a municipality is a maximum.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: When do Alabama's unposted statutory speed limits govern a stretch of road?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Statutory limits apply unless a different speed zone has been set and posted on official regulatory signs.
