sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Unless posted otherwise, what are Alabama's statutory limits for urban districts, unpaved roads, and county paved roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.memory_hook: Thirty urban, thirty-five dirt, forty-five county
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Statutory limits are thirty miles per hour in an urban district, thirty-five on an unpaved road, and forty-five on a county paved road unless posted.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What default highway limit applies elsewhere in Alabama, and what two higher speeds apply where posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Elsewhere the statutory limit is fifty-five miles per hour, with sixty-five where posted and seventy where posted on an interstate.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What two rules forbid creeping too slowly in normal conditions or where a minimum speed is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.memory_hook: Match posted minimums, never block flow
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Where a minimum speed is posted, going slower is unlawful in normal conditions, and you must never drive so slowly that you hold up traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Near which crossings, roadside warnings, and sightline blockers must you drop your speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.memory_hook: Ease off near crossings, flares, crests
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Slow down near street, highway and railroad crossings, near flags, flares or fuses on the road, and approaching hill crests and curves.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: In what three-step order do you pick your exact stopping point at a STOP sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: At a STOP sign, stop at the marked line; with no line, before the near crosswalk; with neither, at the point nearest the cross street where you can see traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: When might obeying a STOP sign require stopping a second time before pulling out?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.memory_hook: Stop twice when view stays blocked
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: A second stop may be needed when something blocked your view at the first one and cross traffic is coming.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Where must you come to a full stop when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or building?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Coming out of an alley, private driveway or building in a business or residence district, always stop before the sidewalk or crosswalk area.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What must you do when a school patrol member extends a patrol flag in the STOP position?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: You must stop when a school patrol member holds an official flag in the STOP position.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: What is the standard rule at a steady red light, and when may you turn right on red?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.memory_hook: Stop first, right from proper lane
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: At a red light, wait for green and a clear way, though you may turn right after stopping if you are in the proper lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Under what exact street layout may you turn left on red after coming to a full stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: A left turn on red after stopping is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street whose traffic moves right to left.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Whom must every turn on red yield to, and what sign cancels the privilege altogether?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.memory_hook: Yield to all, obey prohibition signs
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Any turn on red must yield to traffic and pedestrians lawfully in the intersection and is not allowed where a sign prohibits it.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: How must drivers treat an intersection when the traffic signal goes completely dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Treat an intersection with a dead traffic light as a four-way stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Which roadside sign carries the exact same legal meaning as a flashing red signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: A flashing red signal means the same as a STOP sign.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Which rail crossings, bridges, and human traffic directors also require an immediate stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: You must also stop at railroad crossings posted with STOP signs or when a flagman or device there directs, at bridges opening for boats, and when a construction flagman or police officer orders it.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches from ahead or behind with siren and lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and siren, ahead or behind, pull to the curb or roadside and stop completely.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: How long must oncoming and following drivers stay stopped for a school or church bus with red lights and stop arm?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.memory_hook: Hold until arm folds, lights off
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Following or meeting a stopped school or church bus with its stop arm out and red lights flashing, stop and stay stopped until the arm folds and lights go off.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: Does the school-bus stop rule still bind oncoming traffic on an undivided four-to-six-lane highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: That stop also applies on a four to six lane undivided highway.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: In what two highway or loading-zone setups may oncoming traffic keep moving past a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: No stop is needed on a divided highway of four or more lanes when the bus is in the opposing roadway, or in a roadside loading zone where pedestrians may not cross.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What message do flashing amber lights atop a school bus send to nearby drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Flashing amber lights on a school bus are a pre-warning that it is about to stop to load or unload children.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: How far ahead of a stop do amber school-bus lights start flashing on rural roads versus city streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.memory_hook: Three hundred rural, one hundred city
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: The amber lights come on at least three hundred feet before the stop in rural areas and at least one hundred feet before it in municipalities.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: When red bus lights flash and the stop arm swings out, how far away must drivers stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.memory_hook: Stop at least twenty feet away
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Red flashing lights with the stop arm out mean the bus is loading or unloading, and drivers from either direction stop at least twenty feet from it.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does your legal duty change when school-bus lights shift from flashing amber to red with the arm out?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.memory_hook: Amber prepare, red stop twenty feet
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Amber bus lights mean get ready, with red lights and stop arm meaning stop at least twenty feet away.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What crash pattern stems from breaking right-of-way laws, and what two principles anchor those rules?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Breaking right-of-way rules is one of the main causes of crashes; the rules rest on courtesy and common sense.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: When two cars on crossing streets reach an uncontrolled intersection together, who yields?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: When two vehicles from different roads reach an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: What happens to your right-of-way if you approach an uncontrolled intersection at an unlawful speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Entering an uncontrolled intersection at an unlawful speed forfeits any right of way you would have had.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection, what sequence must you follow?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.memory_hook: Clear intersection first, then pull over
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle, pull over and stop whether it is overtaking or meeting you, but clear an intersection first, and wait until it passes.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: What two visual cues identify a blind pedestrian for whom you must stop at any intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.memory_hook: Guide dog or red-tipped white cane
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: At any intersection you must stop for a blind person using a guide dog or holding out a red-tipped white cane.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: What must a driver entering from a private road or driveway do before joining a public street?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.memory_hook: Stop first, yield to road traffic
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: A car coming from a private road or driveway must stop and yield to traffic on the public road.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: What two actions are required when approaching a YIELD sign facing your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: At a YIELD sign facing you, slow down and stop if needed for vehicles and pedestrians lawfully crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: When turning left across oncoming lanes, which approaching vehicles get the right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: Turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: Even when entering on a green arrow, whom must a turning driver still yield to?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: Drivers entering on a green arrow still yield to traffic lawfully using the intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: Which two crash types from careless passing cause heavy fatalities on two-lane highways?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: Head-on and sideswipe crashes on two-lane highways, mostly from careless passing, cause many deaths and serious injuries.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: Even outside marked no-passing zones, which lighting and surface conditions demand extreme passing caution?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: Beyond the marked no-passing areas, use extreme care everywhere in darkness, poor visibility, and on roads slick from rain, snow or ice.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: On a two-way, two-lane road, may you exceed the speed limit briefly to finish passing on the left?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: On a two-way, two-lane road you may pass on the left only if you can finish safely without exceeding the speed limit.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: What checks and driver alerts belong right before pulling out to pass ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.memory_hook: Scan ahead behind, tap or flick
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: Before passing, check far enough ahead and behind for drivers about to pass you, and alert the driver ahead with a horn tap, or a headlight flick at night.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.front: Which signals frame a pass, and what mirror sight tells you it is safe to pull back right?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.memory_hook: Whole front bumper in inside mirror
sec10-card-sec10-F41.expected_back: Signal left before passing and right before moving back, returning only when the passed car's whole front shows in your inside mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.front: What two rules apply to you while another driver is overtaking and passing your vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.expected_back: When someone is passing you, keep to your lane and do not speed up.

sec10-card-sec10-F43.front: On which two roadway layouts does Alabama allow passing another vehicle on the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F43.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed on one-way roads and on roads marked for two or more lanes going the same way.

sec10-card-sec10-F44.front: When, if ever, may a driver leave the pavement onto the shoulder to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F44.memory_hook: Never pass on shoulder except crisis
sec10-card-sec10-F44.expected_back: Using the shoulder to pass is unlawful except in an emergency or when traffic authorities direct it.

sec10-card-sec10-F45.front: Why must you never trust a front car's turn signal alone as permission to pass on the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F45.memory_hook: Blinker never guarantees safe right pass
sec10-card-sec10-F45.expected_back: A signal alone gives no right to pass on the right; check both ways and watch the car closely, since some states forbid the move.

sec10-card-sec10-F46.front: How many clear feet of sight distance are required to cross the centerline and pass on a hill or curve?
sec10-card-sec10-F46.expected_back: Do not cross the center line to pass on a curve or hill unless you can see a clear passing distance of at least five hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F47.front: At which four locations or yellow-line markings is crossing the centerline to pass outlawed?
sec10-card-sec10-F47.expected_back: Do not cross the center line to pass at a highway intersection, when meeting oncoming traffic, where signs forbid it, or with a solid yellow line on your side; double solid yellow bars both directions.

sec10-card-sec10-F48.front: Around which roadside spots and lighting conditions must you scan hardest for pedestrians?
sec10-card-sec10-F48.expected_back: Watch hardest for pedestrians near parked cars, in darkness, near schools and play areas, and near churches, mailboxes and bus stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F49.front: What four duties do drivers owe school children, blind pedestrians, crosswalks, and school buses?
sec10-card-sec10-F49.expected_back: Drivers must stop for school children and safety patrols, yield to blind walkers, keep crosswalks clear while waiting, and stop for a bus with its stop arm out.

sec10-card-sec10-F50.front: Who must yield when a pedestrian crosses the roadway outside a crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F50.expected_back: Pedestrians crossing anywhere other than a crosswalk must yield to all vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F51.front: When walking along a road without sidewalks, how should pedestrians position themselves and dress at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F51.memory_hook: Far left single file, bright gear
sec10-card-sec10-F51.expected_back: Walkers on a roadway keep far left in single file, carry a light or wear light or reflective clothing at night, and make eye contact with drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-F52.front: How far back must ordinary drivers stay behind an emergency vehicle on a run?
sec10-card-sec10-F52.expected_back: Only vehicles on necessary official business may follow within five hundred feet of an emergency vehicle on a run.

sec10-card-sec10-F53.front: When is driving across an unprotected fire hose stretched over the street allowed?
sec10-card-sec10-F53.expected_back: Never drive over an unprotected fire hose unless a police officer or fire official authorizes it.

sec10-card-sec10-F54.front: What check comes before entering to back up, and where must you look instead of trusting mirrors?
sec10-card-sec10-F54.expected_back: Before backing, walk around the car, then look front, sides and rear and keep looking over your right shoulder, not trusting the mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-F55.front: Who is the sole exception to the ban on backing up along freeways and expressways?
sec10-card-sec10-F55.expected_back: Backing is banned on freeways and expressways except for emergency vehicles on duty.

sec10-card-sec10-F56.front: Into which lane must you steer when backing out of a driveway onto a street?
sec10-card-sec10-F56.expected_back: Back out of a driveway only into the nearest lane, never across other lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F78.front: When is backing on a public street advisable, and what rule covers backing out of angle parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F78.expected_back: Aside from backing into a parking space, backing on a public street or road is never advisable, and drivers should follow the same backing rules when pulling out from angle parking into traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F57.front: Under what condition is driving along the highway shoulder lawful in Alabama?
sec10-card-sec10-F57.expected_back: Driving on the shoulder is unlawful except in emergency conditions.

sec10-card-sec10-F58.front: What does Alabama law say about signs, posters, or materials placed on vehicle windows?
sec10-card-sec10-F58.expected_back: State law bars any sign, poster or other material that obstructs a vehicle window.

sec10-card-sec10-F59.front: What checks come before changing lanes, and does flicking your turn signal grant right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F59.expected_back: Before changing lanes, check clearance beside, ahead and behind, and glance over your shoulder at the blind spot; a signal does not give you the right to move.

sec10-card-sec10-F60.front: How do you position your left arm for stop or slow, left turn, and right turn hand signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F60.memory_hook: Down slow, straight left, up right
sec10-card-sec10-F60.expected_back: Hand signals: arm down to stop or slow, arm straight out for a left turn, arm up for a right turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F79.front: Who suffers injury most often when drivers make improper turns at intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F79.expected_back: Improper turns cause many crashes, and the pedestrian at an intersection is often the one hurt.

sec10-card-sec10-F61.front: When do cargo or front-seat passengers make operating a vehicle unlawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F61.expected_back: It is unlawful to drive with a load, or more than three people in the front seat, that blocks the driver's view or control.

sec10-card-sec10-F62.front: What is the maximum combined or end overhang a load may extend past the front and rear?
sec10-card-sec10-F62.expected_back: A load may stick out no more than five feet beyond the front and rear of the vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F63.front: Once a rear load projects four feet or more, what daytime and nighttime warnings are required?
sec10-card-sec10-F63.memory_hook: Twelve-inch red flag, red tail lamp
sec10-card-sec10-F63.expected_back: A load reaching four feet or more past the rear needs a red flag at least twelve inches square by day and a red light visible for two hundred feet at night.

sec10-card-sec10-F64.front: What four actions should you take right away when police lights signal you to pull over?
sec10-card-sec10-F64.memory_hook: Signal off, kill engine, stay inside
sec10-card-sec10-F64.expected_back: When stopped by police, signal and pull off safely, turn off the engine and radio, and stay inside unless told to get out.

sec10-card-sec10-F65.front: Where should hands, devices, and cabin lights be for you and passengers during a police stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F65.memory_hook: Hands visible, devices down, dome on
sec10-card-sec10-F65.expected_back: Keep both hands on the wheel, ask passengers to stay calm with hands visible, put devices down, and turn on interior lights at night.

sec10-card-sec10-F66.front: What must you disclose at first contact with an officer, and when should you reach for documents?
sec10-card-sec10-F66.memory_hook: Disclose weapons first, wait before reaching
sec10-card-sec10-F66.expected_back: Tell the officer at first contact about any weapons, and do not reach for your license or papers until told to.

sec10-card-sec10-F80.front: What should you do before stretching for a license, registration, or insurance card stored out of reach?
sec10-card-sec10-F80.expected_back: If your license, insurance proof or registration is out of reach, tell the officer before you reach for it.

sec10-card-sec10-F67.front: What identification applies when an officer not wearing a uniform conducts a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F67.expected_back: An officer out of uniform will show credentials, and you may ask to see them.

sec10-card-sec10-F68.front: What does signing a traffic ticket mean legally, and where should you dispute it?
sec10-card-sec10-F68.memory_hook: Signature promises appearance, contest in court
sec10-card-sec10-F68.expected_back: Signing a citation does not admit guilt, but refusing one may get you arrested; contest it in court instead of arguing.

sec10-card-sec10-F69.front: If you believe an officer acted improperly during a stop, what details should you note and where do they go?
sec10-card-sec10-F69.memory_hook: Log time, place, report to agency
sec10-card-sec10-F69.expected_back: If you think an officer acted wrongly, record the time, date, place and details and report it promptly to the officer's agency.

sec10-card-sec10-F70.front: Which three documents must a driver have ready to present during a traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F70.expected_back: At a traffic stop you need your driver license, proof of insurance and vehicle registration.

sec10-card-sec10-F71.front: Which two vehicle actions are barred without coverage under Alabama's Mandatory Liability Insurance Law?
sec10-card-sec10-F71.expected_back: Alabama's Mandatory Liability Insurance Law bars operating or registering a road vehicle without liability insurance.

sec10-card-sec10-F72.front: What three dollar minimums make up Alabama's required liability insurance coverage?
sec10-card-sec10-F72.expected_back: Minimum coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars for one person's injury or death, fifty thousand dollars for two or more, and twenty-five thousand dollars for property damage.

sec10-card-sec10-F73.front: What maximum fines and license suspension can follow first and repeat liability insurance violations?
sec10-card-sec10-F73.memory_hook: Five hundred first, thousand repeat, suspension
sec10-card-sec10-F73.expected_back: An insurance violation can bring a fine up to five hundred dollars the first time, up to one thousand dollars after that, and or or a six month suspension.

sec10-card-sec10-F74.front: How many inches at the top of a vehicle's windshield may carry window tint in Alabama?
sec10-card-sec10-F74.expected_back: On every vehicle only the top six inches of the windshield may be tinted.

sec10-card-sec10-F75.front: How much light must pass through car side and rear tint, and which windows follow that rule on SUVs or trucks?
sec10-card-sec10-F75.memory_hook: Thirty-two percent cars, front SUV sides
sec10-card-sec10-F75.expected_back: Passenger car side and rear windows need tint passing at least thirty-two percent of light; SUVs, trucks, vans and RVs follow that only for front side windows.

sec10-card-sec10-F81.front: On SUVs, pickup trucks, vans, and RVs, which windows may carry darker tint than thirty-two percent?
sec10-card-sec10-F81.expected_back: On SUVs, trucks, vans and RVs, darker tint is allowed on windows behind the driver.

sec10-card-sec10-F76.front: On a road with four or more lanes, what must you do for a stopped emergency unit or amber-lit wrecker?
sec10-card-sec10-F76.expected_back: On roads of four or more lanes, leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a wrecker with amber lights.

sec10-card-sec10-F77.front: How much must you slow when blocked from moving over, and what speed rules apply on two-lane roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F77.memory_hook: Fifteen under, or ten in twenty
sec10-card-sec10-F77.expected_back: If you cannot move over, slow to at least fifteen miles per hour under the limit; on two lanes, move away within your lane and slow fifteen under when the limit is twenty-five or more, or go ten where it is twenty or less.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Under Alabama's move-over law, when is slowing down allowed instead of changing lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.memory_hook: Move over first, slow when blocked
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Move-over means leave the adjacent lane on four or more lanes, but only slow down when you cannot change lanes or are on two lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: At what birthday do Alabama's graduated driver license rules stop applying completely?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Alabama's graduated driver license rules do not apply to anyone eighteen years of age or older.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: How long must a seventeen-year-old hold a valid license to step outside the graduated rules?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: They also do not apply to a seventeen-year-old or older driver who has held a valid license for six months or more.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: Which two family or household statuses exempt a driver aged sixteen or older from graduated rules?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: A person sixteen or older who is married or is the head of a household is exempt from the graduated rules.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Do Alabama's graduated license rules cover a teen legally relieved of minority status?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Someone who has been legally relieved of minority status is also outside the graduated rules.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How does qualifying for a graduated-license exemption at seventeen differ from turning eighteen?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: A seventeen-year-old is free of the graduated rules only after holding a valid license for six months, while anyone eighteen or older is exempt outright.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Which two groups of young licensed drivers remain under Alabama's graduated license restrictions?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: The license restrictions apply to drivers who are sixteen, and to seventeen-year-olds who have held a license for less than six months.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: What age, learner-hold time, and compliance record must someone under eighteen meet before applying for an unrestricted license?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: A person under eighteen cannot apply for an unrestricted license until holding a learner license for at least six months with no restriction violations, and must be seventeen.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: Which four categories of adults sitting right beside a fifteen-year-old learner satisfy the supervision rule?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: A fifteen-year-old holding a valid learner license may drive only when a parent, legal guardian, licensed driver aged twenty-one or older, or licensed or certified driving instructor occupies the front seat beside the driver.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Does a licensed or certified driving instructor in the front passenger seat qualify to supervise a fifteen-year-old learner?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: A licensed or certified driving instructor sitting in the front seat beside the fifteen-year-old also satisfies the supervision rule.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: For what two milestones does a sixteen-year-old need permission from a parent or legal guardian?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: A sixteen-year-old needs a parent's or legal guardian's permission both to get a license and to drive without supervision.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How does front-seat supervision for a fifteen-year-old learner contrast with passenger rules for a restricted sixteen-year-old?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: A fifteen-year-old learner must have a parent, legal guardian, licensed driver aged twenty-one or older, or licensed or certified driving instructor in the front seat next to the driver, whereas a restricted sixteen-year-old or seventeen-year-old licensed less than six months may carry at most one nonfamily passenger besides a parent, guardian, or supervising licensed driver twenty-one or older.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Without a supervising adult along, how many nonfamily passengers may a restricted teen carry?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: A restricted driver may carry no more than one nonfamily passenger besides the parent, guardian or supervising licensed driver aged at least twenty-one, a limit cut from four in two thousand ten.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: During which overnight hours is a restricted teen barred from driving without a parent, guardian, or exception?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: A restricted driver may not drive between twelve midnight and six a.m. unless a parent or legal guardian is along or an exception applies.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: Which accompanying adults, scheduled trips, or emergencies allow a restricted teen to drive between midnight and six in the morning?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: A restricted young driver may not operate a vehicle from midnight to six a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, riding with a licensed driver twenty-one or older with parental consent, traveling to or from regular work or a school- or religious-sponsored event, or driving for a medical, fire, or law-enforcement emergency.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: Which three routine destinations let a restricted driver commute solo during overnight curfew hours?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Late-night driving is also allowed when going to or from the driver's regular workplace, a school-sponsored event or a religious-sponsored event.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What communication device rule binds restricted drivers, and what two consequences can follow breaking it?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: The restrictions also bar driving while using any handheld communication device, and violating that rule extends the graduated period and or or suspends the license.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: When riding overnight with a licensed adult twenty-one or older who is not your parent, what extra condition applies?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Driving between twelve midnight and six a.m. is allowed with a parent or guardian, while riding with another adult licensee twenty-one or older also needs parental consent.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: How does Alabama classify breaking a graduated-license condition regarding criminal records and court costs?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Breaking a graduated-license condition is a traffic violation but carries no criminal penalty or court costs.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: When may an officer issue a citation for breaking a graduated driver license restriction?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: A citation for a graduated-license violation is issued only when the driver is stopped and cited for a separate violation of the law.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: How many driver-record points are added for violating a graduated license restriction?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: No points go on the record for violating the graduated-license restrictions.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: Can an officer write a standalone graduated-license ticket without citing another offense?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: A GDL citation is never written on its own; the officer must first stop and cite the driver for a separate violation.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: How long does breaking any graduated restriction extend a teen's restricted period?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Any restriction violation extends the restricted period by six months or until the driver turns eighteen.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: Even with zero points and no criminal fine, what penalty still hits after a restriction violation?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: A restriction violation adds no points and brings no criminal penalty, yet it still extends the restricted period by six months or until eighteen.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: Which moving-violation count or single-offense point value triggers an automatic sixty-day restricted suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: A restricted driver's license is automatically suspended for sixty days after a second moving violation conviction or any conviction worth four or more points.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: Which six dangerous-driving or hit-and-run convictions also trigger the automatic sixty-day suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: The same sixty-day suspension follows a conviction for failing to give information or render aid, racing, fleeing or eluding an officer, reckless driving, illegal passing or driving on the wrong side.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: How does the penalty for breaking a teen restriction differ from a second moving or four-point conviction?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Breaking a restriction extends the graduated period, but a second moving violation or a four-point offense brings an automatic sixty-day suspension.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: According to crash records, what share of highway wrecks trace back to the driver and which human failures cause them?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: According to crash records, more than ninety percent of highway crashes trace back to the driver: error, missing knowledge, inattention, physical or mental condition, a poor attitude or faulty judgment.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Once you master basic car handling, what else must you keep learning to become a truly good driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Basic skills are not enough to make a good driver; after mastering them you must keep learning the finer points of driving and the physical and mental conditions that affect it.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: How do personal worries, family quarrels, illness at home, fear, or overconfidence affect your crash risk?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Family troubles, quarrels, money worries, a serious illness at home, personal fears or overconfidence can make you temporarily accident-prone, because a preoccupied mind cannot stay alert enough to drive safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What should someone do before driving right after a heated argument or while angry or grieving?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Someone who has just had a violent argument, or who is angry or grieving, needs time to cool off before driving, since venting emotions behind the wheel is very poor judgment.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What does the manual recommend whenever you feel ill, worried, nervous, frightened, angry, or depressed?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: When you feel worried, ill, nervous, frightened, angry or depressed, the manual's advice is to let another person drive.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What term does the manual use for sharing the roadway fairly and seeing traffic from every user's viewpoint?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: A well-adjusted driver understands that traffic means sharing the road fairly and acts from the point of view of every road user, which the manual calls social responsibility.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What personal trait do sound driving attitudes and actions reflect, and which age groups need it?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Good driving attitudes and sound actions show mental and emotional maturity, and that maturity matters for younger and older drivers alike.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Because concentration is vital to safe driving, which four casual habits have zero place behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Concentration is among the most important parts of safe driving, so the driver's seat is no place for daydreaming, window shopping, sightseeing or distracting talk.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Why does the manual call driving a full-time job, and what breaks down first when focus slips?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Driving is a full-time job, and poor concentration dulls your observation enough to cause crashes that could have been avoided.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Even when you legally use a cell phone in the car, what remains your number-one duty?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: If you use a cell phone while driving, your first responsibility is still driving the vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What two checks or habits help before placing a phone call from the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Before making a call, size up the traffic, and know your keypad well enough to use speed dial where you can.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Which practical steps make placing or taking phone calls safer in a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Make calls while stopped or let a passenger place them, keep the phone within easy reach, and use a speaker phone or hands-free device.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which conversation types and road conditions call for avoiding phone talk or pulling off the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Steer clear of intense, emotional or complicated calls, avoid phone talk in heavy traffic or bad weather, and pull off the road to dial or finish a conversation.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Which wireless messaging actions are outlawed while operating a motor vehicle in Alabama?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: While operating a motor vehicle in Alabama, you may not use a wireless device to write, send or read texts, instant messages or e-mail.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What dollar fines does the manual list for first, second, and third or later texting convictions?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: The manual lists texting fines of twenty-five dollars for a first offense, fifty dollars for a second and seventy-five dollars for a third or later offense.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Besides the cash fine, how many violation points does a texting conviction add to your driving record?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Every texting offense also adds a two-point violation to the offender's driving record.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Across repeat Alabama texting tickets, how does the fine progression differ from the driver-record point penalty?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: The texting fines climb from twenty-five dollars to fifty dollars to seventy-five dollars, but the record penalty stays the same two points for every offense.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What should you do the moment drowsiness hits behind the wheel instead of trying to push through?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Stop driving as soon as you feel drowsy instead of fighting it, and leave the highway at the first rest stop or service area.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: How does the manual separate a short fix for mild tiredness from what a truly sleepy driver must do?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Coffee and some stretching may revive a driver who is only getting tired, but a driver who is truly sleepy should get off the highway and nap.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Why does the manual warn interstate drivers away from taking stay-awake drugs?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Drowsiness is one of the biggest dangers of interstate driving, and stay-awake drugs are likely to make your driving more dangerous, not less.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: By distance or by clock time, how often should you stop to walk and stretch on long trips?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Take a regular break every one hundred miles or every two hours, getting out of the car to walk, stretch and relax.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: What simple rest habit does the manual suggest before setting out on a long drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Before a long trip it is a good idea to take a nap.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What is highway hypnosis, and which steady road sounds help trigger it on expressways?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Highway hypnosis is drowsiness or unawareness caused by monotony, such as wind noise, tire sound on the pavement and the steady hum of the engine, and expressway drivers are prone to it.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Which active eye habits keep highway hypnosis from setting in on open roads?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: To fight highway hypnosis, keep moving your eyes across the road and focus on objects near and far, left and right; reading highway signs can also keep you alert.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Putting the fatigue rules together, when does coffee help, when must you nap, and when do stay-awake drugs fit?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A tired driver may get by with coffee and stretching, but a truly sleepy driver must leave the highway and nap, and drugs to stay awake are never the answer.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Which physical factors or substances can degrade driving ability enough to cause or contribute to crashes?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Your physical condition strongly affects driving ability, and alcohol, drugs, illness or disability can cause or contribute to crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does research show most drivers are already impaired?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Drinking by drivers is a major contributing factor in traffic crashes, and research shows a blood alcohol concentration of point zero five percent already impairs most people's driving to some degree.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: At what blood alcohol concentration is every single driver definitely impaired without exception?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Impairment grows as blood alcohol concentration rises, and at point zero eight percent every person is definitely impaired.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: Roughly what share of fatal traffic crashes each year involve drivers who have been drinking?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: The manual reports that drinking drivers are involved in roughly fifty percent of fatal crashes each year.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: How does one bottle of beer compare in alcohol content and driver impact to a shot of whiskey or glass of wine?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: The manual says one bottle of beer holds about as much alcohol as an average shot of whiskey or a glass of wine, with the same effect on the average driver.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Is alcohol a stimulant or a depressant, and what does it do to vision, reflexes, and judgment?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Alcohol is a depressant rather than a stimulant, bringing drowsiness, blurred vision and slower reflexes and weakening judgment and coordination.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: Must your blood alcohol reach unlawful intoxication before your driving ability becomes impaired?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: A driver can be impaired before reaching the point of legal intoxication.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How does the point-zero-five research benchmark compare with Alabama's point-zero-eight adult unlawful threshold?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Research puts the start of impairment for most drivers at point zero five percent, below the point zero eight percent level that makes driving unlawful.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: Why do some drinkers feel energized or revved up when alcohol is actually a depressant?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: People who feel stimulated after drinking are really experiencing lowered inhibitions, which strip away caution and self-control.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: Does choosing beer, wine, or whiskey change impairment, or what single factor actually matters?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: Beer, wine or whiskey makes no difference; what counts is how much alcohol reaches the blood.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.front: Why can the exact same drink hit you harder one day than another, especially around meals?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.expected_back: Alcohol can hit you differently from one time to the next, and a small amount affects you more on an empty stomach than after eating.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.front: Why do black coffee, food, and cold showers fail to make an impaired drinker sober?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.expected_back: Black coffee, food or a cold shower may wake you but will not sober you, because the liver must break alcohol down over time before the body eliminates it.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.front: Which seven driving abilities and mental safeguards does the manual say alcohol damages or destroys?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.expected_back: The manual's reasons not to drink and drive are that alcohol dulls judgment, slows reflexes, impairs vision, harms coordination, removes inhibitions, breeds overconfidence and prevents concentration.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Under Alabama law, what general blood alcohol concentration or condition makes driving unlawful?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Under Alabama law it is unlawful to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of point zero eight percent or more, or while under the influence of alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Besides driving drunk, what does state law ban regarding drugs, mixed substances, and physical control of a car?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: State law forbids driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or of a drug or an alcohol-drug combination that leaves you unable to drive safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: What blood alcohol concentration makes driving unlawful for commercial vehicle operators in Alabama?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: For commercial vehicle operators the unlawful blood alcohol level is point zero four percent or more.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: At what blood alcohol concentration is driving unlawful for anyone under age twenty-one in Alabama?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: For persons under twenty-one years of age the unlawful blood alcohol level is point zero two percent or more.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: Which strict blood alcohol concentration cutoff applies to school bus and daycare vehicle drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: For school bus and daycare drivers the unlawful blood alcohol level is also point zero two percent or more.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How do Alabama's unlawful alcohol cutoffs compare across general adults, commercial drivers, under-twenty-one drivers, and school-bus or daycare drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.memory_hook: Zero-eight adult, zero-four rig, zero-two youth
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The general limit is point zero eight percent, but commercial operators are held to point zero four percent and drivers under twenty-one and school bus or daycare drivers to point zero two percent.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: Simply by driving on Alabama public highways, which three chemical tests have you already agreed to take?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: Under the implied consent law, anyone driving on Alabama's public highways is treated as having agreed to chemical testing of blood, breath or urine for alcohol content.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: What happens to your driver license if you are arrested for DUI and refuse a directed chemical breath test?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: A driver arrested for DUI who refuses an officer's direction to take a chemical breath test will have the driver license suspended.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: What fine range, maximum jail time, and license suspension hit a first Alabama DUI conviction?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: For a first DUI conviction the penalty is a six hundred dollars to two thousand one hundred dollars fine, a jail term of up to one year, or both, and the license is suspended for ninety days.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: What fines, mandatory jail or community service, and license penalty follow a second DUI within ten years?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: A second conviction within ten years brings a one thousand one hundred dollars to five thousand one hundred dollars fine, up to one year in jail or both, a mandatory forty-eight hours in jail or twenty days of community service, and a one-year license revocation.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: What fine range, license revocation length, and non-suspendable minimum jail time hit a third DUI conviction?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: A third conviction brings a two thousand one hundred dollars to ten thousand one hundred dollars fine, a three-year license revocation, and up to one year in jail with a mandatory minimum of sixty days that cannot be probated or suspended.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: How is a fourth or later DUI classified, and what fines, revocation, and prison range follow?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: A fourth or later conviction is a Class C felony with fines of four thousand one hundred dollars to ten thousand one hundred dollars, a five-year revocation, and imprisonment of at least one year and one day and no more than ten years.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How does the driver-license penalty escalate from a first DUI conviction to a second within ten years?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: A first DUI conviction brings a ninety-day suspension, while a second conviction within ten years brings a one-year revocation.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How do license loss and offense grade step up from a third DUI conviction to a fourth or later?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A third conviction costs the license for three years, while a fourth or later conviction is a felony with a five-year revocation.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Regardless of legal fault in a car-motorcycle collision, who usually suffers worst and how can motorists help?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Winning a right-of-way argument means nothing when a rider has zero steel cage around them on impact.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: What does the term No-Zones mean around large trucks and buses?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Hovering next to a trailer feels harmless until you realize your entire sedan vanishes from cab mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What visual check tells you immediately whether a truck or bus driver can spot your car beside them?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Big-rig side blind spots swallow whole lanes on both sides, making that mirror-face check your lifeline.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Which side should you use to pass a truck or bus, and how should you pace the pass?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Lingering alongside eighteen-wheelers keeps you trapped beside giant tires and hidden inside the cab's right or left blind zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: How far back can a truck or bus rear No-Zone stretch, and why is tailgating there a triple trap?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Riding a trailer bumper blinds both you and the trucker while stripping away every escape path during hard braking.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Why must you switch to low beams whenever you trail a large truck or bus after dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Oversized West Coast mirrors catch high-beam glare and bounce blinding light straight into the trucker's eyes.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How does your strategy for clearing side No-Zones differ from avoiding the two-hundred-foot rear No-Zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Each blind zone demands its own counterplay so you never linger beside trailers or camp behind tailgates.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: After overtaking a large vehicle, what must appear in your rearview mirror before you merge back over?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Slicing in right off a rig's front bumper steals the heavy truck's braking cushion and forces panic stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Roughly how much stopping distance do trucks and buses require compared with passenger cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Massive cargo weight builds momentum that air brakes simply cannot scrub off in passenger-car distances.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, how many feet did the cited safety study find a loaded truck needs versus a car?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Exam questions test both exact numbers to prove a highway-speed rig travels more than two extra football-field-widths stopping.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How do the fifty-five-mile-per-hour stopping numbers connect to the general rule on truck braking space?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Needing well over twice a sedan's stopping footage explains why cutting inside a rig's front buffer turns deadly.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Why should you never slip behind a truck or bus while it is backing up?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Box trailers block every rear sightline completely, so a reversing driver has zero chance of spotting your car.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Why do large trucks and buses often swing left before making a right-hand corner?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Long trailers track tighter than cab wheels, and drivers misread that left swing as a lane change opening.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: What must you avoid doing whenever a large vehicle ahead has its right turn signal flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Ducking into that tempting right-side gap wedges your car between trailer axles and the concrete curb.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What separates the front No-Zone mistake from the turning No-Zone mistake around large trucks?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: One cuts off forward braking space after overtaking, while the other traps impatient drivers beside turning trailers.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What must you do with any vehicle left standing beside a rural highway, or if it cannot move?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: High-speed country traffic crests hills expecting clear lanes, so a dark stalled car on pavement triggers rear-end wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Which brake and gear steps apply every single time you park on a slope?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Relying on transmission pins or cables alone risks a runaway roll if either mechanical link slips.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Facing downhill next to a curb, which way do your front wheels point and what gear holds the car?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Angling tires into the concrete curb blocks the nose immediately instead of letting gravity pull you into traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Facing uphill next to a curb, how should you angle your front tires and set the transmission?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Turning left lets the back of the right front tire catch smoothly against the curb if brakes slip.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: When parking uphill or downhill where there is no curb at all, which direction do your wheels turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Without concrete to catch a tire, steering toward the shoulder guides any runaway car away from travel lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: At a curb, how do wheel angle and manual gear choice flip between downhill and uphill parking?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Test questions swap uphill away and downhill toward constantly, so pair uphill-curb-away as your single exception.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Which three pedestrian and traffic surfaces are off-limits for parking at all times?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Leaving a vehicle on pedestrian paths forces walkers and wheelchair users out into live moving lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Within how many feet of a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection is parking prohibited?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Cars parked right up to unmarked corner crossings hide stepping pedestrians from approaching drivers until too late.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: How many feet of clear space must you leave before a roadside stop sign, flashing beacon, or traffic signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Tall SUVs or vans parked close to corner posts block approaching drivers from spotting stop signs early.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: Within what distance of the nearest railroad track rail is parking outlawed?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Parked cars near grade crossings block sightlines down the tracks and trap queued cars near oncoming trains.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park in Alabama?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Fire crews need unobstructed curb access so thick high-pressure supply hoses never kink during emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Besides corners and crossings, which three access points or roadway structures forbid parking?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Bridges and tunnels have zero shoulder width, turning any parked car into an instant bottleneck hazard.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What counts as double parking, and does Alabama law allow it even briefly?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Stopping in the live travel lane next to parked cars chokes traffic flow and forces risky swerves.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: What do a yellow-painted curb and official no-parking signs tell a driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Cities paint curbs yellow at loading zones and tight corners where stationary cars create immediate bottlenecks.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: In ascending order, which four footage buffers govern parking near hydrants, crosswalks, roadside signals, and rails?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Memorizing those four numbers in rising order prevents mixing up hydrant, crosswalk, stop-sign, and railroad questions.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: In order, how do you line up, reverse, and finish steering into a parallel parking space?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Starting even with the forward car sets your pivot angle so you tuck cleanly parallel beside the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Who inside a vehicle must wear a restraint under Alabama's safety belt law?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: One unbuckled rider becomes a flying projectile during a rollover, injuring buckled passengers sharing the cabin.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: Where on your body should the lap portion of a seat belt sit for peak crash protection?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Letting a loose belt ride high over your soft stomach risks severe internal injuries during sudden stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Through what age must young riders be properly restrained under Alabama's child restraint statute?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Exam traps stop child-restraint coverage at elementary ages, yet Alabama's law reaches all riders through fifteen.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Which seating rows and vehicle types fall under Alabama's child restraint requirements?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Moving kids to the third row of a minivan or pickup cab never exempts them from proper restraints.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: What two consequences hit a driver who violates Alabama's child restraint law?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Unlike minor non-moving tickets, failing to buckle a child adds points directly onto the driver's record.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: Until what age or weight threshold must an infant ride in a rear-facing car seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle fragile infant necks and spines against forward crash forces far better than forward harnesses.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: After outgrowing rear-facing, until what age or weight does a child ride in a forward-facing seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Five-point harnesses spread crash forces across a toddler's shoulders and hips until their frame handles a booster.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Until a child reaches what birthday is a booster seat mandatory in Alabama?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Boosters lift smaller kids so adult shoulder and lap belts cross strong bones instead of necks and bellies.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: Once a child graduates from a booster at six, what size-appropriate restraint applies and until what age?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Graduating out of a booster simply shifts older kids into properly fitted vehicle belts through their mid-teens.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: What single habit does the manual identify as the most effective defense against serious crash injuries?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Airbags are supplemental cushions only, whereas fastened seat belts keep occupants inside the protective cabin shell.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: How does Alabama's general safety belt law pair with its specific child restraint law?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Adult belts alone fail small bodies, so state law layers staged child seats underneath universal occupant buckling.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How do the age and weight cutoffs line up across rear-facing, forward-facing, and booster stages?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Locking those three sequential thresholds together stops exam mix-ups between infant, toddler, and booster transitions.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: How quickly must a driver recognize traffic signs, lights, and markings—and how must regulatory boards be treated?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: At sixty miles per hour, hesitating two seconds to puzzle over a road rule carries you nearly two hundred feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: For what two visibility reasons do modern highway boards favor bold graphics over wordy text?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Crisp silhouettes register in a split second at interstate speeds long before small lettering sharpens.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Which two visual features of a road board are coded to its message category even before you read it?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Snow, mud, or sun glare can hide text, yet an octagon or pennant outline still tells you the rule.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Into which three functional groups does Alabama divide all traffic boards?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Every board on the highway either states a law, warns of a hazard, or guides your route.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What do regulatory boards govern, what standard colors do they use, and are they optional?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Aside from red stop, yield, or wrong-way boards, crisp black-and-white panels state enforceable traffic law.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: When vehicles reach a four-way stop one after another, which driver earns the right to proceed first?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Rolling stops do not count—order goes strictly by who came to a full halt first.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: When two or more drivers halt at a four-way stop at the exact same instant, who goes first?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Yielding to the driver on your right breaks simultaneous-arrival ties cleanly without awkward hand-waving.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Even when right-of-way is clearly yours at a four-way stop, why should you wait a few seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Plenty of impatient drivers roll through four-way stops out of turn—waiting briefly prevents low-speed T-bones.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: What speed adjustment and two right-of-way priorities does a yield board require?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Slowing early prepares you for a full stop whenever pedestrians or intersecting cars occupy your gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What critical mistake does a white-on-red wrong-way regulatory board alert you to?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Spotting white-on-red wrong-way lettering means head-on freeway traffic is coming—pull aside and turn back safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What does the regulatory board placed at the mouth of an oncoming one-way roadway forbid?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Do-not-enter posts guard exit ramps and one-way street mouths so turning drivers never enter head-on.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What approach mindset and track check does the white railroad regulatory crossbuck require?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Treating a crossbuck like a yield check ensures every set of steel rails is clear before crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: What movement is prohibited at an intersection displaying a crossed-out left-turn arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Turning left there blocks oncoming queues or enters a one-way cross street the wrong way.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Under a posted no-parking board, does staying behind the wheel make sitting there legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Drivers often think idling in the seat dodges a no-parking zone—Alabama explicitly bans parking occupied or empty.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What two conditions—person and decal—must both be met to park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Notice the rule covers both public streets and private shopping lots alike unless both conditions hold.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: For what sole reason may you pull over beside an emergency-stopping-only board?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Checking texts, swapping drivers, or reading maps on a narrow freeway shoulder invites deadly high-speed strikes.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Under what weather and road conditions does a posted speed-limit number—such as thirty—apply as the top speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Heavy rain, fog, or packed traffic lowers your safe legal ceiling below thirty even though the metal number stays.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: On which types of highways do dual maximum-and-minimum speed boards usually stand?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Crawling far below freeway pace creates closing-speed hazards nearly as dangerous as speeding.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What two ways tell you a reduced school-zone speed limit is currently in effect?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Slowing strictly during posted arrival-dismissal windows or blinking amber beacons guards children crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What must every vehicle occupying a lane marked left-lane-must-turn-left do at the upcoming corner?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Continuing straight out of a mandatory turn bay sideswipes opposing or dual-turning neighbors.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Which turning directions are off-limits when an intersection posts a no-turns board?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Through traffic keeps flowing straight ahead smoothly without waiting behind stopped turning cars.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What exact boundary along a highway does a regulatory do-not-pass board mark?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Once abreast of that white rectangular marker, finish or abort any overtake before crossing solid paint.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which red-light turns are forbidden when a no-turn-on-red board hangs at a traffic light?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Even one-way left-on-red and standard right-on-red stay completely locked until green appears.
sec08-card-sec08-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Neither right nor left on red

visual_sync.text_span: Neither right nor left on red

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: On which side must you pass a regulatory keep-right divider board?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Straying left of a median nose puts you head-on into opposing turn bays.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: How can a multi-lane regulatory panel split duties between the curb lane and the adjacent lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Drivers in the second lane may go straight or arc wide right alongside curb-lane turners.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Where are side-by-side double right turns legal in Alabama, and what applies everywhere else?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Turning right from a second lane without explicit signage cuts directly across the curb-lane car.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What travel rule does a horizontal black-and-white one-way arrow enforce?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Checking horizontal one-way arrows before turning off a two-way street prevents wrong-way turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: How do standard hazard warnings and road-construction warnings split background colors?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Spotting orange diamonds ahead warns instantly that temporary lanes, cones, and workers replace normal pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Which two high-alert foot-traffic zones use bright fluorescent yellow warning panels?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: High-visibility fluorescent pigment pops out during dawn, dusk, and rain where walkers and students cross.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What geometric outline identifies the vast majority of roadway warning boards?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Pointed-top diamond silhouettes signal upcoming road hazards long before black symbols resolve.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How do yellow, orange, and fluorescent yellow divide warning duties across Alabama roads?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Sorting those three warning palettes locks in a guaranteed color-code question on knowledge tests.
sec08-card-sec08-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Yellow general, orange work, fluorescent walkers

visual_sync.text_span: Yellow general, orange work, fluorescent walkers

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Which four bend or alignment changes do curved-arrow warning diamonds preview?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Reading arrow angles early tells you whether one gentle bend or a snake of curves lies ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: What junction geometry do perpendicular and angled stem warning diamonds show?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Watching the right shoulder for hidden farm driveways or angled county roads prevents surprise pull-outs.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What surface hazard and driver response go with a bump warning diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Hitting a sharp frost heave or speed hump fast bottoms suspension and jolts steering loose.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: What must you prepare to do when a T-intersection warning shows your road ending straight ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Missing a T-junction warning at night risks driving straight across the crossroad into a ditch.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Why must you keep all four tires on paved asphalt beside a soft-shoulder warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Muddy or sandy shoulders sink right-side tires deep and drag vehicles toward roadside ditches.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.question_text: What two tight alignment layouts do sharp-zag and double-arrow T-end diamonds warn about?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.teaching_text: Sharp ninety-degree zig-zags demand much lower entry speeds than sweeping highway curves.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.question_text: How are directional curve-arrow boards arranged along the outside of a sharp bend?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.teaching_text: Sequential arrows trace the exact arc radius at night so headlights follow the bend smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: How does a road-narrows warning differ slightly in meaning from a pavement-narrows warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Both demand tucking neatly inside your lane before shoulders or outer asphalt pinch inward.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: Which sides of an upcoming traffic island may you use after passing an island-ahead split-arrow diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Unlike a one-way median divider, a split-flow island routes same-direction traffic smoothly left or right.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: What roadway feature and speed action does a dip warning diamond call for?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Low dips scrape front bumpers at speed and often collect standing rainwater during storms.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: How wide is the span ahead when you pass a one-lane-bridge warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Only one vehicle fits across the deck at a time—yield if an oncoming truck is already entering.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How do road-narrows, pavement-narrows, and one-lane-bridge escalate from tighter room to single-file?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Keeping those three width warnings distinct stops test-takers from confusing narrowed two-lane asphalt with a one-car bridge.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: What upcoming intersection rules do stop-ahead and yield-ahead diamonds prepare you for?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Trees, hills, or curves often hide the octagon or triangle until braking distance would run short.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Do you halt right beside a stop-ahead warning diamond or farther down the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Slamming to a stop beside the yellow advance diamond shocks drivers behind you—halt at the red octagon.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.question_text: What does a small square yellow advisory-speed plaque mounted beneath a curve diamond tell you?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.teaching_text: Engineers calculate curve banking and sightlines so taking the bend at or below that number stays planted.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.question_text: What three actions belong at a railroad-crossing-ahead warning—and why does physics demand them?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.teaching_text: Heavy locomotives need a mile to stop, leaving all crash-avoidance responsibility on the approaching motorist.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.question_text: What roadside elevation hazard does a low-shoulder warning diamond highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.teaching_text: Dropping right wheels off a steep asphalt step can trigger a rollover if jerked back abruptly.

sec08-card-sec08-F46.question_text: What entering traffic must you scan for near truck-crossing and fire-station warning diamonds?
sec08-card-sec08-F46.teaching_text: Loaded log trucks accelerate slowly while responding fire engines pull out urgently with lights and sirens.

sec08-card-sec08-F47.question_text: How do pavement-ends and dead-end warnings differ in what lies down the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F47.teaching_text: Pavement-ends drops tire grip onto dirt or gravel, while dead-end warns through drivers there is zero exit.

sec08-card-sec08-F48.question_text: Why does Alabama place lane-ends warnings in a three-board sequence ahead of a dropped lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F48.teaching_text: Three spaced warnings ensure drivers boxed beside a semi still catch notice in time to merge smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F49.question_text: On which side of a two-lane highway—and at what zone boundary—does the no-passing warning stand?
sec08-card-sec08-F49.teaching_text: Mounting the yellow pennant on the left shoulder keeps it visible even when a tall truck blocks the right shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Why should your eyes sweep the left roadside—not just the right—before starting a two-lane pass?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Almost every other road post stands on the right, making left-side placement a favorite exam question.

sec08-card-sec08-F50.question_text: What happens if your vehicle or rooftop cargo exceeds the feet-and-inches number on a low-clearance diamond?
sec08-card-sec08-F50.teaching_text: Renting a tall moving van or strapping kayaks high overhead makes reading bridge-clearance numbers essential.

sec08-card-sec08-F51.question_text: What transition—and ongoing reminder—does a vertical two-way-traffic warning convey?
sec08-card-sec08-F51.teaching_text: Forgetting you just left a divided four-lane highway can put you head-on into oncoming left-lane traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F52.question_text: At a merge warning diamond, who yields right-of-way and how should the ramp driver blend in?
sec08-card-sec08-F52.teaching_text: Using the acceleration strip to match highway flow lets you slip cleanly into a gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F53.question_text: Which four signal, junction, median, or slope changes have dedicated advance warning diamonds?
sec08-card-sec08-F53.teaching_text: Steep downhill grades heat truck brakes fast while divided-highway-ends warnings bring opposing traffic back together.

sec08-card-sec08-F54.question_text: Which four traction, bridge, livestock, or wildlife hazards do specialized warning diamonds announce?
sec08-card-sec08-F54.teaching_text: Deer travel in small groups at dawn and dusk—spotting one crossing means more likely trail right behind.

sec08-card-sec08-F55.question_text: Do pedestrian-crossing boards appear strictly at corners, and what duty applies when walkers step in?
sec08-card-sec08-F55.teaching_text: Mid-block trail and campus crosswalks surprise drivers who only scan for walkers at traffic lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F56.question_text: What two student-safety alerts come from school-crossing boards and school-bus-stop-ahead boards?
sec08-card-sec08-F56.teaching_text: Bus-stop-ahead warnings guard rural hills or curves where a halted yellow bus sits out of sight.

sec08-card-sec08-F57.question_text: Why might you encounter bicycle, pedestrian, or school boards in two different yellow shades across Alabama?
sec08-card-sec08-F57.teaching_text: Towns phase in fluorescent yellow-green gradually, so both older standard yellow and bright green-yellow carry full force.

sec08-card-sec08-F58.question_text: At least how many feet of side clearance does Alabama's bicycle-passing regulatory board require?
sec08-card-sec08-F58.teaching_text: Three open feet keeps side mirrors and wind buffeting safely clear of handlebars.

sec08-card-sec08-F59.question_text: When does Alabama's bikes-may-use-full-lane board remind drivers that cyclists belong right in the travel lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F59.teaching_text: On narrow lanes too tight to share safely side by side, riding center prevents unsafe squeeze-passes.

sec08-card-sec08-F60.question_text: What nickname describes shared-lane bicycle pavement markings, and what do they remind drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-F60.teaching_text: Bike-and-chevron sharrows guide riders away from parked-car door zones and alert motorists to share patiently.

sec08-card-sec08-F61.question_text: What four potential changes—and driver response—come with a road-construction warning?
sec08-card-sec08-F61.teaching_text: Work-zone layouts shift daily, so human flagger directions override normal lane habits.

sec08-card-sec08-F62.question_text: Which three human or equipment hazards get dedicated orange work-zone warnings along Alabama highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F62.teaching_text: Slow highway shoulder mowers kick up hidden gravel and swing wide around culvert posts.

sec08-card-sec08-F63.question_text: During which hours do large sequencing work-zone arrow panels run, and what two messages do they send?
sec08-card-sec08-F63.teaching_text: Bright lighted arrow boards cut through noon glare and midnight darkness alike to shift traffic out of closed lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What is the purpose of guide boards, and which color pair gives route directions and distances?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Spotting white lettering on green overhead panels lets you line up your exit mileposts early.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What roadside needs are advertised on blue-and-white highway guide boards?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Gas, food, lodging, hospital, and rest-area icons always ride on blue backgrounds.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Which destinations are marked by brown-and-white roadside guide boards?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: State parks, historic battlefields, campgrounds, and museums stand out cleanly on brown panels.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What three practical purposes do green roadside mileposts serve along Alabama's main highways?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Reading the nearest milepost to nine-one-one dispatchers brings troopers and paramedics straight to a rural breakdown.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: At which two compass state borders—or route start—does Alabama highway milepost numbering begin at zero?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Rising numbers heading north or east tell you both your exact mileage from the border and travel direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Into what four broad categories does Alabama group roadway pavement markings?
