sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Roadway paint works alongside upright posts to keep lanes, shoulders, and pedestrian zones clear in your forward view.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What traffic does a centerline divide, and how does Alabama's manual state its color on two-lane versus multi-lane or one-way roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Watch Alabama's exact manual wording—opposing two-lane centerlines are yellow while multi-lane and one-way lane dividers are white.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What passing rule applies along a broken, dashed centerline?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Dashed paint permits overtaking only after you verify clear sightlines and zero oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: When a solid yellow stripe runs alongside a broken stripe, how do you tell whether passing is banned for you?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Always obey the stripe closest to your left tires—solid on your side locks you in lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What passing rule applies when two solid yellow stripes replace the broken centerline?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Curves, hills, and busy driveway stretches use double yellow to lock both directions out of oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How do broken alone, solid-on-your-side, and double-solid yellow stripes step up passing restrictions?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Reading your nearest stripe solves every two-lane passing-paint question in one glance.
sec09-card-sec09-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Broken allows, single yours, double everyone

visual_sync.text_span: Broken allows, single yours, double everyone

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: On a two-lane road marked no-passing both ways, for what sole maneuver may you cross the centerline?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Turning left into a driveway, alley, or side street stays legal across double yellow once oncoming cars clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: On an undivided multi-lane two-way highway, when is crossing the centerline permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: With multiple lanes already going your way, overtaking never crosses into opposing traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Which drivers—and from which directions—are allowed inside a center two-way left-turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Using the shared center bay as a passing strip or long acceleration runway invites head-on collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What lane flow do broken white stripes divide, and may you cross them?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: White dashes always tell you neighboring lanes roll the same direction as you.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What boundary does a solid white right-edge stripe mark, and when may tires cross it?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Bright right-edge stripes guide your eyes past oncoming headlight glare and keep wheels off soft shoulders.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: Where do yellow left-edge lines appear on divided roads, and on which side must you pass yellow-painted islands?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Yellow always stays to your left—passing right of yellow-painted islands keeps you out of oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Between lanes moving the same way, does a normal solid white stripe ban lane changes or discourage them?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Solid white near intersections and ramps urges holding your lane, though careful crossing is not illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What extra message does an extra-wide solid white lane stripe add beyond a standard stripe?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Wide white channelizing stripes border turn bays and exit gores where speed differences run sharp.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What is the legal rule when two parallel solid white lines separate same-direction lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Notice the three-step white ladder—single discourages, wide demands extra care, and double solid bans crossing flatly.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Where can solid white crosswalk stripes appear, and what must you do when pedestrians occupy an unsignalized one?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Mid-block painted crosswalks carry the exact same stop-for-pedestrians mandate as corner crosswalks.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: In what color are pavement words like school zone or railroad crossing painted, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Tall elongated white stencils hit your downward sightline even when trucks block roadside posts.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What is your baseline duty at a steady circular red light—and what post-stop turns can apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Coming to a dead stop behind the line always comes first before any permitted red-light turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Which lamp precedes steady yellow, what does yellow mean, and what entry rule hits on red?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Yellow clears cars already entering—crossing the line after red lights up is running a red light.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Which movements does a steady circular green allow—and whom must you still yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Green gives permission rather than blind immunity—left turners and everyone else still yield to lawful crossers.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What do alternating red flashers paired with a railroad crossbuck mean, and what multi-track check follows?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Alternating red crossing lamps carry mandatory stop authority—never roll until every track is verified empty.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: At a gated railroad crossing, do you wait for the gate arm to drop before stopping or stop as soon as lights blink?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Stopping the instant red lights start keeps your roof clear of descending gate arms.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: How do green and yellow turn arrows govern turning lanes compared with circular traffic lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Dedicated arrow phases separate turning queues cleanly from fast opposing through traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Why is turning on a green arrow called a protected movement?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: While your green arrow glows brightly, conflicting oncoming through lanes face red.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: When a steady green arrow glows alongside another lens, what moves may you make and whom do you yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Even on a green arrow, leftover pedestrians finishing the crosswalk still keep priority.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: What is ending whenever a steady yellow arrow replaces a green arrow—including alongside a circular green?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Oncoming traffic is about to receive green—prepare to stop or yield depending on the next phase.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: When a steady yellow arrow glows alone or beside circular red, what happens once that yellow arrow goes dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Entering the intersection after that yellow arrow extinguishes violates mandatory red-turn clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How does a green turn arrow contrast directly with the yellow arrow that follows it?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Never floor the gas to beat a yellow arrow—opposing six-lane traffic is seconds from launching.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: Where are lane-use control lights mounted, and what do they regulate?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Tunnels, bridges, and rush-hour reversible corridors switch lane direction overhead throughout the day.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: What does a steady red X hanging directly above a lane forbid—and how strong is its authority?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Oncoming traffic or crash crews may occupy that strip—vacate immediately regardless of green intersection lights ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: What does a steady downward green arrow over a lane allow—and do normal road rules still apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: An open-lane gantry arrow still requires stopping at red intersection lights and obeying speed limits ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: In Alabama's manual, what unique rule applies under a steady yellow X hanging over a lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Watch Alabama's specific manual definition—steady yellow X warns of potentially hazardous conditions requiring extra caution.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do Alabama's red X, downward green arrow, and steady yellow X divide overhead lane control?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Locking in red-closed, green-open, and Alabama's yellow-caution covers every overhead lane-control question.
sec09-card-sec09-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Red closed, green open, yellow caution

visual_sync.text_span: Red closed, green open, yellow caution

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How is a roundabout controlled, and in which clock direction does traffic circle the center island?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Yield control at each entry replaces red-light waits while counterclockwise motion keeps everyone flowing one way.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Which way do you steer to enter a roundabout, whom do you yield to, and how do you reach your street?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Every trip—whether going right, straight, left, or turning back—starts with a right-hand entry.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: Why are roundabouts replacing traditional intersections across the United States?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Eliminating left turns across oncoming lanes wipes out the deadliest head-on and T-bone collision angles.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: By roughly what three percentages do roundabouts cut fatal crashes, injury crashes, and total crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Slashing fatal wrecks by ninety percent makes that ninety-seventy-five-thirty-five trio a standout Alabama statistic.
sec09-card-sec09-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Ninety fatal, seventy-five injury, thirty-five all

visual_sync.text_span: Ninety fatal, seventy-five injury, thirty-five all

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: Before reaching the yield line of a roundabout, what speed, sign, and crosswalk duties come first?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Splitter-island crosswalks sit one car-length upstream of the circle—yield there first before scanning left.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: From which side does circulating roundabout traffic approach your bumper—and when do you pull in?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Because traffic circles counterclockwise, every car that can cross your bow comes strictly from your left.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: How fast should you drive once inside a roundabout, and how do you depart onto your target road?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: Low neighborhood speeds make tight curves comfortable and give approaching drivers predictable gaps.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.question_text: Walking across a roundabout leg, which way does a pedestrian look at the curb versus on the center splitter island?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.teaching_text: The raised splitter island breaks crossing into two one-way checks—entering cars from left, exiting cars from right.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.question_text: What two legal ways can a bicyclist navigate through a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.teaching_text: Confident riders take the center of the low-speed lane while others hop onto the perimeter sidewalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F49.question_text: Between entering drivers on the approach and drivers already inside the roundabout, who holds right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F49.teaching_text: Keeping the inner ring flowing prevents gridlock from locking up every leg at once.

sec09-card-sec09-F50.question_text: Even when your destination road lies to your left, why must you never turn left at a roundabout entry?
sec09-card-sec09-F50.teaching_text: Turning left at the splitter island drives head-on clockwise into oncoming circulating cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.question_text: Whom must you watch for and yield to again as you peel out of a roundabout exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.teaching_text: Drivers focused left on circulating cars often forget walkers stepping off the splitter island across their exit.

sec09-card-sec09-F46.question_text: What is the effortless fix—and strict ban—if you accidentally pass your intended roundabout exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F46.teaching_text: One ten-second lap brings your street right back around safely, whereas backing up causes instant rear-ends.

sec09-card-sec09-F47.question_text: How do you clear the way for an ambulance depending on whether you are approaching or already inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F47.teaching_text: Stopping inside the narrow ring traps wide fire engines—clear your exit first and pull right.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Why does emergency-vehicle response flip once your front bumper crosses into the roundabout circle?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Before the yield line shoulders are wide; inside the island ring, exiting clears the bottleneck fastest.

sec09-card-sec09-F48.question_text: What is the raised paved collar around a roundabout's center island for, and who should stay off it?
sec09-card-sec09-F48.teaching_text: Long semi-trailers track tightly across that raised apron—sedans, pickups, and sport utility vehicles stay in paved lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F51.question_text: Under what sole circumstance should you ever stop your vehicle inside a roundabout circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F51.teaching_text: Stopping politely inside the circle to wave an entering car in triggers rear-end collisions behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F52.question_text: What two steps are critical before pulling into a two-lane roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F52.teaching_text: Crossing the outer lane into the inner lane requires a clean gap across both circulating streams simultaneously.

sec09-card-sec09-F53.question_text: In a two-lane roundabout, which lanes handle right turns, left or U-turns, and straight-through travel?
sec09-card-sec09-F53.teaching_text: Checking approach arrows for straight-through prevents cutting across an outer-lane driver at the exit.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Why must drivers actively study bad weather, low light, and emergency situations?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Beginner practice mostly happens on clear dry days, leaving storms, darkness, and sudden failures unpracticed unless you study ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Roughly what fraction of Alabama's fatal traffic crashes happen after dark despite lighter traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Fewer cars on the road lull drivers into relaxed speeds right when shortened sightlines make hazards deadly.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What does never overdriving your headlights require of your nighttime speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Outrunning your beam reach means a stalled car or deer enters view too late for full braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Under normal clear conditions, roughly how many feet ahead do high-beam headlights illuminate?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Even bright high beams cover barely past a football field, capping safe highway speed after dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Within how many feet must Alabama drivers dim high beams for oncoming cars versus cars ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: High beams blind oncoming eyes from five hundred feet out and bounce off rearview mirrors within two hundred.
sec11-card-sec11-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred meeting, two hundred following

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred meeting, two hundred following

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: What should you do if an oncoming driver refuses to dim high beams after you switch to low?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Flashing high beams back leaves two blinded drivers closing at highway speed instead of just one.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: How should you maintain vehicle lights and glass to protect visibility at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Road film, frost, or cabin steam scatters oncoming headlights into blinding haze across your windshield.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: When does state law require full headlights rather than parking lights by clock window and visibility?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Parking lights never light the lane ahead, and dim dusk or storm gloom demands full low beams.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: If twilight or gray weather leaves you unsure whether headlights are needed, what should you switch on?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Turning on low beams early sharpens your forward view while helping oncoming drivers spot your bumper sooner.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Which five unlit or slow road hazards demand close night scanning, and what trip prep helps?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Knowing your route beforehand keeps your eyes hunting dark walkers, cyclists, livestock, and slow farm gear.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: How can a passenger and deliberate eye movement keep your vision sharp on night drives?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Staring rigidly at one spot breeds highway trance, whereas shifting focus near, far, and sideways refreshes alertness.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How do the two high-beam dimming distances line up against the visibility threshold requiring headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Pairing five hundred feet for both oncoming dimming and visibility keeps two hundred feet distinct for following.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Where should you guide your eyes when bright oncoming headlights threaten to dazzle you?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Tracking the white fog line keeps your car centered in its lane while sparing your retinas direct glare.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: How do you cut blinding headlight glare shining into your cabin from traffic behind you?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Tilting the prism tab dims trailing high beams without losing track of vehicles following your bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What four actions protect you first if your vehicle breaks down at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Getting completely off live asphalt with hazards blinking warns fast night traffic while steel protects you inside.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: If forced to walk after a night breakdown, how do you walk and where do flares or reflectors belong?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Placing warnings one hundred to five hundred feet back along the right edge alerts approaching lanes early.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Why is speeding extra dangerous after dark, even along routes you drive every day?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Knowing every curve by heart never reveals a fallen tree or stalled truck sitting beyond your beam range.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Which six winter hazards challenge drivers, and does bad weather alone excuse most winter crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Slick pavement and winter gloom are foreseeable hazards, meaning crashes usually stem from failing to slow down.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: What three steps ready your engine, windows, and washer tank before pulling out in winter?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole or running plain water in the reservoir blinds you mid-drive.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Why should you skip spraying windshield washers at highway speed during extreme cold?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Bitter wind chill can flash-freeze washer spray into an opaque ice sheet across your glass in moments.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: How can you safely gauge road slipperiness in winter and set your pace?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Feeling how early tires slip at low speed tells you how much speed to shed before live traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Where do snow treads go, and what speed and spacing adjustments remain required?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Deeper drive-wheel lugs help you pull forward in snow without shortening panic braking distances.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Do snow treads grip glare ice, and what equipment works best on severe ice or deep snow?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Rubber lugs slide across smooth ice, whereas reinforced metal links bite into packed snow and frozen glaze.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: When do running windshield wipers trigger Alabama's headlight law, and what wiper setting is excluded?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Continuous rain, sleet, or snow hides gray cars in spray, while occasional mist wipes stay outside the rule.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: How many times longer is your stopping distance on snow or ice compared with dry asphalt?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Normal dry-road following gaps evaporate instantly when winter surfaces multiply braking distance up to twelvefold.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: How should manual-clutch and automatic drivers start moving on slick snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Spinning the drive wheels polishes snow into slicker ice, whereas second gear or feather-light throttle keeps bite.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: How should you brake normally or stop suddenly on packed snow or ice, and what stays engaged?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Easing off whenever wheels lock restores rolling grip while engine drag helps slow the car smoothly.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: What happens to engine, brake, and steering control the moment tires lose traction in a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Every pedal and wheel input acts through four small tire patches, so sliding rubber ignores driver commands.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: Why must you stay off the brake pedal during a skid until forward rolling returns?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Slamming brakes locks front tires into helpless sled runners that slide straight regardless of wheel angle.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: How do you straighten a skid in a rear-wheel-drive vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Lifting off the gas slows the pushing rear wheels so they stop swinging past the nose.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: How does throttle technique change when straightening a skid in a front-wheel-drive car?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: A gentle touch on the pedal lets pulling front tires tug the nose ahead of the sliding tail.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: When tight space prevents accelerating out of a skid, what fallback does the manual note alongside expert caution?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Removing drive torque lets tires roll freely toward the skid, though panicked shifting into neutral carries risk.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: At what wet-road speeds does a standard car start partial hydroplaning and reach total hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Water wedges lift rubber progressively above thirty-five until tires ride completely on water near fifty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: Why can a mild crosswind or gentle road crown spin a totally hydroplaning vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Floating completely off the asphalt erases braking, accelerating, and steering grip all at once.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: What is your immediate pedal move when hydroplaning, and how do partial and total responses differ?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Decelerating naturally lets tires sink back through standing water without violent steering snaps once grip returns.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: Even with deep tire tread, when should you expect complete hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Once storm puddles stand deeper than your grooves can channel away, speed above fifty floats any tire.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: When should you drive in fog or heavy snow, and what rule governs your pace if you must?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Staying parked beats guessing blindly, and driving requires keeping stopping distance shorter than visible pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: Which headlight setting belongs in fog or falling snow, and why?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight off suspended water droplets and snowflakes into a blinding white wall.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: What should you do if dense fog blinds your view or exhausts your eyes?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Stopping in a travel lane invites pileups, whereas parking well clear with lights glowing stays visible.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: How should you handle narrow hilly or wooded roads with hidden blind pockets?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Crests and trees hide oncoming cars until feet away, so a warning tap alerts hidden drivers.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: What does Alabama law say about shifting into neutral to coast down hills?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Dropping into neutral disconnects engine braking and leaves you slower to respond on steep grades.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: Why does deadly carbon monoxide risk spike in winter, and can you smell the gas?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Warming engines and rolled-up windows trap invisible, scentless exhaust leaks inside the cabin.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: Which four physical symptoms warn of carbon monoxide exposure, and what is the sole remedy?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: Sudden drowsiness at the wheel may be toxic exhaust rather than boredom, demanding immediate open air.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.question_text: What three habits prevent carbon monoxide buildup in or around your vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.teaching_text: Running an engine inside a shut garage fills the space with lethal gas in minutes.
sec11-card-sec11-F43.must_match_memory_hook: Inspect exhaust, crack glass, open garage

visual_sync.text_span: Inspect exhaust, crack glass, open garage

sec11-card-sec11-F44.question_text: Why does the manual stress thinking before acting during any sudden driving emergency?
sec11-card-sec11-F44.teaching_text: Panic reflexes like stomping the brake pedal in a blowout or skid turn recoverable slips into wrecks.

sec11-card-sec11-F45.question_text: What early sound warns of a bad tire, and what four steps handle a sudden blowout?
sec11-card-sec11-F45.teaching_text: Fighting the sideways tug with two firm hands while coasting down prevents flipping the vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F46.question_text: What tire neglect commonly triggers blowouts, and how does rapid air loss steer the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F46.teaching_text: Under-inflated sidewalls flex and overheat at highway speed until they rupture and yank toward the flat side.

sec11-card-sec11-F47.question_text: How do the warning signs and driver actions for losing a wheel compare with a tire blowout?
sec11-card-sec11-F47.teaching_text: Holding straight and easing off the gas without braking keeps the dragging corner from digging in and rolling.

sec11-card-sec11-F48.question_text: If your steering suddenly stops responding, how should you handle gas, gears, and brakes?
sec11-card-sec11-F48.teaching_text: Hard braking or shifting with disconnected steering pitches weight abruptly and spins the car off course.
sec11-card-sec11-F48.must_match_memory_hook: Lift gas smoothly, brake gently later

visual_sync.text_span: Lift gas smoothly, brake gently later

sec11-card-sec11-F49.question_text: What early pedal feel warns of brake trouble, and what do you do if the pedal drops to the floor?
sec11-card-sec11-F49.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can build enough residual hydraulic pressure in dual-circuit lines to slow the vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F50.question_text: If pumping a dead brake pedal fails, what three backup methods can slow and stop the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F50.teaching_text: Applying the parking brake gradually avoids rear lockup, while killing ignition in gear drops power assist.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Which three mechanical failures all share the rule of easing off the gas instead of braking hard?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Grouping all three directional emergencies together keeps panic braking off your mind when stability vanishes.

sec11-card-sec11-F51.question_text: What three steps bring you safely back after your right wheels drop onto a low shoulder?
sec11-card-sec11-F51.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel immediately against the pavement lip slingshots your car across into oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F52.question_text: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane head-on, what four actions apply and which lane is off-limits?
sec11-card-sec11-F52.teaching_text: Dodging left puts you straight back into impact when the sleepy or distracted oncoming driver snaps right.
sec11-card-sec11-F52.must_match_memory_hook: Pull right, slow, warn, never left

visual_sync.text_span: Pull right, slow, warn, never left

sec11-card-sec11-F53.question_text: How should you adjust speed or lane position if an overtaking car gets trapped beside you?
sec11-card-sec11-F53.teaching_text: Braking when they are nearly past, accelerating if they drop back, or taking a firm shoulder prevents a three-car wreck.

sec11-card-sec11-F54.question_text: How does clearing a car stalled on railroad tracks differ between manual and automatic transmissions?
sec11-card-sec11-F54.teaching_text: Automatics block starter engagement in drive gears, leaving manual pushing as the sole way to roll clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F55.question_text: When a train approaches your stalled car on the tracks, which direction must you evacuate on foot?
sec11-card-sec11-F55.teaching_text: Impact hurls wreckage forward down the tracks, so moving forty-five degrees toward the locomotive dodges flying steel.

sec11-card-sec11-F56.question_text: If your vehicle plunges into deep water and briefly floats, how must you exit right away?
sec11-card-sec11-F56.teaching_text: Opening a submerged door floods the cabin instantly while outside water pressure often pins doors shut anyway.
sec11-card-sec11-F56.must_match_memory_hook: Climb out window, keep doors shut

visual_sync.text_span: Climb out window, keep doors shut

sec11-card-sec11-F57.question_text: Which end of a submerged car usually sinks first, and how do you survive if it goes under?
sec11-card-sec11-F57.teaching_text: Heavy engine weight pulls the nose down first, trapping breathable air near the back glass until pressure equalizes.

sec11-card-sec11-F58.question_text: How do you respond to smoke rolling from under the hood, and what must never touch an engine fire?
sec11-card-sec11-F58.teaching_text: Throwing water onto burning gasoline or oil spreads flaming liquid instead of smothering the blaze.

sec11-card-sec11-F59.question_text: How can you cool an engine in stop-and-go traffic, and what rule applies if steam boils out?
sec11-card-sec11-F59.teaching_text: Spinning the fan faster in neutral boosts airflow, while twisting a hot radiator cap unleashes scalding steam.
sec11-card-sec11-F59.must_match_memory_hook: Rev in neutral, leave cap shut

visual_sync.text_span: Rev in neutral, leave cap shut

sec11-card-sec11-F60.question_text: Which backup lights should you try if headlights die, and where do you slow on a dark empty road?
sec11-card-sec11-F60.teaching_text: Braking down while still on smooth asphalt keeps you out of hidden ditches before easing onto the shoulder.

sec11-card-sec11-F61.question_text: What three steps save you if wipers quit in a downpour or the hood flies open at speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F61.teaching_text: Rolling down the side window restores a sightline along the lane edge so you can pull off safely.

sec11-card-sec11-F62.question_text: What two moves handle an accelerator pedal that sticks down while driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F62.teaching_text: Hooking your shoe under a jammed linkage may pop it free, and cutting engine power stops runaway acceleration.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Which Alabama residents need a driver license on public roads, and what single farm exception exists?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Briefly moving a tractor or farm implement down the road needs no license, unlike driving any regular motor vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Who must pass the Alabama driver exam, and when can an expired out-of-state license skip testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Letting an Alabama card lapse past three years forces full retesting, while out-of-state cards expired within one year transfer exam-free.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How does the expiration cutoff that triggers a driver exam differ between Alabama and out-of-state licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Permit questions love swapping the generous three-year home grace cutoff with the strict one-year out-of-state limit.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: When may a federal employee legally drive in Alabama without holding an Alabama driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: The federal exemption covers official trips in government-owned or government-leased vehicles, never personal family errands.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Which drivers aged 16 or older with a valid license from another state or country need no Alabama license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Stationed military members and their dependents keep driving legally on unexpired home-state cards throughout long Alabama assignments.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Under what condition and yearly day cap may a visitor aged 16+ from a non-licensing country drive in Alabama?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Without current-year vehicle registration from that home country, the ninety-day calendar-year visitor privilege disappears.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: How many days after moving to Alabama may a new resident keep driving on a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Waiting past one month after establishing Alabama residency turns your valid old state card into an overdue transfer.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How does a new Alabama resident's grace window compare with the yearly cap for visitors from non-licensing countries?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Keeping the thirty-day move-in deadline separate from the ninety-day foreign visitor rule prevents an easy number mix-up.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: When may an out-of-state student attending school in Alabama drive without getting an Alabama license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Part-time classes do not qualify, whereas full-time campus or trade students keep driving legally on valid home licenses.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which three groups based on age, out-of-state record, or testing will Alabama refuse to license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: An active suspension in another state follows you nationwide and blocks Alabama licensing until cleared.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Which substance-abuse or health conditions cause Alabama to deny a driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Habitual alcohol or narcotic addiction, or any impairment preventing ordinary vehicle control in ALEA's view, bars licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What education requirement must license applicants under age 19 satisfy in Alabama?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Under Act ninety-three-three hundred sixty-eight, teens under nineteen must show high school graduation, enrollment, or a narrow exclusion.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does Alabama's minimum regular licensing age differ from the age cutoff for the school-attendance rule?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Turning sixteen unlocks regular licensing eligibility, yet school enrollment verification stays active all the way until age nineteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What federal status must every applicant prove when applying for a first-time Alabama license or ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Original Alabama credentials cannot be issued until federal lawful-presence verification passes at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which two document-count options prove your identity at the counter, and what list must always be represented?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Whether you bring two items including a photo or three non-photo items, missing a Primary Listing document stops the application.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does the two-document ID path differ from the three-document ID path regarding photos?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Bringing zero photo IDs forces you onto the three-document track, while both tracks still demand one Primary item.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which three items must you bring to transfer an out-of-state driver license to Alabama?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Your old state card alone is never enough without Social Security number proof and one more Primary document.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: How do you prove your birth date if you have no prior Alabama license or ID record on file?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Without an existing Alabama record, examiners accept only an original or certified item straight from the Primary Listing.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which document versions are accepted at the license counter, and what must a certified copy show?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Photocopies of a certified document get rejected because the copy itself must bear an original agency certification.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: What physical flaws or missing signatures will cause an examiner to reject an identity document?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Even a staple hole, tear, fold, or dab of white-out obscuring a key date or missing signature invalidates the paper.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: Which five elements must appear clearly on a notarized document for Alabama to accept it?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: If the notary's commission had already expired on the signing date or the stamp smudges, the notarization fails.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Name the core identity records that qualify on Alabama's Primary Listing?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Certified US birth records, unexpired passports, Alabama cards, citizenship papers, or foreign passports with immigration docs anchor identity.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What must every 15-year-old bring, and what extra rule applies to a foreign birth certificate without a US passport?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Foreign birth certificates require an English translation and embassy certification unless the teen presents a valid US passport.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: Which everyday school, military, or court records count on Alabama's secondary document list?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: School photo IDs, DD-214 forms, marriage licenses, and adoption or name-change decrees back up your Primary item.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: When must you bring proof of your Social Security number, even if you opt out of printing it on your card?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Keeping the digits off the plastic face does not waive verifying your number for licenses, renewals, vessels, or IDs.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: What must acceptable Social Security proof display, and which five original records qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Redacted W-2s showing only the last four digits fail; bring an original full-number card, SSA letter, DD-214, W-2, or A-suffix Medicare card.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: At least how many days of authorized stay in the United States must immigration documents show?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Presenting immigration papers with fewer than thirty permitted days left makes you ineligible for card issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Which additional federal records may non-citizen applicants submit alongside their application?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Pairing an Employment Authorization Document with a Social Security card, a thirty-plus-day visa, or a valid I-94 proves status.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Besides English, which eleven foreign languages are available for Alabama's written knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Testing stations offer eleven translated written options spanning European, Middle Eastern, and Asian languages so newcomers test accurately.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: What testing accommodation is available if an applicant cannot read and understand the written knowledge check?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Automated testing terminals read questions aloud so reading barriers do not block safe drivers from qualifying.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: When did Alabama's Graduated Driver License law take effect, and what general minimum driving age does it set?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Since October first, two thousand two, Alabama has phased teen privileges in around the base driving age of sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: What exact license class and restriction letter do you earn by passing the written knowledge exam at age 15?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: In Alabama a teen learner permit is actually a Class D card stamped with the Y learner restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Who is legally allowed to ride in the front passenger seat beside a 15-year-old Y-restricted learner?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Having an eighteen-year-old friend or unlicensed adult up front violates the Y restriction before your sixteenth birthday.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: How does the front-seat companion rule change once a learner turns 16, and how long does a 15-year-old's permit last?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: After your sixteenth birthday any licensed driver can supervise up front, and the four-year card renews only once.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does the required front-seat supervisor for a 15-year-old learner compare with a learner who has turned 16?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Watch the birthday cutoff closely because before sixteen requires an Alabama twenty-one-plus driver or instructor, then relaxes.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How many years is a learner license issued at age 15 valid, and how many renewals are allowed?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Alabama caps fifteen-year-old learner cards at one single renewal rather than letting learners renew indefinitely.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: What restriction code, supervision rule, and term length apply to a Learner License first earned at age 16 or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Starting at sixteen or twenty-five still stamps the Y restriction requiring a licensed copilot across a four-year term.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Why is the companion rule simpler when you get your Learner License at 16 or older instead of 15?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Once you are sixteen or older, the supervisor beside you only needs a valid license rather than being twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: What two sets of violations can get an Alabama Learner License suspended or revoked?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Driving solo without your required front-seat supervisor breaks your Y-restriction terms and can revoke the permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: When does a teen aged 16 or 17 become eligible to take the road skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Comparable out-of-state learner time counts toward the six months, or turning eighteen waives the waiting clock.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How long must a 16- or 17-year-old hold a learner license before scheduling the road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Rushing straight to the road skills check on your sixteenth birthday fails unless you already logged six learner months.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: What happens to your learner card, your Y restriction, and the fee when you pass the road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Passing trades in your learner plastic and lifts the Y restriction at zero extra fee for the remaining term.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Does lifting the Y restriction after passing the road skills check start a brand-new four-year expiration period?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Upgrading from Y-restricted to unrestricted keeps the original expiration date printed from your learner issue.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: What license, restriction code, weight cap, and engine limit apply to 14- and 15-year-old motor-driven cycle riders?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Fourteen- and fifteen-year-olds are capped at light cycles weighing up to two hundred pounds with one hundred fifty cc max.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: Starting at age 16, what vehicles does an unrestricted Class M motorcycle license cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Class M covers motorcycles only—saddle-seated machines running on three or fewer ground wheels, excluding tractors.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How does a Class D license with a Y restriction differ from a Class M license with a B restriction?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Mixing up restriction letters is easy—Y marks a supervised car learner, while B caps young riders to light cycles.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: What kinds of driving restrictions can the ALEA Director add to a license, and what happens if you ignore one?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: Driving without required glasses or hand controls breaks a legal condition of your license and can strip your privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: At what minimum age can you earn an Alabama vessel license, and what two paths qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: Twelve-year-olds qualify for motorized watercraft credentials either by passing the office exam or bringing an approved boating certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What must you wear during the road test if your permit or license already carries a corrective-lens restriction?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Showing up to drive for the examiner without required glasses or contacts stops your driving check before leaving the lot.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What restriction gets added to your license if the counter vision screening shows you need corrective lenses?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Passing the eye chart only with glasses or contacts means every future trip behind the wheel legally requires them.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What is your next step after failing the counter vision check, and when can you finish testing?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Failing the counter eye check pauses your application until a licensed eye doctor certifies your vision supports safe driving.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: How does the corrective-lens rule for the road test connect with the rule triggered by the vision screening?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Already-restricted drivers must wear lenses for the road evaluation, while needing lenses on the eye chart adds an all-trips requirement.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Which three core subjects appear on Alabama's knowledge test, and what single study source supplies every question?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Every single multiple-choice item pulls straight from Alabama's driver manual covering traffic statutes, signs, and safe habits.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which test plus fee unlocks a learner license, and which test plus fee unlocks a regular driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Passing the written check and paying the fee issues your learner permit, whereas full licensing waits for road skills and fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: What testing and study rules apply if you want both a motor-driven cycle license and a car learner license?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Car knowledge alone does not cover two-wheel dynamics, so dual applicants sit for both exams using the separate motorcycle booklet.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Which knowledge-test applicants are allowed to use Alabama's automated testing terminals?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Every knowledge-exam candidate can use the automated computer stations rather than needing a special request.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How do the knowledge test and the road test split up the path from beginner to regular driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Think of the written check as your supervised-practice ticket and the behind-the-wheel drive as your solo graduation.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Who administers Alabama's road test, and who must accompany a 16-year-old applicant to the appointment?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Driving solo or bringing an older teen friend at age sixteen gets turned away without a parent or legal guardian present.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: Which specific lights, signals, and sound equipment does the examiner inspect on your car before starting the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: A burned-out brake bulb, dead turn signal, or silent horn cancels your drive right in the inspection lane.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Which two vehicle papers must you show before the road test, and when is a rental car allowed?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Bringing a parent's rental car fails inspection unless the rental contract specifically lists your name as an additional driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: How do you insert a penny to check tire tread, and what visual cue means the tire must be replaced?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Seeing the top of Abe Lincoln's head inside the deepest groove means bald rubber that hydroplanes easily on wet asphalt.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: How should you position your back and feet in the driver's seat, and what safety risk comes from slouching?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Slumping forward lets your hips slide underneath the lap belt during a crash instead of letting belts and airbags catch you.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Where should your right heel stay for pedal control, and how high should the top of the steering wheel sit?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Pivoting on a planted heel speeds brake transitions, while keeping the rim below chin height prevents airbag face injuries.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: What can ALEA require if a driver appears to have a condition affecting safe driving, and what happens if unreported?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Concealing a medical condition that impairs driving control can trigger license revocation instead of periodic medical clearance.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: What identity proof does an Alabama non-driver ID require, and which three groups of residents is it meant for?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Residents who hold no Alabama license, cannot physically qualify, or are retiring from driving still get full state photo ID.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: How many years does an Alabama license last, and how many days early can you renew before expiration?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Renewing up to roughly six months ahead of your birthday lets you beat counter lines without losing your valid status.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: Which residents temporarily away from Alabama may renew by mail, and what four-year rule applies to their card?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Stationed service members, dependents, college students, and out-of-state workers qualify only if a photo-signature card issued within four years.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: How long is Alabama's post-expiration renewal grace period, and does your license stay valid during those days?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: State law keeps your driving privilege active for sixty days past the printed date so you can renew cleanly.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: How long after expiration can you renew without retesting, and what start date anchors the new four-year term?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Waiting two years to renew does not buy two bonus years because the four-year clock counts from the old expiration date.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: Once you are past the grace period, may you legally drive on an expired license just because the three-year renewal window is open?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Skipping the retest at the counter never excuses driving on the street with an expired license past grace.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: How does the 180-day window before expiration differ from the 60-day window after expiration?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Don't flip the numbers—you get six months ahead to renew early, and only sixty days afterward of valid grace.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: What single benefit does the three-year post-expiration window grant, and what does it strictly forbid?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Get a ride to the licensing office because driving yourself there on a long-expired card risks a citation.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How does the four-year term start date differ between a timely renewal and a late renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Late renewals anchor back to your prior expiration date rather than starting fresh on the day you visit.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Where and how do you replace a lost, destroyed, or unreadable license that has not expired?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Bring identity proof like a certified birth certificate to the Probate Judge or License Commissioner for an exam-free duplicate.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: What criminal charges and penalties can strike someone who files a false affidavit to get a duplicate license?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Lying on a sworn lost-card form to keep an extra plastic ID triggers felony-grade forgery or perjury prosecution.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: When do you apply for a duplicate license rather than a license renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Duplicates replace missing or damaged cards mid-term, whereas renewals extend cards that are expiring or already expired.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: Who must process changes to license classes, restrictions, or endorsements, and will mail forwarding deliver your card?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Postal mail never forwards Alabama licenses or IDs to a new address, preventing stolen identity cards.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Which documents are needed to change the name on your license, and where must STAR ID holders go?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Update Social Security first, bring your marriage certificate or court order, and visit an ALEA office if holding STAR ID.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: Within how many days of moving inside Alabama must you report your new address, and what does updating your record cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Reporting your new street address within thirty days updates Driver License Division files free without needing a new card.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How does the cost of reporting an in-state address move compare with getting a corrected card after a name change?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Updating your digital address file costs zero dollars, whereas printing a new plastic card for a name change charges a duplicate fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: Which vehicles and craft do Alabama's non-commercial Classes D, M, and V each cover?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Remembering D for everyday cars, M for motorcycles, and V for vessels covers every non-commercial Alabama letter.
sec02-card-sec02-F27.must_match_memory_hook: D passenger, M cycles, V boats

visual_sync.text_span: D passenger, M cycles, V boats

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Which license class covers standard passenger cars, and which two letters cover motorcycles and motorized boats?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Holding an ordinary Class D car license does not automatically let you ride a motorcycle or pilot a powerboat.
sec02-card-sec02-R08.must_match_memory_hook: D cars, M bikes, V vessels

visual_sync.text_span: D cars, M bikes, V vessels

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: What combined weight rating and towed-unit rating trigger the need for a Class A commercial license?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Pulling a trailer rated above ten thousand pounds in a combination topping twenty-six thousand pounds requires Class A.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: Which vehicles require a Class B license versus a Class C commercial license?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Class B covers heavy single trucks with light tows, while Class C covers sixteen-person passenger vans and placarded hazmat.
sec02-card-sec02-F29.must_match_memory_hook: B heavy single, C sixteen-plus hazmat

visual_sync.text_span: B heavy single, C sixteen-plus hazmat

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: When two heavy rigs both exceed 26,000 pounds, what exact trailer rating separates Class A from Class B?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Ten thousand pounds on the towed trailer is the exact dividing line between a Class A combo and Class B.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: Which lower vehicle classes may holders of Class A, Class B, or Class C licenses legally drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Class A covers B, C, and D; Class B covers C and D; and Class C covers everyday Class D cars.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: When does a licensed 12- or 13-year-old boater need an adult aboard, and at what age may a licensed teen boat solo?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Licensed twelve- and thirteen-year-olds need a licensed adult twenty-one or older ready at the helm until turning fourteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: What birthday cutoff exempts boaters from the vessel exam, and what office step is still required?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Boaters born before April twenty-eighth, nineteen fifty-four skip testing yet still visit an office to add Class V.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: What credential must you physically carry whenever driving, and whom must you show it to on request?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Leaving your wallet at home breaks Alabama's carry requirement even if your license status is active in the database.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: Under Alabama's June 2024 Hands-Free Law, when does physically holding a wireless device become a violation?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Drifting across lane lines un-signaled, swerving, or driving sloppily with a phone in hand triggers a hands-free stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: Within a 24-month window, what fines and license points apply to first, second, and third hands-free convictions?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Each repeat inside two years adds another fifty dollars and one more point—climbing from fifty and one to one-fifty and three.
sec02-card-sec02-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Fifty one, hundred two, one-fifty three

visual_sync.text_span: Fifty one, hundred two, one-fifty three

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: How broadly does Alabama's Hands-Free Law define a wireless device?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Tablets, smartwatches, or any gadget starting or receiving communication data count right alongside smartphones.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: How do the fine and points on second and third hands-free convictions within 24 months scale up from the first?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Racking up three phone tickets inside two years stacks six total points on your record alongside rising fines.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Beyond court fines or jail, in which four administrative ways can a traffic conviction cost your driving privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Paying a court clerk never guarantees your license stays active if ALEA triggers one of four separate actions.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What minimum reinstatement fee applies before you can get relicensed after losing your Alabama privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Clearing your suspension clock alone is not enough until you pay at least one hundred dollars and meet state conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: How much extra money gets tacked on if you fail to surrender a canceled, revoked, or suspended license on time?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Holding onto invalidated plastic past the deadline adds an avoidable fifty-dollar penalty onto your reinstatement bill.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which extra reinstatement charges follow a drug-related conviction versus an unpaid child-support suspension?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Permit questions test both add-ons—twenty-five extra dollars after drug convictions and fifty extra after child-support holds.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: How do Alabama's base reinstatement fee and its three possible extra charges stack together?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Starting at one hundred dollars, late surrender adds fifty, drug convictions add twenty-five, and child support adds fifty.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: For what eligibility or paperwork reasons may the ALEA Director cancel a driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Leaving off required facts, submitting false details, or failing basic eligibility lets ALEA void the card outright.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Once a revocation period finally ends, what must a driver do to get licensed again?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Revocation wipes out your old license completely, requiring a brand-new application and passing every exam from scratch.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How does getting licensed after revocation differ from the core reason behind a cancellation?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Revocation terminates a valid privilege and forces full retesting, whereas cancellation means you never qualified originally.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Which fatal crash or criminal-use convictions force the ALEA Director to revoke a license?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Manslaughter or homicide with a motor vehicle, or using any vehicle to commit a felony, triggers mandatory revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Which alcohol or controlled-substance driving convictions trigger mandatory license revocation in Alabama?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: A second alcohol DUI or driving while addicted to or unsafely impaired by controlled substances mandates revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: Which conviction number makes license revocation mandatory for alcohol or controlled-substance impaired driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: While a first DUI triggers suspension, picking up a second or subsequent impaired conviction upgrades to mandatory revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: What failure at an injury or fatal crash scene triggers mandatory license revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Fleeing a crash that hurts or kills someone without stopping, rendering aid, and identifying yourself revokes your license.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which sworn-statement crime, twelve-month reckless streak, or vehicle-theft offense also mandates revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Lying under oath to the Director, racking up three reckless convictions in twelve months, or joyriding revokes privileges.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What triggers a license suspension, and what two snags can block reinstatement afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Unlike revocation, a suspended card comes back afterward unless it expired mid-term or required conditions remain unfinished.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Even when your suspension calendar finishes, which two things prevent automatic license reinstatement?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Check your plastic's expiration date and finish every fee or filing so your privilege actually reactivates.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Which three patterns of poor driving skill or repeated violations are grounds for license suspension?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Even without hitting mandatory revocation, stacking serious moving tickets or showing driving incompetence suspends your card.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: How can lending out, damaging, or misbehaving out of state get your Alabama license suspended?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Letting someone borrow your card, altering it, or catching a serious out-of-state ticket follows you home to ALEA.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Which police-pursuit, street-racing, or traffic-court failures can suspend your license?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Ignoring a court date or ticket fine suspends your license right alongside fleeing police or highway street racing.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Which age group of drivers risks license suspension for withdrawing from school before graduation?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Leaving secondary school early without a qualifying exemption can suspend teen driving privileges from fifteen through eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Which insurance, family-court, or health issues appear on Alabama's suspension list?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Letting required SR-22 proof lapse, falling behind on child support, or developing unsafe medical issues suspends driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: What record point count or Graduated Driver License ticket count appears on the suspension list?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Teens on a Graduated Driver License have a hair-trigger threshold at just two moving violations.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: How does the four-point suspension listing relate to the two-violation Graduated Driver License listing?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Either four record points or two moving tickets on a graduated license can independently trigger suspension review.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: How does Alabama's suspension list treat a first-offense DUI or drug conviction for juveniles and adults?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Whether you are a teenager or an adult, a first alcohol or drug offense lands squarely on the suspension list.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Does a traffic conviction outside Alabama add points to your Alabama driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Interstate reporting sends out-of-state speeding or reckless convictions straight back onto your Alabama point tally.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: How many points hit your record for an alcohol-and-driving conviction that does not trigger mandatory revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Six points is Alabama's highest single-ticket hit, immediately putting you halfway to a sixty-day point suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: How many points do reckless driving, vehicular reckless endangerment, and Admin Per Se violations each carry?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Catching two six-point convictions within two years hits twelve points and triggers an automatic sixty-day suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: How many points are assessed for failing to yield right-of-way or illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Alabama ranks blowing past a school bus and cutting off right-of-way just one point below reckless driving.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: By how many points do reckless driving and Admin Per Se exceed failing to yield or passing a school bus?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Locking in six for reckless or Admin Per Se versus five for bus passes and yield failures nails point-tier questions.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: How do the points for passing a stopped school bus compare with an emergency-vehicle violation?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Don't assume both flashing-light violations match—passing a stopped school bus charges five points while emergency violations charge two.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: How many points apply to wrong-side driving or illegal passing versus following too closely?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Crossing into opposing lanes or passing illegally adds four points, while tailgating adds three.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: How do the point values for tailgating and work-zone marker violations compare with illegal passing?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Grouping tailgating and disobeying construction markers together at three points keeps them cleanly below four-point illegal passes.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: At what exact speed over the posted limit does speeding jump from 2 points to 5 points?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Hitting twenty-six miles per hour over the limit more than doubles your point hit from two straight to five.
sec03-card-sec03-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Two up to twenty-five, five above

visual_sync.text_span: Two up to twenty-five, five above

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Speeding 26 mph or more over the limit carries the exact same 5-point hit as which right-of-way offense?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Extreme speeding at twenty-six-plus over lands in the exact five-point bracket as failing to yield and school bus passes.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: How many points are charged for failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Ignoring cones, arrows, or channelizing signs around road crews puts three points on your driving record.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: How many points apply to inability to control a vehicle, improper lane use, drinking while operating, motorcycle misuse, or emergency violations?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Every offense in that everyday control, lane, open-drinking, cycle, and emergency group adds two points.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: How many points do missing or wrong turn signals, improper turns, coasting, and unsafe operation each add?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Skipping blinkers, coasting in neutral, or swinging wide turns chips two points apiece toward suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Over a two-year window, how many suspension days follow 12–14 points, 15–17 points, and 18–20 points?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Every three extra points inside twenty-four months tacks thirty more days onto your suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: Over a two-year window, how long is your license suspended at 21–23 points versus 24 or more points?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Crossing twenty-one points benches you half a year, and hitting twenty-four suspends you for three hundred sixty-five days.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: At what two-year point totals do Alabama's shortest 60-day suspension and longest 365-day suspension begin?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Doubling the twelve-point entry threshold to twenty-four points jumps your penalty from two months to a full year.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: What kind of hearing may you request after getting a suspension notice, and where is it held?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: You can ask for a pre-suspension or administrative review in front of an ALEA agent right in your home county.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: What are the two ways to submit a request for an Alabama administrative license hearing?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Filing promptly either online or in writing to Driver License Services preserves your right to review before suspension locks.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What highway design features set freeways apart and make long trips safer with less driver fatigue?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Eliminating stop signs, signals, and cross-street traffic removes intersection T-bones across high-speed miles.
sec12-card-sec12-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Divided lanes, zero stops, zero crossings

visual_sync.text_span: Divided lanes, zero stops, zero crossings

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: What two habits anchor safe freeway driving, and which lane belongs to slower-moving vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Camping slowly in left lanes forces faster traffic to pass unpredictably on the right.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Why should you pick one freeway lane matching your desired pace instead of weaving across lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Constant lane-hopping multiplies blindspot exposure at seventy miles per hour while saving almost zero travel time.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Before shifting freeway lanes to overtake or exit, what two steps must come well ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: High freeway speeds close gaps fast, so early blinkers warn nearby cars before you cross dashed paint.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Where must you park during a freeway breakdown, and where should you stay if possible?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Wandering along a high-speed freeway shoulder exposes pedestrians to distracted drifting trucks.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Which three visual distress signals tell patrolling officers you need help on a freeway shoulder?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Displaying clear breakdown markers flags troopers down for help without stepping toward live freeway lanes.
sec12-card-sec12-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Open trunk, raised hood, white cloth

visual_sync.text_span: Open trunk, raised hood, white cloth

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Under what sole circumstance is parking along a freeway permitted?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Pulling onto a freeway shoulder for phone calls or naps invites deadly high-speed rear-end strikes.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How do entrance ramps and acceleration lanes work together when joining a freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Using the acceleration strip to match highway velocity lets you slip into traffic without forcing hard braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What three actions move you smoothly from the acceleration lane into live freeway traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Picking your gap early while blinking lets your entry blend seamlessly into right-lane speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: While through drivers should make room, who legally yields when entering a freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Assuming highway cars will move left for you causes sideswipes whenever a truck boxes them into the right lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: When, if ever, should you come to a full stop inside a freeway acceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Halting in an acceleration strip traps trailing ramp cars and forces a dangerous zero-to-seventy merge.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: How must you enter a freeway ramp posted with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Without a speed-matching strip, muscling into fast traffic causes immediate rear-end collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: How does a highway interchange let traffic cross, enter, or leave without conflicting?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Bridges and dedicated ramps separate crossing streams vertically so nobody cuts across oncoming freeway speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: What are the four standard highway interchange designs named in the Alabama manual?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Recognizing ramp geometry early keeps you from guessing whether an exit loops sharply or meets a signal.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What traffic pattern does a directional interchange serve, and how are minor turns handled?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Direct flyover ramps carry major volume fast while ordinary diamond ramps handle lighter cross movements.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How does a cloverleaf interchange connect four directions, and which two conflicts does it eliminate?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Sweeping right-hand loop ramps replace across-traffic left turns, though tight loop curves demand early slowdowns.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: How many ramps form a diamond interchange, and where do left turns take place?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Straight off-ramps carry you down to the crossroad intersection before any left turn happens.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: At what roadway meeting shape is a trumpet interchange built?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: When one road terminates against a freeway without continuing across, a sweeping trumpet loop links every turn.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: At a diamond interchange, do left turns happen on the freeway mainline or after leaving on a ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Never hunt for a left-hand median turn on a diamond freeway because all four ramps exit right first.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: How should you position your vehicle as your planned freeway exit approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Diving across three lanes at the last gore stripe triggers multi-lane freeway pileups.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Where must you shed speed when leaving a freeway, and what awaits at the ramp end?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Braking hard on the main freeway lane surprises seventy-mile-per-hour traffic right behind your bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Which three moves are strictly forbidden if you roll past your freeway exit, and what should you do?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Stopping, reversing, or cutting the median turns a five-minute detour into a fatal high-speed collision.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: What two vehicle conditions are prerequisites for safe driving under Alabama equipment law?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Sharp driver reflexes cannot stop a car in time when neglected brakes, tires, or lights fail.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Which two independent braking controls must every automobile carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: A separate mechanical parking brake gives emergency stopping power if hydraulic foot lines lose pressure.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: What must every vehicle's muffler prevent, and which exhaust modifications are outlawed?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Loud cutouts and bypasses mask nearby emergency sirens while breaking state equipment statutes.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: What deadly hazard requires periodic inspection of your vehicle's exhaust system?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Rusted pipes or loose clamps let odorless lethal exhaust seep through floorboards into closed cabins.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: What equipment rule applies to every motor vehicle built with a windshield?
