sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Streaking or dead blades blind you instantly when a sudden summer cloudburst or truck splash hits.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: How many feet behind the vehicle must required rearview mirrors show clearly?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Seeing two hundred feet aft tracks fast-closing highway traffic before you brake or change lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: Which four front and rear lamp types make up Alabama's minimum vehicle lighting list?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Missing a brake lamp or tag light invites immediate nighttime stops and rear-end crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: From how far must all required lamps be seen, and how far ahead must properly aimed high beams reach?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Other drivers spot your bulbs from five hundred feet out while aimed high beams illuminate hazards three-fifty ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: Is flashing both turn signals together permitted to warn approaching traffic of a vehicle hazard?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Blinking paired lamps alert fast-moving traffic early whenever a breakdown or slowdown creates danger.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How do the footage rules compare across rearview mirrors, lamp visibility, and high-beam reach?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Keeping mirror view, bulb visibility, and beam reach distinct prevents mixing footage numbers on equipment prompts.
sec12-card-sec12-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Two hundred mirror, five hundred, three-fifty

visual_sync.text_span: Two hundred mirror, five hundred, three-fifty

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: What shares of crash deaths stem from hitting the steering assembly versus windshield or dash without belts?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Seventy percent of fatal interior impacts come from that violent second collision belts prevent.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.question_text: Under what age do children require special infant or child restraints under the manual's equipment section?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.teaching_text: Adult seatbelts ride too high on young frames under six, failing to hold them safely during impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: Why are special child and infant seats critical for young passengers in crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Traffic wrecks remain the top killer of children, and unrestrained toddlers launch forward on impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: What sound device must every motor vehicle carry, and who alone may mount bells, sirens, or whistles?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Reserving sirens and bells strictly for emergency rigs keeps urgent rescue warnings unmistakable in traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: When is honking your horn lawful, and what can needless honking bring?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Blasting the horn in driveways to summon passengers is unlawful and dulls everyone to genuine hazard alerts.
sec12-card-sec12-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Safety warnings only, needless risks arrest

visual_sync.text_span: Safety warnings only, needless risks arrest

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: What four checks cover tire load rating, air pressure, and uneven tread wear?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Uneven bald patches reveal bent wheels or bad alignment before a weakened casing blows at highway speed.
sec12-card-sec12-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Right load, proper air, check wear

visual_sync.text_span: Right load, proper air, check wear

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: Below what tread depth measurement does an automobile tire become illegal in Alabama?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Worn tread thinner than one-sixteenth inch loses wet grip and turns rain showers into hydroplane traps.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: Which driving habits and trip checks protect your tires and spare from premature failure?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Hard launches, fast cornering, and summer heat cook tire rubber, while a flat spare strands you roadside.
sec12-card-sec12-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Smooth starts, cool breaks, check spare

visual_sync.text_span: Smooth starts, cool breaks, check spare

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: What rule governs mixing different tire types on your car or between front and rear axles?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Mismatched tire carcasses flex differently in hard corners and emergency stops, upsetting handling balance.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: Which six vehicle systems wear down over time and require periodic inspection to prevent serious crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Neglecting brakes, exhaust, cooling, lights, wipers, or tires lets one cheap worn part trigger a major wreck.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: What route details should you lock down with a map before starting a freeway trip?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Knowing your interchange numbers beforehand prevents panicked last-second lane dives near unfamiliar exits.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: Why must you check fuel, water, oil, and all five tires before entering a freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Controlled-access highways have no direct roadside pumps or shops, turning an empty tank into a shoulder hazard.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: Where do most pupil-transportation injuries and deaths happen, and what does the manual call that area?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Drivers blowing past flashing red lights and extended stop arms strike children stepping around the bus perimeter.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: Which core attitudes and habits define a safe driver on every single trip?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Quick neighborhood errands trigger sloppy shortcuts when drivers assume short trips carry less crash risk than highway drives.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What steps belong right after climbing into the car and before turning on the ignition?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Fumbling with seat tracks or mirrors while rolling pulls your eyes off driveway hazards and cross traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: How does starting an engine with a manual transmission differ from starting an automatic?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Cranking a manual in gear without pressing the clutch can lurch the vehicle straight into an obstacle.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How should you sit and grip the steering wheel, and when may one hand leave it?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: White-knuckling the rim tenses your shoulders and delays quick evasive steering when a sudden hazard appears.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What sequence gets you safely out of a parallel parking spot and into traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Swinging across two lanes straight from the curb blindsides faster traffic approaching in your mirror blind zone.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: What rule governs staying inside your lane instead of drifting across lane lines?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Drifting across painted dividers confuses drivers beside you and sets up preventable sideswipe collisions in multi-lane traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: Does a roadway section need painted lines to count legally as a traffic lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Test takers often think unpainted residential streets have no lanes, yet lane rules apply wherever cars fit safely.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: When should you decide on an upcoming turn and merge into the proper turning lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Diving across lanes at the last second forces trailing drivers to slam their brakes at busy intersections.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: At least how far ahead must your turn signal start blinking, and how long does it stay on?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Clicking your blinker mid-turn gives nearby walkers and trailing drivers zero time to anticipate your slowing car.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: While actually rounding a corner, where must your hands stay and who holds right-of-way?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Turning drivers fixate on gaps in vehicle traffic and miss pedestrians already stepping into the cross street.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: From slowing down on approach to finishing in your new lane, what steps complete a safe turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Leaving a blinker flashing after finishing a turn tricks cross-street waiting drivers into pulling out ahead of you.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: Why might you pair hand and arm signals with your electric turn signals during daytime driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Direct afternoon glare can make tail lamps look unlit, so a crisp arm signal backs up your intention.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Which lane do you start in and which lane do you enter when turning right from a four-lane highway?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Swinging wide into the middle lane mid-turn puts your fender directly into cross-street traffic turning opposite you.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: Unless signs or markings allow extra turn lanes, how do you execute a left turn off a four-lane or divided road?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Cutting the corner early or drifting wide mid-intersection puts your car across adjacent turning or oncoming paths.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: On a four-lane highway, how does your starting lane for a right turn compare with your starting lane for a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Starting a turn from the wrong through lane cuts straight across vehicles beside you moving at full speed.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: When must your turn signal start flashing, and when do you switch it off?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Both late signaling before corners and forgotten blinkers afterward feed intersection misunderstandings that trigger avoidable T-bone crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: Do hand and arm signals replace your electric turn lights in daylight, or how are they used?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Exam distractors claim arm signals substitute for working blinkers, when Alabama treats them strictly as daytime backup.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Under what visibility and traffic conditions is a three-point turn normally permitted?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Blocking both directions across a narrow roadway takes several seconds, leaving zero margin if fast traffic appears suddenly.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: On which road types and sightline distances are three-point turns strictly outlawed?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Cresting traffic at highway speed covers five hundred feet in seconds and cannot stop for a sideways car.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: Which laws regulate three-point turns, and can you count on a sign marking every illegal spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Waiting for a posted no-turnaround sign will get you ticketed where city rules or short sightlines apply.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: If no sign forbids a turnaround, may you make a three-point turn when oncoming traffic inside five hundred feet lacks sightlines?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Sightline physics overrides missing signage every time, making blind-hill turnarounds unlawful whether a sign stands nearby or not.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: When do you shed speed for a curve, and how do you use the gas while rounding it?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Entering a bend too fast and slamming brakes mid-curve upsets tire grip and pulls you across center.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: How do the road rights and traffic duties of bicyclists compare with those of motor vehicle drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Treating bicycles like toys instead of legal traffic leads drivers to cut off riders who hold lawful right-of-way.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: Where on a roadway does a bicyclist normally ride, and which situations allow moving left?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Broken glass, opening car doors, or left-turn prep force riders out from the gutter, so expect lateral moves.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: Are cyclists allowed to ride two abreast in Alabama, and which direction must they travel?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Honking at two side-by-side riders mistakes legal riding for obstruction, whereas riding against traffic invites head-on collisions.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does the keep-right rule fit together with riding two abreast and moving left on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Test questions pair the right-edge baseline with lawful exceptions so you recognize why cyclists legally claim extra width.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Which signals do bicyclists use to warn others before turning, changing lanes, or stopping?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Knowing standard left-arm hand positions lets you read a cyclist's next move instantly even without electric blinkers.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: When a bicycle lane is present, must cyclists use it, and what is Alabama's rule on sidewalk riding?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Many learners assume sidewalks are safer for bikes, yet Alabama bans sidewalk cycling and mandates marked bike lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Which age group of cyclists must wear a fastened helmet, and on what public places does that apply?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Unfastened straps fly off on first impact, and the mandate reaches parks and public paths besides streets.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: What are the only three reasons a motorist may legally enter a marked bicycle lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Cruising down a bike lane to bypass backed-up traffic illegally invades space reserved for vulnerable two-wheeled riders.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: How should you position your vehicle before turning across a bicycle lane at an intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Turning right straight from the travel lane hooks across a cyclist's path and causes classic right-hook crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: When must drivers stay out of a bicycle lane, and how do they handle turning across one?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Merging safely into the dashed bike stripe blocks overtaking riders from getting trapped beside your right fender.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: At least how much space must you leave when passing a bicyclist in Alabama, and why does speed matter?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Even without bumper contact, the air blast off a fast car can shove a lightweight bike off balance.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: How does the group covered by the bicycle helmet mandate differ from who must obey the three-foot passing rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Adult riders without helmets still get the full three-foot buffer from every single passing motorist on the road.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: In which road locations and traffic situations should you hold back instead of passing a cyclist?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Squeezing past a rider when oncoming cars fill the next lane forces a deadly choice between two collisions.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: How should you behave behind a cyclist when a narrow roadway makes safe passing impossible?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Blasting a horn right behind a bicyclist startles the rider and can trigger a wobble into your bumper.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: At which three everyday conflict points must drivers scan extra carefully for approaching bicycles?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Backing out of driveways or rolling across crosswalks without scanning both ways catches quiet bicycles completely by surprise.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: What happens to a bicycle's braking power in wet weather, and how must drivers adjust?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Wet rims and skinny tires lengthen a cyclist's stopping distance dramatically, so give extra room before stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: What equipment should bicycles carry for night riding, and how should motorists adjust after dark?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Tiny bike reflectors blend into wet pavement glare at night, demanding slower speeds and sharper headlight scanning.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: What road rights do motorcyclists hold, and which group of riders shows up in many motorcycle crashes?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Inexperienced riders may hesitate or brake awkwardly in traffic, so surrounding drivers should leave generous margin.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: How wide is a motorcycle compared with a passenger car, and how does that affect a driver's eyes?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Human depth perception reads narrow shapes as farther away and slower than they really are at intersections.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: Which car maneuver causes a huge share of car-motorcycle injury crashes, and what must you verify first?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Turning left across an approaching bike's path leaves the rider nowhere to go and almost zero armor.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Why is merely spotting an oncoming motorcycle not enough before starting a left turn across its lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: One quick glance spots the headlight, while a second glance tracks how fast that single light closes distance.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: Before pulling out or turning in front of a signaling vehicle, what must you confirm first?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack self-canceling turn signals, so trusting a flashing light alone invites a T-bone collision.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: How much following time should you keep behind a motorcycle in normal conditions, and why avoid tailgating?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Riding a motorcyclist's rear fender forces their eyes into mirrors instead of potholes and traffic ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: May you pull alongside a motorcycle inside the same traffic lane if the lane looks wide enough?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Riders need every foot of lane width to swerve around potholes, oil streaks, and sudden wind gusts.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: If a motorcyclist rides near one edge of the lane, may a car squeeze into the open side?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Riders shift left and right inside their lane to see ahead and stay visible, never inviting cars beside.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: When must you stretch your following gap behind a motorcycle beyond normal, and what visual trap appears?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Wet asphalt reflects streetlamps and headlights into blinding streaks that swallow a motorcycle's single small taillight.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: How does your two-second dry-road gap behind a motorcycle change when darkness, rain, or slick pavement hits?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Bikes balance on two tiny tire patches, so slick pavement demands extra stopping buffer from cars behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.question_text: Which wind forces and road-surface hazards can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or lane path abruptly?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.teaching_text: Loose gravel, bridge grates, or rail tracks that barely rattle a sedan can jolt handlebars instantly sideways.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Does a medicine need a doctor's prescription to impair your driving, or do store-bought remedies count too?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Pharmacy shelf availability never guarantees alertness behind the wheel—both prescription and non-prescription drugs slow reflexes.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What specific question should you ask your physician whenever starting a prescription medication?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Checking side effects at the clinic keeps blurred vision, dizziness, or drowsiness from ambushing you mid-commute.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Which four impairing ingredients lurk inside some non-prescription cold pills and allergy remedies?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Reading active-ingredient labels catches liquid syrups and sinus tablets that quietly pack alcohol or sedatives.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: What three mental or alertness side effects can antihistamines trigger—so strongly some double as sleep aids?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Popping a sinus tablet before a highway drive can hit your brain just like a nighttime sleeping pill.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: What medical class are barbiturates, and what drunk-like effects appear when someone overuses them?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Slurred coordination, mental fog, and heavy drowsiness leave anyone overusing sedatives completely unfit to steer.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: How does Alabama's manual contrast antihistamine side effects with overused barbiturates?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Antihistamines bring drowsiness and confusion at regular doses, whereas excess barbiturates mimic full intoxication.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: How can illegal drugs like hallucinogens and heroin affect environmental awareness, and may users ever drive?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Losing touch with real-time traffic speed, lane edges, and pedestrians turns any vehicle into a lethal weapon.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What link do studies cited in Alabama's manual find between marijuana use and traffic violations?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Slowed time judgment and divided-attention errors explain why researchers link cannabis users to higher ticket rates.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Does mixing alcohol with medication merely double impairment, or do something far worse?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Exam traps offer doubling as a distractor—remember alcohol plus medicine compounds impairment to fatal extremes.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: When a driver lives with a chronic illness or physical impairment, who is responsible for explaining any driving restrictions?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Your doctor understands how seizures, vision changes, or mobility conditions interact with safe vehicle control.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which bad habit causes most rear-end crashes, and which space around your car is easiest to control?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: You cannot force a tailgater off your rear bumper, yet easing off the gas opens front cushion instantly.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Which two real-time factors should determine how much following distance you leave ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Matching your cushion to current speed and surface grip ensures you can always stop short of trouble.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Which time-based method replaced the old one-car-length-per-ten-miles-per-hour formula in Alabama's manual?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Time-based counting scales automatically with highway speed and beats guessing invisible car lengths on asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: How do you apply Alabama's two-second rule using a fixed roadside landmark?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Reaching the sign or shadow before finishing one-thousand-two warns you to ease back right away.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: Under what weather, road, or vehicle-length conditions should you stretch your following count to four or five seconds?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Wet pavement and heavy trailers demand double-plus stopping room beyond dry passenger-car baselines.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How does Alabama's following-distance count shift from ideal passenger-car driving to bad conditions or long rigs?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Pairing two seconds for clear dry sedans with four-to-five for rain or trailers nails Alabama's gap questions.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: How should your right foot respond immediately whenever brake lights glow or the gap ahead shrinks?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Covering the pedal early shaves precious reaction distance if traffic ahead suddenly slams to zero.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What does stopping distance help determine, and which human factor governs actual stopping distance first?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Before brakes ever squeeze a rotor, your brain and foot burn distance recognizing danger and moving pedals.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How does rough dry concrete compare in stopping grip against slippery brick or smooth asphalt?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Surface texture changes friction dramatically, stretching stops on polished asphalt or wet historic brick streets.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: Which three tire characteristics govern stopping traction, and where do you verify proper tire size?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Matching tire type and deep tread with manufacturer sizing keeps full rubber contact planted under hard stops.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What stopping trade-off separates wide tires from small narrow tires across dry versus wet roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Wide tread floats sooner on standing puddles, whereas narrow rubber slices water yet gives up dry stopping bite.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Beyond tires, which suspension and brake factors affect stopping—and what happens if one wheel locks early?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: A single out-of-balance brake locking before the other three yanks the car sideways into a dangerous spin.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: Which wind condition surprises many drivers by stretching a sudden high-speed highway stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Gale-force wind pushing your trunk adds forward load right when brakes are fighting highway momentum.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: On Alabama's stopping chart, what thinking, braking, and total footage apply at twenty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Even at neighborhood twenty-five, your car rolls over sixty-one feet before coming to rest.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour on Alabama's chart, how many feet go to reacting, braking, and total stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Two hundred twenty-eight feet exceeds three-quarters of a football field on two-lane country highways.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: At sixty-five miles per hour on Alabama's chart, what thinking, braking, and total distances are needed?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Pushing past three hundred five feet matches an entire goal-line-to-goal-line football field.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What four immediate obligations apply right after you are involved in a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Setting out flares, flags, or warning markers right away keeps oncoming cars from piling into the wreck.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Under what sole life-or-death threat may you move an injured crash victim—and how should they rest?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Twisting a hidden neck or spinal fracture causes permanent paralysis unless fire forces an emergency drag.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: Along with comfort and shock care, what caution does Alabama's manual give untrained helpers?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Well-meaning amateurs can worsen trauma by doing too much, which is why Red Cross training is urged.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: Which three details must you state—and which credential must you display—to others involved in any crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Every collision requires stopping and sharing full identity and vehicle registration before leaving.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Whose names and addresses—plus scene notes—should you write down for your own protection at a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Independent bystander contact info disappears within minutes once traffic clears around the scene.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: What insurance details must you share if another involved party asks—and what if you lack them on-scene?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Keeping your insurance card in the glovebox saves having to track down the other driver afterward.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: What three options satisfy Alabama law if you bump into an unattended parked vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Leaving a clear name-and-address note—or finding the owner or police—prevents a hit-and-run charge.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: What must you do if a driving mishap damages a mailbox, fence, sign, or other non-vehicle property?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Driving off quietly after knocking down someone's fence or mailbox violates crash-reporting duties.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: How fast must an injury or fatal crash be reported—and how does city versus state-highway jurisdiction split?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Dialing local police inside town limits or State Troopers on state highways dispatches the right unit fast.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: After injury, death, or five hundred dollars damage, when and within how many days is Safety Responsibility form thirty-one required?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Notice the huge relief—when both drivers carry valid insurance, neither party needs to file that thirty-day form.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Which state unit receives Safety Responsibility thirty-one forms, and what two delivery methods work?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Submitting online through Alabama Law Enforcement Agency's license portal or mailing directly meets the thirty-day clock.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How does immediate police notification for injury crashes contrast with the thirty-day written crash form?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Keeping immediate emergency reporting separate from thirty-day uninsured paperwork avoids mixing up deadlines.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: What four scene facts should a witness give dispatchers when calling in a crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Pinpointing location and lane blockages tells dispatchers how many ambulances, tow trucks, and cruisers to send.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: What shape, colors, and markings identify the advance railroad warning—and how many feet ahead does it stand?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Memorize seven hundred fifty feet—Alabama's specific advance railroad distance is a top permit-exam favorite.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: What three painted road markings work together ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: White stop bars keep your front bumper safely clear of overhanging locomotives while yellow stripes ban passing.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: What is mandatory the instant red railroad crossing lights start flashing?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Treating flashing red crossing lamps like a yield sign gambles your life against an unstoppable locomotive.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: When red lights flash and crossing gates drop, what two conditions must both finish before you roll?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Starting forward the second gates twitch—while red lamps still flash for a second train—causes deadly strikes.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: How must you handle a railroad crossing that has no active lights or gates?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Rolling down a window and quieting cabin music helps catch train horns at passive country crossings.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.question_text: What action does a white railroad crossbuck direct, and what does a numbered plaque underneath warn?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.teaching_text: Spotting a multi-track number plaque warns you that a second hidden train may follow on parallel rails.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How do the round yellow railroad marker and the white crossbuck differ in placement?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Round yellow gives early highway-speed notice while the crossbuck marks the immediate track edge.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.question_text: Which four bus and hazmat vehicle groups must stop before every railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.teaching_text: Notice Alabama specifically includes church buses alongside school buses, passenger buses, and flammable or explosive haulers.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.question_text: Within what exact range of feet from the tracks must a required railroad stop take place?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet crowds locomotive overhang while stopping past fifty blocks track sightlines.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.question_text: How fast may you approach tracks, and what is required at crossings with active electric or mechanical warnings?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.teaching_text: Outrunning your sightline onto blind tracks leaves zero stopping margin if bells suddenly ring.

sec07-card-sec07-F46.question_text: Besides stopping for gates or trains, what extra check applies whenever a crossing spans multiple tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F46.teaching_text: Two trains frequently pass in opposite directions—never roll across until every set of rails is open.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How do railroad stopping rules split between buses or hazmat trucks and ordinary passenger cars?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Expect buses and tankers ahead of you to stop on green traffic even when crossing lamps are dark.

sec07-card-sec07-F47.question_text: Why must you never shift gears while crossing railroad rails—and how do manual drivers prepare?
sec07-card-sec07-F47.teaching_text: Missing a shift or stalling a clutch directly across steel rails traps your car in a locomotive's path.

sec07-card-sec07-F48.question_text: When can a train appear, and what rule applies in bumper-to-bumper traffic at a crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F48.teaching_text: Freight trains run unscheduled twenty-four hours—never pull onto rails until full car-length space opens beyond.

sec07-card-sec07-F49.question_text: Right after a caboose or last railcar clears the crossing, what hidden ambush must you wait to rule out?
sec07-card-sec07-F49.teaching_text: A departing freight train blocks your view and sound of a fast train approaching on the adjacent track.

sec07-card-sec07-F50.question_text: May you ever weave around lowered crossing gates or try to beat an oncoming train?
sec07-card-sec07-F50.teaching_text: Large locomotives look deceptively slow—drivers who race trains or dodge gates misjudge closing speed fatally.

sec07-card-sec07-F51.question_text: How should you adjust when following a bus or hazmat tanker toward railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F51.teaching_text: Leaving extra room behind buses and placarded tankers prevents rear-ending them when they stop trackside.

sec07-card-sec07-F53.question_text: How do yearly railroad-crossing deaths compare with aviation crashes, and what share occur at active-warning crossings?
sec07-card-sec07-F53.teaching_text: Nearly fifty percent happening where lights or gates work proves impatient driver choices—not missing warnings—cause wrecks.

sec07-card-sec07-F54.question_text: Is walking or playing on railroad tracks, trestles, or rail yards legal—and where may you cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F54.teaching_text: Modern trains roll surprisingly quietly along welded steel until too close for trespassers on trestles to escape.

sec07-card-sec07-F55.question_text: What two immediate steps come in order if your car stalls directly on railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F55.teaching_text: Human lives come before sheet metal—get every rider far clear of the rails first, then call authorities.

sec07-card-sec07-F56.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, how far—in miles and football fields—does a freight train need to stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F56.teaching_text: Even if the engineer slams emergency brakes the instant they see you, physics carries the train past a mile.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Which four groups of people using the roadway are bound by Alabama traffic laws?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Predictable traffic depends on cars, motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians following one shared playbook at every crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Why does the manual advise every driver to review the handbook again every few years?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Relying on decade-old habits invites tickets and crashes after state lawmakers revise move-over, phone, or right-of-way rules.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What is the primary crash danger of high speed according to the manual?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Impact energy climbs sharply with velocity, turning a survivable fender bump into a deadly wreck.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What four live conditions limit your legal pace under Alabama's basic speed law?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Driving the posted number during pouring rain or heavy fog still breaks the law when conditions demand slower speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What legal weight does exceeding a speed limit carry, and how strict is every municipal limit?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Crossing any town or city limit crosses an absolute ceiling and gives officers immediate grounds for unlawful-speed enforcement.
sec10-card-sec10-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Over limit risks arrest, city maximum

visual_sync.text_span: Over limit risks arrest, city maximum

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: When do Alabama's unposted statutory speed limits govern a stretch of road?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Missing a speed sign never means unlimited speed because statewide defaults fill in wherever regulatory zones are unposted.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, what are Alabama's statutory limits for urban districts, unpaved roads, and county paved roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Permit questions love scrambling these three local numbers, so step up by five then ten across town, gravel, and county asphalt.
sec10-card-sec10-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty urban, thirty-five dirt, forty-five county

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty urban, thirty-five dirt, forty-five county

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What default highway limit applies elsewhere in Alabama, and what two higher speeds apply where posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Treat fifty-five as your open-road ceiling unless signs explicitly raise the corridor to sixty-five or interstate seventy.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What two rules forbid creeping too slowly in normal conditions or where a minimum speed is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Crawling far below normal traffic triggers sudden lane swerves and rear-end collisions nearly as fast as speeding.
sec10-card-sec10-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Match posted minimums, never block flow

visual_sync.text_span: Match posted minimums, never block flow

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Near which crossings, roadside warnings, and sightline blockers must you drop your speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Blind hilltops, tight bends, rail tracks, and road flares all hide stopped hazards until your braking margin shrinks.
sec10-card-sec10-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Ease off near crossings, flares, crests

visual_sync.text_span: Ease off near crossings, flares, crests

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: In what three-step order do you pick your exact stopping point at a STOP sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Rolling past the white line or blocking a walkway pushes your bumper into pedestrians before you even check cross traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: When might obeying a STOP sign require stopping a second time before pulling out?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Hedges or parked trucks often hide oncoming cars at the legal stop line, forcing a cautious creep and second halt.
sec10-card-sec10-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Stop twice when view stays blocked

visual_sync.text_span: Stop twice when view stays blocked

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Where must you come to a full stop when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or building?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Stopping before the walkway keeps joggers, strollers, and kids safe before your hood noses toward street lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What must you do when a school patrol member extends a patrol flag in the STOP position?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Student crossing guards step out right before children enter the lane, making that held-out flag a binding stop command.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: What is the standard rule at a steady red light, and when may you turn right on red?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Skipping the complete stop before turning right on red is a top intersection ticket and crosswalk crash trigger.
sec10-card-sec10-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Stop first, right from proper lane

visual_sync.text_span: Stop first, right from proper lane

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Under what exact street layout may you turn left on red after coming to a full stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Only a one-way-to-one-way corner avoids crossing opposing lanes, making any two-way left on red illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Whom must every turn on red yield to, and what sign cancels the privilege altogether?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Crosswalk walkers and green-light cross traffic own the intersection, and posted turn bans override red-turn permissions.
sec10-card-sec10-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Yield to all, obey prohibition signs

visual_sync.text_span: Yield to all, obey prohibition signs

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: How must drivers treat an intersection when the traffic signal goes completely dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Blowing through a powerless signal causes T-bone wrecks when cross-street drivers assume everybody is stopping in turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Which roadside sign carries the exact same legal meaning as a flashing red signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Come to a complete halt and yield until clear rather than pausing once and assuming cross traffic also flashes red.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Which rail crossings, bridges, and human traffic directors also require an immediate stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Human commands, opening bridge spans, and active rail warnings override ordinary green lights or open pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches from ahead or behind with siren and lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Clearing the center lanes from both directions carves an open corridor when seconds decide survival.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: How long must oncoming and following drivers stay stopped for a school or church bus with red lights and stop arm?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Pulling out while red lights still blink risks hitting a late child darting across the lane.
sec10-card-sec10-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Hold until arm folds, lights off

visual_sync.text_span: Hold until arm folds, lights off

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: Does the school-bus stop rule still bind oncoming traffic on an undivided four-to-six-lane highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Extra painted lanes without a physical median never block kids from crossing, so every lane in both directions halts.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: In what two highway or loading-zone setups may oncoming traffic keep moving past a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Only a physical barrier on four-plus lanes or a controlled loading bay where walkers cannot cross removes oncoming stop duty.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What message do flashing amber lights atop a school bus send to nearby drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Easing off the gas during amber flashers keeps you from slamming brakes or running the red stop arm moments later.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: How far ahead of a stop do amber school-bus lights start flashing on rural roads versus city streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Higher rural highway speeds need triple the advance warning footage compared with slower municipal streets.
sec10-card-sec10-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Three hundred rural, one hundred city

visual_sync.text_span: Three hundred rural, one hundred city

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: When red bus lights flash and the stop arm swings out, how far away must drivers stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Stopping twenty feet back preserves a clear sight zone around both bumpers where small children step out.
sec10-card-sec10-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Stop at least twenty feet away

visual_sync.text_span: Stop at least twenty feet away

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does your legal duty change when school-bus lights shift from flashing amber to red with the arm out?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Treating amber like a race to pass traps you right beside the bus as red lights lock in.
sec10-card-sec10-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Amber prepare, red stop twenty feet

visual_sync.text_span: Amber prepare, red stop twenty feet

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What crash pattern stems from breaking right-of-way laws, and what two principles anchor those rules?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Insisting on going first turns routine intersections into Alabama's most preventable crash zones.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: When two cars on crossing streets reach an uncontrolled intersection together, who yields?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Giving priority to the car on your right breaks ties cleanly when no signs or lights govern the corner.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: What happens to your right-of-way if you approach an uncontrolled intersection at an unlawful speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Speeding into an unsigned corner strips away any legal priority you would otherwise claim from the right.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection, what sequence must you follow?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Stopping dead in the middle of cross streets blocks the ambulance or fire truck instead of opening its path.
sec10-card-sec10-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Clear intersection first, then pull over

visual_sync.text_span: Clear intersection first, then pull over

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: What two visual cues identify a blind pedestrian for whom you must stop at any intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Blind walkers cannot judge silent rolling cars, so stopping completely protects them across every lane.
sec10-card-sec10-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Guide dog or red-tipped white cane

visual_sync.text_span: Guide dog or red-tipped white cane

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: What must a driver entering from a private road or driveway do before joining a public street?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Through traffic on public pavement expects uninterrupted flow, not sudden pull-outs from private aprons.
sec10-card-sec10-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Stop first, yield to road traffic

visual_sync.text_span: Stop first, yield to road traffic

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: What two actions are required when approaching a YIELD sign facing your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Treating a yield triangle like a free merge causes collisions whenever walkers or cross cars occupy the gap.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: When turning left across oncoming lanes, which approaching vehicles get the right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed during a left turn creates severe front-quarter impacts across open lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: Even when entering on a green arrow, whom must a turning driver still yield to?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Pedestrians finishing a crossing or vehicles lawfully clearing the box never become fair targets just because your arrow lit.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: Which two crash types from careless passing cause heavy fatalities on two-lane highways?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Entering opposing highway speed with poor timing leaves nowhere to escape a combined-velocity impact.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: Even outside marked no-passing zones, which lighting and surface conditions demand extreme passing caution?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Broken centerline paint guarantees sight geometry in dry daylight, not traction on ice or visibility in fog.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: On a two-way, two-lane road, may you exceed the speed limit briefly to finish passing on the left?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: If overtaking a car requires breaking the posted speed limit, that car is already moving fast enough to follow.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: What checks and driver alerts belong right before pulling out to pass ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: Checking mirrors prevents pulling into a car already overtaking you while a quick horn or beam flick warns ahead.
sec10-card-sec10-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Scan ahead behind, tap or flick

visual_sync.text_span: Scan ahead behind, tap or flick

sec10-card-sec10-F41.question_text: Which signals frame a pass, and what mirror sight tells you it is safe to pull back right?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.teaching_text: Cutting back before both headlights fill your center mirror clips the overtaken car's front fender.
sec10-card-sec10-F41.must_match_memory_hook: Whole front bumper in inside mirror

visual_sync.text_span: Whole front bumper in inside mirror

sec10-card-sec10-F42.question_text: What two rules apply to you while another driver is overtaking and passing your vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.teaching_text: Speeding up beside an overtaking car traps that driver in oncoming traffic and invites a multi-car wreck.

sec10-card-sec10-F43.question_text: On which two roadway layouts does Alabama allow passing another vehicle on the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F43.teaching_text: Marked same-direction lanes give room to pass right safely without dropping tires off the paved roadway.

sec10-card-sec10-F44.question_text: When, if ever, may a driver leave the pavement onto the shoulder to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F44.teaching_text: Soft gravel, parked breakdowns, and right-turning cars turn illegal shoulder passes into high-speed rollovers.
sec10-card-sec10-F44.must_match_memory_hook: Never pass on shoulder except crisis

visual_sync.text_span: Never pass on shoulder except crisis

sec10-card-sec10-F45.question_text: Why must you never trust a front car's turn signal alone as permission to pass on the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F45.teaching_text: Drivers leave left blinkers flashing by mistake then swing right unexpectedly, and several states outlaw right passes.
sec10-card-sec10-F45.must_match_memory_hook: Blinker never guarantees safe right pass

visual_sync.text_span: Blinker never guarantees safe right pass

sec10-card-sec10-F46.question_text: How many clear feet of sight distance are required to cross the centerline and pass on a hill or curve?
sec10-card-sec10-F46.teaching_text: Closing speeds double head-on, eating up anything shorter than five hundred feet before you can tuck back in.

sec10-card-sec10-F47.question_text: At which four locations or yellow-line markings is crossing the centerline to pass outlawed?
sec10-card-sec10-F47.teaching_text: Left-turning cross traffic and solid yellow paint mark spots where overtaking steals the sole escape path.

sec10-card-sec10-F48.question_text: Around which roadside spots and lighting conditions must you scan hardest for pedestrians?
sec10-card-sec10-F48.teaching_text: Kids and commuters step from behind parked bumpers, mailboxes, and church or bus stops with almost zero warning.

sec10-card-sec10-F49.question_text: What four duties do drivers owe school children, blind pedestrians, crosswalks, and school buses?
sec10-card-sec10-F49.teaching_text: Blocking a painted crosswalk while waiting at a light forces walkers out into live moving traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F50.question_text: Who must yield when a pedestrian crosses the roadway outside a crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F50.teaching_text: Stepping across mid-block pavement leaves drivers unwarned, though alert motorists still brake to prevent harm.

sec10-card-sec10-F51.question_text: When walking along a road without sidewalks, how should pedestrians position themselves and dress at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F51.teaching_text: Facing oncoming headlights in single file with reflective gear lets walkers spot drifting cars and stay visible.
sec10-card-sec10-F51.must_match_memory_hook: Far left single file, bright gear

visual_sync.text_span: Far left single file, bright gear

sec10-card-sec10-F52.question_text: How far back must ordinary drivers stay behind an emergency vehicle on a run?
sec10-card-sec10-F52.teaching_text: Tailgating a responding fire truck or ambulance crowds rescue crews if they brake hard or turn suddenly.

sec10-card-sec10-F53.question_text: When is driving across an unprotected fire hose stretched over the street allowed?
sec10-card-sec10-F53.teaching_text: Crushing a pressurized supply line cuts water pressure instantly for crews fighting an active blaze inside.

sec10-card-sec10-F54.question_text: What check comes before entering to back up, and where must you look instead of trusting mirrors?
sec10-card-sec10-F54.teaching_text: Walking the perimeter spots low hazards first, and turning over your right shoulder beats tiny mirror angles.

sec10-card-sec10-F55.question_text: Who is the sole exception to the ban on backing up along freeways and expressways?
sec10-card-sec10-F55.teaching_text: Backing up against fast freeway traffic leaves closing motorists zero space to avoid catastrophic rear-end pileups.

sec10-card-sec10-F56.question_text: Into which lane must you steer when backing out of a driveway onto a street?
sec10-card-sec10-F56.teaching_text: Swinging backward across multiple lanes exposes your broadside to both directions of street traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F78.question_text: When is backing on a public street advisable, and what rule covers backing out of angle parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F78.teaching_text: Reversing along live travel lanes surprises following traffic, and angle spaces hide oncoming cars behind taller SUVs.

sec10-card-sec10-F57.question_text: Under what condition is driving along the highway shoulder lawful in Alabama?
sec10-card-sec10-F57.teaching_text: Keeping shoulders clear gives disabled cars and emergency responders a refuge away from live lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F58.question_text: What does Alabama law say about signs, posters, or materials placed on vehicle windows?
sec10-card-sec10-F58.teaching_text: Stickers, decals, or hanging clutter carve artificial blind spots big enough to hide cyclists and cross traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F59.question_text: What checks come before changing lanes, and does flicking your turn signal grant right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F59.teaching_text: A blinker announces intention without clearing space, so skipping your shoulder glance causes sideswipes.

sec10-card-sec10-F60.question_text: How do you position your left arm for stop or slow, left turn, and right turn hand signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F60.teaching_text: Crisp left-arm positions tell trailing drivers your next move whenever bright sun or bulb failure hides brake lights.
sec10-card-sec10-F60.must_match_memory_hook: Down slow, straight left, up right

visual_sync.text_span: Down slow, straight left, up right

sec10-card-sec10-F79.question_text: Who suffers injury most often when drivers make improper turns at intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F79.teaching_text: Cutting corners or rushing gaps pulls drivers' eyes toward cars while unprotected pedestrians step into the crosswalk.

sec10-card-sec10-F61.question_text: When do cargo or front-seat passengers make operating a vehicle unlawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F61.teaching_text: Packing four people up front or stacking tall boxes jams your elbows and blocks mirrors when swerving.

sec10-card-sec10-F62.question_text: What is the maximum combined or end overhang a load may extend past the front and rear?
sec10-card-sec10-F62.teaching_text: Long overhanging lumber swings wide in turns and impales windshields if following drivers misjudge bumper depth.

sec10-card-sec10-F63.question_text: Once a rear load projects four feet or more, what daytime and nighttime warnings are required?
sec10-card-sec10-F63.teaching_text: Unmarked poles jutting past the bumper blend into asphalt until trailing drivers close within braking range.
sec10-card-sec10-F63.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve-inch red flag, red tail lamp

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve-inch red flag, red tail lamp

sec10-card-sec10-F64.question_text: What four actions should you take right away when police lights signal you to pull over?
sec10-card-sec10-F64.teaching_text: Jumping out of your car on the shoulder startles approaching officers and exposes you to passing lane traffic.
sec10-card-sec10-F64.must_match_memory_hook: Signal off, kill engine, stay inside

visual_sync.text_span: Signal off, kill engine, stay inside

sec10-card-sec10-F65.question_text: Where should hands, devices, and cabin lights be for you and passengers during a police stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F65.teaching_text: Illuminating the cabin after dark with visible hands removes uncertainty as an officer walks up beside traffic.
sec10-card-sec10-F65.must_match_memory_hook: Hands visible, devices down, dome on

visual_sync.text_span: Hands visible, devices down, dome on

sec10-card-sec10-F66.question_text: What must you disclose at first contact with an officer, and when should you reach for documents?
sec10-card-sec10-F66.teaching_text: Digging into a console or glovebox before speaking looks dangerous from outside the window.
sec10-card-sec10-F66.must_match_memory_hook: Disclose weapons first, wait before reaching

visual_sync.text_span: Disclose weapons first, wait before reaching

sec10-card-sec10-F80.question_text: What should you do before stretching for a license, registration, or insurance card stored out of reach?
sec10-card-sec10-F80.teaching_text: Explaining where your wallet or registration sits keeps sudden movements across the cabin completely transparent.

sec10-card-sec10-F67.question_text: What identification applies when an officer not wearing a uniform conducts a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F67.teaching_text: Asking politely to verify credentials confirms lawful authority whenever a stop involves an unmarked unit.

sec10-card-sec10-F68.question_text: What does signing a traffic ticket mean legally, and where should you dispute it?
sec10-card-sec10-F68.teaching_text: Signing merely acknowledges receipt, whereas refusing the clipboard on the roadside can turn a ticket into arrest.
sec10-card-sec10-F68.must_match_memory_hook: Signature promises appearance, contest in court

visual_sync.text_span: Signature promises appearance, contest in court

sec10-card-sec10-F69.question_text: If you believe an officer acted improperly during a stop, what details should you note and where do they go?
sec10-card-sec10-F69.teaching_text: Writing down exact timestamps and location right afterward preserves clear facts for the department review.
sec10-card-sec10-F69.must_match_memory_hook: Log time, place, report to agency

visual_sync.text_span: Log time, place, report to agency

sec10-card-sec10-F70.question_text: Which three documents must a driver have ready to present during a traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F70.teaching_text: Keeping all three current and accessible prevents extra citations during an otherwise quick roadside stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F71.question_text: Which two vehicle actions are barred without coverage under Alabama's Mandatory Liability Insurance Law?
sec10-card-sec10-F71.teaching_text: Liability coverage protects crash victims financially before tags are issued or tires ever hit public asphalt.

sec10-card-sec10-F72.question_text: What three dollar minimums make up Alabama's required liability insurance coverage?
sec10-card-sec10-F72.teaching_text: Memorizing one person, two-plus people, and property damage in order nails every insurance minimum prompt.

sec10-card-sec10-F73.question_text: What maximum fines and license suspension can follow first and repeat liability insurance violations?
sec10-card-sec10-F73.teaching_text: Driving uninsured can cost double on a repeat ticket and park your registration or license for half a year.
sec10-card-sec10-F73.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred first, thousand repeat, suspension

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred first, thousand repeat, suspension

sec10-card-sec10-F74.question_text: How many inches at the top of a vehicle's windshield may carry window tint in Alabama?
sec10-card-sec10-F74.teaching_text: Tinting lower across the front glass darkens nighttime sightlines where unlit walkers and animals appear.

sec10-card-sec10-F75.question_text: How much light must pass through car side and rear tint, and which windows follow that rule on SUVs or trucks?
sec10-card-sec10-F75.teaching_text: Keeping front side glass bright enough preserves eye contact with walkers and clear mirror checks at night.
sec10-card-sec10-F75.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty-two percent cars, front SUV sides

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty-two percent cars, front SUV sides

sec10-card-sec10-F81.question_text: On SUVs, pickup trucks, vans, and RVs, which windows may carry darker tint than thirty-two percent?
sec10-card-sec10-F81.teaching_text: Privacy glass behind the front row shields cargo and rear seats without dimming the driver's front side sightlines.

sec10-card-sec10-F76.question_text: On a road with four or more lanes, what must you do for a stopped emergency unit or amber-lit wrecker?
sec10-card-sec10-F76.teaching_text: Putting a full empty lane between highway traffic and roadside responders saves officers and tow crews from sideswipes.

sec10-card-sec10-F77.question_text: How much must you slow when blocked from moving over, and what speed rules apply on two-lane roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F77.teaching_text: Dropping at least fifteen under, or down to ten in low-speed zones, shrinks wind blast and stopping distance.
sec10-card-sec10-F77.must_match_memory_hook: Fifteen under, or ten in twenty

visual_sync.text_span: Fifteen under, or ten in twenty

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Under Alabama's move-over law, when is slowing down allowed instead of changing lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Slowing in the adjacent lane on an open four-lane road still violates the law when you could safely merge away.
sec10-card-sec10-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Move over first, slow when blocked

visual_sync.text_span: Move over first, slow when blocked

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: At what birthday do Alabama's graduated driver license rules stop applying completely?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Turning eighteen immediately lifts teen passenger, curfew, and graduated restriction rules regardless of prior licensing months.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: How long must a seventeen-year-old hold a valid license to step outside the graduated rules?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Merely turning seventeen is not enough until you also log at least six months holding a valid license.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Which two family or household statuses exempt a driver aged sixteen or older from graduated rules?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Running an independent household or marriage carries work and family driving duties that lift teen restrictions.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Do Alabama's graduated license rules cover a teen legally relieved of minority status?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Court emancipation grants adult legal standing, placing that young driver outside teen graduated restrictions.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How does qualifying for a graduated-license exemption at seventeen differ from turning eighteen?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Permit questions test whether you spot that seventeen still requires six licensed months whereas eighteen clears outright.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Which two groups of young licensed drivers remain under Alabama's graduated license restrictions?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Every sixteen-year-old licensee and any seventeen-year-old shy of six licensed months follows teen curfews and caps.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What age, learner-hold time, and compliance record must someone under eighteen meet before applying for an unrestricted license?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: A single restriction slip resets your clean-record requirement before you can upgrade at seventeen.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: Which four categories of adults sitting right beside a fifteen-year-old learner satisfy the supervision rule?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Putting a twenty-year-old friend or backseat adult in the car still violates the front-seat supervision law.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Does a licensed or certified driving instructor in the front passenger seat qualify to supervise a fifteen-year-old learner?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Driver-education lessons count legally even when neither parent nor an adult over twenty-one is along.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: For what two milestones does a sixteen-year-old need permission from a parent or legal guardian?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Passing the road check alone is not enough at sixteen without parent approval for both issuance and solo trips.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How does front-seat supervision for a fifteen-year-old learner contrast with passenger rules for a restricted sixteen-year-old?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Learners always need an approved front-seat coach, whereas restricted teens drive solo with at most one nonfamily peer.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Without a supervising adult along, how many nonfamily passengers may a restricted teen carry?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Cutting the old four-friend cap down to one removes loud peer distraction that spikes teen crash rates.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: During which overnight hours is a restricted teen barred from driving without a parent, guardian, or exception?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Late-night fatigue and darkness multiply teen crash risk during the quietest hours before dawn.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: Which accompanying adults, scheduled trips, or emergencies allow a restricted teen to drive between midnight and six in the morning?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Legitimate jobs, worship or school events, consented adult riders, and true emergencies stay legal overnight.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Which three routine destinations let a restricted driver commute solo during overnight curfew hours?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Early shifts, away-game buses, and youth worship events stay covered only on direct trips there and home.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What communication device rule binds restricted drivers, and what two consequences can follow breaking it?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Picking up a phone on a restricted license risks stretching your teen restrictions longer or losing your card.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: When riding overnight with a licensed adult twenty-one or older who is not your parent, what extra condition applies?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Having an older cousin or friend twenty-one-plus beside you after midnight only counts when your parent approved.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: How does Alabama classify breaking a graduated-license condition regarding criminal records and court costs?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Breaking a teen restriction triggers licensing consequences rather than a criminal record or court fee bill.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: When may an officer issue a citation for breaking a graduated driver license restriction?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Secondary enforcement means another traffic offense must trigger both the stop and a separate ticket first.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: How many driver-record points are added for violating a graduated license restriction?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: While underlying speeding tickets still carry points, the teen restriction violation itself adds zero points.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: Can an officer write a standalone graduated-license ticket without citing another offense?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Remembering that a restriction ticket never stands alone nails secondary-enforcement distractors every time.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: How long does breaking any graduated restriction extend a teen's restricted period?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Sneaking an extra passenger or breaking curfew pushes unrestricted freedom back half a year.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: Even with zero points and no criminal fine, what penalty still hits after a restriction violation?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Do not mistake zero points for a free pass when six extra months of teen limits still attach.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Which moving-violation count or single-offense point value triggers an automatic sixty-day restricted suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: One serious four-point ticket or two smaller moving convictions parks a restricted teen's license for two months.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: Which six dangerous-driving or hit-and-run convictions also trigger the automatic sixty-day suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: High-risk offenses like racing, eluding police, wrong-way driving, or illegal passing bring immediate sixty-day loss.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: How does the penalty for breaking a teen restriction differ from a second moving or four-point conviction?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Keeping six-month restriction extensions separate from sixty-day moving suspensions prevents mixing Alabama's two teen penalties.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: According to crash records, what share of highway wrecks trace back to the driver and which human failures cause them?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Blaming weather or roads misses the real risk when driver inattention, bad attitude, or faulty judgment starts crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Once you master basic car handling, what else must you keep learning to become a truly good driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Passing a road test proves basic steering, while lifelong safety depends on reading your own mental and physical state.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: How do personal worries, family quarrels, illness at home, fear, or overconfidence affect your crash risk?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Mental replay of money stress or arguments steals the split-second awareness needed to spot braking traffic ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What should someone do before driving right after a heated argument or while angry or grieving?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Turning a two-ton vehicle into an outlet for anger or grief fuels aggressive speed and blind tunnel vision.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What does the manual recommend whenever you feel ill, worried, nervous, frightened, angry, or depressed?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Recognizing when illness or heavy emotion blunts your reflexes and handing keys over prevents avoidable wrecks.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What term does the manual use for sharing the roadway fairly and seeing traffic from every user's viewpoint?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Thinking ahead from walkers', cyclists', and merging drivers' perspectives defuses road conflicts before horns ever blow.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What personal trait do sound driving attitudes and actions reflect, and which age groups need it?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Calendar birthdays never guarantee calm judgment on the highway, making emotional self-control vital for teen and veteran drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Because concentration is vital to safe driving, which four casual habits have zero place behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Glancing at storefront displays or zoning out for three seconds covers a football field blind at highway speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Why does the manual call driving a full-time job, and what breaks down first when focus slips?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Half-hearted attention dulls visual scanning first, turning routine slowdowns ahead into sudden preventable rear-end crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Even when you legally use a cell phone in the car, what remains your number-one duty?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: No incoming call or notification ever outranks steering, braking, and scanning live traffic around your bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What two checks or habits help before placing a phone call from the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Pecking out ten-digit numbers steals eye time right when merging or dense traffic demands full visual focus.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Which practical steps make placing or taking phone calls safer in a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Handing phone duty to a passenger or waiting for a parked stop keeps both hands and eyes free.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Which conversation types and road conditions call for avoiding phone talk or pulling off the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Heavy rain, dense traffic, and heated phone arguments overload working memory and spike reaction times dangerously.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Which wireless messaging actions are outlawed while operating a motor vehicle in Alabama?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Test questions check all three verbs because reading an incoming text or email breaks the law just like typing.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What dollar fines does the manual list for first, second, and third or later texting convictions?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Each repeat messaging ticket steps the fine up by twenty-five dollars through your third offense and beyond.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Besides the cash fine, how many violation points does a texting conviction add to your driving record?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: License points stack toward suspension and raise teen insurance rates long after a small fine is paid.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Across repeat Alabama texting tickets, how does the fine progression differ from the driver-record point penalty?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Exam options love claiming points double on repeat tickets, whereas points hold steady at two each time.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What should you do the moment drowsiness hits behind the wheel instead of trying to push through?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Microsleeps strike without warning once eyelids feel heavy, turning highway lanes into high-speed drift zones.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: How does the manual separate a short fix for mild tiredness from what a truly sleepy driver must do?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Caffeine and leg stretches buy brief alertness when mildly fatigued, yet only actual sleep fixes real sleepiness.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Why does the manual warn interstate drivers away from taking stay-awake drugs?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Stimulant pills mask exhaustion briefly before jittery side effects and sudden crashes make highway driving worse.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: By distance or by clock time, how often should you stop to walk and stretch on long trips?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Stepping out to walk and loosen stiff muscles resets circulation before highway fatigue creeps up unnoticed.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: What simple rest habit does the manual suggest before setting out on a long drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Starting a multi-hour drive fully rested gives you a crucial alertness buffer against monotonous afternoon miles.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What is highway hypnosis, and which steady road sounds help trigger it on expressways?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Unchanging wind rush, tire drone, and engine hum numb your brain into staring blankly ahead without processing hazards.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Which active eye habits keep highway hypnosis from setting in on open roads?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Shifting gaze across mirrors, distant horizon, shoulders, and road signs forces active visual processing instead of staring.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Putting the fatigue rules together, when does coffee help, when must you nap, and when do stay-awake drugs fit?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Exam traps offer stimulant pills as a backup option, when real sleep off the road is irreplaceable.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Which physical factors or substances can degrade driving ability enough to cause or contribute to crashes?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Safe driving relies on sharp sight, steady muscles, and clear nerves that sickness or chemicals quickly erode.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does research show most drivers are already impaired?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Waiting for the unlawful limit ignores proven reaction loss that starts well below eight hundredths.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration is every single driver definitely impaired without exception?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Nobody builds immunity to blood alcohol, because eight hundredths degrades every human brain's tracking and braking.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Roughly what share of fatal traffic crashes each year involve drivers who have been drinking?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Alcohol shows up in about half of deadly wrecks because slowed reflexes combine with high-speed risk-taking.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: How does one bottle of beer compare in alcohol content and driver impact to a shot of whiskey or glass of wine?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Switching from liquor shots to bottled beer changes liquid volume, never the dose of pure alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Is alcohol a stimulant or a depressant, and what does it do to vision, reflexes, and judgment?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Even if partygoers talk louder at first, alcohol chemically sedates central nervous pathways needed to steer.
